headline: Lamp not lit atop deepathoon, Supreme Court to hear contempt case
content: NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu government’s failure to comply with the Supreme Court’s order to allow the lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp atop deepathoon as a one-time arrangement may lead to contempt proceedings.On Wednesday, the Supreme Court said it would hear the contempt case despite the Madurai Collector’s apology to the court. A fresh petition has also been filed seeking directions to light the lamp atop deepathoon, the disputed stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai.Appearing for the Collector, senior advocate Gopal Sankarnarayanan told a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi that the court’s order could not be carried out and the lamp was not lit at the assigned place. He also said the Collector had filed a report.The non-compliance stood out against the backdrop of opposition to the lighting of the lamp atop the deepathoon from Sikandar Badusha Dargah Committee, state government, its Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department, the Madurai district administration, and the Temple Board of Trustees.An array of political parties TVK as well as its predecessor in office, DMK, Congress, Left parties and Muslim outfits, have been opposing the move.Collector apologises for lamp not being lit atop DeepathoonIn a twist to the controversy, the temple administration’s explanation for retaining the customary lighting venue came under question after four sthanikars (traditional temple priests) said their communication regarding lighting the lamp near Uchi Pillaiyar temple was sent last year and that they had submitted no letter regarding this year’s festival. The trustees had cited the priests’ views as one of the reasons for their decision to light the lamp at the customary spot.Senior advocate Guru Krishna Kumar, appearing for the petitioner, told the SC bench there was a “deliberate attempt” not to comply with the apex court’s directive. Kumar again told the bench in the afternoon that a devotee had filed a fresh plea seeking a directive to light the deepam atop the disputed Deepathoon with the flame from the lamp lit Tuesday. The court said it would hear this plea too.Meanwhile, a litigant made a mention before Madras HC seeking to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings over non-compliance with SC’s directive.In the status report, the Madurai collector said he had made all efforts to comply with SC’s directive, and he should not be blamed for failure to do so. “I submit that I took all the steps to comply with the order in good faith....I sincerely apologise for the lamp not being lit at the Deepathoon. The district administration made every effort to secure the authorisation of the Devasthanam and the lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon. However, the board of trustees resolved to light the lamp at the customary place,” the report said.SC had allowed the lighting of the traditional lamp at Deepathoon on Nov 24 as a one-time measure and directed only authorised persons to attend the ceremony.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Consumer forum directs independent inspection of defective BYD electric car, orders repairs and compensation while considering refund or replacement based on expert findings
content: Hyderabad: Two years after purchasing a ‘defective’ electric vehicle, a greentech firm has received some respite, with a district consumer forum directing Mody BYD and BYD India Pvt Ltd to arrange an independent joint technical inspection through an independent automobile expert.The inspection will cover the rear suspension and noise sources, steering assembly, air-conditioning, electrical and charging systems, and overall mechanical roadworthiness. The companies have been directed to rectify any defects identified, free of cost, and extend warranty coverage to all repaired or replaced components.They have also been asked to pay ₹25,000 as compensation and ₹10,000 towards costs.Akshat Greentech Private Limited, the complainant, said it purchased an electric vehicle for Rs 32.57 lakh on Nov 13, 2024, after being impressed by BYD’s advertisements and representations about its features and performance.G Mahesha, the firm’s authorised signatory, alleged that the vehicle was delivered without charging equipment, which was installed only on Nov 30 despite repeated follow-ups, depriving the firm of its use for 17 days.He further alleged that the vehicle emitted abnormal noises, particularly from the rear suspension, from the initial period of use, while the AC was non-functional. Though the defects were brought to the dealer’s notice on Nov 28 and technicians claimed to have rectified them, the problems persisted.Despite multiple repair attempts, the defects remained unresolved, prompting the firm to seek replacement on Dec 3, 2024. During a second test drive on Jan 2, 2025, Mahesha noticed continuing suspension noise and additional noise from the steering mechanism, which was communicated to the company the following day.The firm also alleged that the companies failed to provide the pre-delivery inspection report and promised benefits, including ceramic coating particulars, warranty documents, an accessories kit and free-service coupons. It approached the forum contending that the unresolved defects rendered the vehicle unsuitable for its intended use.During the hearing, the bench observed that a complete refund or replacement could not be ordered merely because a vehicle had undergone multiple repair attempts. There must be conclusive technical evidence establishing an inherent and irreparable manufacturing defect, it said.The forum directed the companies to complete the independent inspection within 30 days of the order. If rectifiable defects are identified, they must be addressed free of cost within 30 days thereafter, with a full service and repair log certified by the expert.“Upon successful rectification, the vehicle shall be delivered to the complainant alongside an expert-certified roadworthiness document and explicit extended warranty coverage for all repaired/replaced components,” the bench said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: Telangana to roll out single-window clearances for poultry farms
content: Hyderabad: Telangana will introduce a single-window system to speed up approvals for poultry farms and take steps to ensure uninterrupted supply of maize and soya bean feed during El Niño conditions, chief minister A Revanth Reddy announced on Wednesday.Speaking at Poultry India Expo 2026 at Hitex, Revanth responded to concerns raised by industry representatives over delays in approvals, availability of feed and other challenges facing the sector.He said govt was already issuing building and layout permissions through its BuildNow single-window portal and would soon extend a similar facility for poultry farms to secure approvals from various departments, including those in gram panchayat limits.On concerns over a possible shortage of maize and soya bean during El Niño, Revanth directed animal husbandry minister Vakiti Srihari to hold a review with officials and poultry industry representatives and, within 48 hours, assess buffer stocks available with govt and the price at which they could be supplied to the sector.“The govt has stocks of maize and soya beans and it should be ensured that they are supplied directly to the poultry sector without the involvement of the middlemen or traders in between,” Revanth said.Responding to the industry’s request for land in Bharat Future City to develop a convention centre, Revanth said a positive decision would be taken during the three-day Invest Telangana Global Summit beginning Dec 7 at Bharat Future City.Assuring the industry of policy continuity, the CM said good existing policies would be retained and improved to facilitate investment.“The state govt will extend all the support needed for the poultry industry to develop. The poultry sector will be recognised as a priority area and formulate policies aimed at providing long-term solutions. We are moving forward with a goal of transforming Telangana into a $3 trillion economy by 2047, and the poultry industry should also play its role in achieving this endeavour,” he said.Revanth said the industry produces 5.3 crore eggs a day in Telangana and plays an important role in providing nutritious food to govt school students, who receive three eggs a week.He also urged the industry to generate more employment for agricultural labourers and farmers, saying the poultry sector strengthens farmers’ economic prospects apart from producing chicken and eggs.The CM also said govt had stockpiled fine rice sufficient to meet requirements for two years amid El Niño conditions.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: Over 80k applications found ineligible for graduates’ rolls
content: Hyderabad: More than 80,000 applications have been found ineligible for enrolment in the two Telangana graduates’ constituencies, leaving 11.9 lakh electors on the draft rolls published on Wednesday.Election officials found 80,635 of the 12.6 lakh applications received ineligible while preparing fresh rolls for the Warangal–Khammam–Nalgonda and Mahbubnagar–Rangareddy–Hyderabad constituencies.Graduates whose names are missing from the draft rolls, including those who missed the Nov 6 deadline, can apply for enrolment until Dec 10. Even those who voted in the previous legislative council election have to enrol afresh.The Warangal–Khammam–Nalgonda constituency has 6.2 lakh electors on its draft roll, while Mahbubnagar–Rangareddy–Hyderabad has 5.6 lakh. Officials found 49,321 applications, or 7.3%, ineligible in the former and 31,314, or 5.2%, in the latter.Rangareddy, with 1.4 lakh electors, Medchal-Malkajgiri with 1.3 lakh and Hyderabad with 97,247 together account for 66.5% of the electorate in the Mahabubnagar–Rangareddy–Hyderabad constituency.In the Warangal–Khammam–Nalgonda constituency, Nalgonda and Khammam were the only districts to cross the one lakh mark.Khammam recorded the highest number of ineligible applications at 8,264, followed by Rangareddy with 7,623 and Nalgonda with 7,437.The highest proportion of ineligible applications was recorded in the four Siddipet mandals covered by the rolls, where 974 of 7,366 applications, or 13.2%, were found ineligible. Across the two constituencies, the rejection rate was 6.3%.The draft rolls have 7.1 lakh men, 4.7 lakh women and 11 third gender electors. Women constitute 40.2% of the overall electorate. Their share is 45.1% in Bhadradri–Kothagudem and 44.1% in Hyderabad, while Jogulamba-Gadwal has the lowest proportion at 32.3%.Fresh enrolment open till Dec 10Chief electoral officer C Sudharsan Reddy urged graduates to check whether their names figure on the rolls through the CEO Telangana website.Indian citizens ordinarily resident in the constituency and who obtained a degree from an Indian university or an equivalent qualification by Oct 31, 2023, are eligible. The qualifying date is Nov 1, 2026.Those seeking enrolment must submit Form 18 along with an attested degree or diploma certificate and proof of ordinary residence. Form 7 can be used to object to an inclusion or seek deletion of a name, while Form 8 is for corrections.Graduates can inspect the rolls and submit forms at the offices of registration officers or designated officers, or through the CEO Telangana website.Officials have to decide claims and objections and prepare supplements by Dec 25. The final rolls are scheduled to be published on Dec 30.Graduates can also apply for enrolment after publication of the final rolls until the last date for filing nominations.The Election Commission has approved 1,703 polling stations for the two constituencies: 809 for Mahabubnagar–Rangareddy–Hyderabad and 894 for Warangal–Khammam–Nalgonda. Six senior IAS officers will oversee the roll exercise.The terms of the two sitting MLCs, S Vani Devi and Teenmar Mallanna, end on March 29, 2027. headline: CMC to have twin-tower net-zero green headquarters
content: Hyderabad: The Cyberabad Municipal Corporation (CMC) has invited e-tenders for the construction of its permanent headquarters at Izzath Nagar, Serilingampally. The project, estimated to cost ₹169 crore, will be developed on 4.11 acres of land adjoining Kotha Kunta lake.The proposed headquarters will feature a state-of-the-art, twin-tower, net-zero green building complex with a total built-up area of 2,41,540 sq ft. The complex will comprise two interconnected towers, one with G+6 floors and the other with G+8 floors, designed to cater to the present and future administrative requirements of the corporation.The headquarters will provide several citizen-centric facilities, including a council hall, Prajavani hall, citizen service centres, an auditorium, an integrated command centre and dedicated office spaces for various departments and allied govt agencies.The project incorporates advanced architectural concepts and green building technologies, including renewable energy systems, energy-efficient infrastructure, water conservation measures, wastewater recycling, smart building management systems and climate-responsive design, to achieve net-zero performance.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: Trump slaps new tariffs on 14 nations; India faces additional 17%
content: Setting the stage for additional duty burden on exports, the US Trade Representative on Wednesday proposed 17% additional tariffs on Indian goods, which can rise to 25% if the bilateral trade deal is not signed.Citing the findings of its Section 301 investigation against 16 countries for alleged structural excess capacity, the Trump administration has proposed additional levies of 15-20% against 14 offending countries, with the developed nations at the lower end of the band and China, Vietnam and Singapore at the top. The move, though not surprising, creates fresh complications for exporters, with two important exports from India, pharma and mobile phones, exempted from additional tariffs.While most developing countries are in the 18% bracket, India has a one-percentage-point “comparative advantage”, provided the first tranche of the agreement which was finalised last Feb, is signed by the time the final hearings are completed and tariffs are announced. With the hearings scheduled on Jan 25, 2027, the fresh levies are likely to kick in next Feb. In India’s case, the probe flagged PLI schemes as part of the Atmanirbhar Bharat push and sector-specific acts, policies and practices in the steel, solar, health and ICT sectors.Government rejects structural excess capacity chargeThe government on Wednesday rejected charges of structural excess capacity in any sector, and said it will work with the US for early conclusion of a bilateral trade agreement. “India and the US are engaged in negotiations for a BTA. It has been India’s position that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of these negotiations,” government said, adding it was examining the USTR notice.While India and the US had announced an agreement on Feb 2, agreeing to 18% additional tariff, it had to be suspended due to the reciprocal tariffs being struck down by the US Supreme Court.The government officials have said that the agreement has largely been finalised and will be sealed once the US tariff framework is ready.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Uttariya instead of robes: West Bengal Government suggests universities to adopt Indian attire in convocations
content: Kolkata West Bengal Higher Education Department has advised all the State-aided universities to adopt Indian attire such as Uttariya and clothes made of handloom fabric instead of Western robes during convocation or any academic ceremony. “We are putting effort to follow our own Indian culture and tradition. Uttariyo is enough for such ceremonies. Why do we have to wear robes? Many institutions, including the Indian Institute of Technology [IIT], have adopted only uttariya. Hence, we made the suggestion,” West Bengal Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chattopadhyay told media persons on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). The development also came days after Mr. Chattopadhyay praised the Jalpaiguri Government Engineering College for upholding Indian traditions by replacing the conventional academic gown with a traditional uttariya. “As we strive to build a self-reliant Bharat, our education system must also reflect our civilisational values and cultural identity,” he wrote on X congratulating the students of the college. In its notice sent to all the vice chancellors of the universities, the department has now said that the UGC had not prescribed any rigid uniform design for ceremonial robes. Hence, the universities have the flexibility to incorporate traditional Indian attire, such as the uttariya, and to design distinct ceremonial attire for dignitaries and degree recipients. Monday’s (November 23) notice to the VCs said that the ceremonial attire made from Indian handloom was more suited to India’s climate. Such a preference for handloom fabrics and traditional Indian attire also supports the rural handloom industry and weavers’ livelihoods, it said. “In view of the above, you are requested to take necessary steps to consider adopting handloom fabrics and traditional attire for the academic robes worn during convocation in your esteemed university as well as affiliated colleges, wherever applicable,” the department stated in the advisory asking the universities to send to confirmation of the communication to the department.

headline: ‘Our artists bringing new perspectives to art world’: PM Modi after Venice Biennale award
content: NEW DELHI: The India Pavilion has received the Visitors’ Lion Award for Best National Participation at the prestigious 61st International Art Exhibition – La Biennale di Venezia (Biennale Arte 2026), with PM Narendra Modi hailing the honour as a “proud moment” for India’s art and cultural world.The India Pavilion returned to Biennale Arte, one of the components of La Biennale di Venezia, after seven years. Curated by Amin Jaffer, the pavilion, under the theme ‘Geographies of Distance: Remembering Home’, brought together works by five contemporary artists — Alwar Balasubramaniam, Sumakshi Singh, Ranjani Shettar, Asim Waqif, and Skarma Sonam Tashi — exploring themes of memory, migration, materiality, and the emotional resonance of ‘home’ across diverse Indian landscapes, from Ladakh to Tamil Nadu.“Our artists are bringing new perspectives to the art world, drawing inspiration from India’s rich and diverse cultural heritage,” PM Modi said on X. “May this achievement inspire more and more youth of India to move forward in the field of art and explore new dimensions of creativity.”Announcing the development, culture minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat earlier in a post on X said, “India wins the Best National Pavilion – Visitors’ Lion at the Venice Art Biennale, the Olympics of the art world. The honour... is a remarkable recognition of India’s growing cultural influence.”Announced by La Biennale di Venezia Wednesday following the conclusion of the exhibition (May 9 – Nov 22), the inaugural Visitors’ Lions were determined through ballots cast by ticket-holding visitors who toured both primary exhibition venues, Giardini and Arsenale.The Pavilion was presented by the ministry of culture in partnership with Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre and Serendipity Arts.The India Pavilion was commissioned by the National Gallery of Modern Art, with the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts serving as the executing agency.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Meta officials meet Congress over suspended accounts
content: NEW DELHI: A team of Meta officials met the Congress social media department in the wake of complaints by the opposition party and amid protests by the Indian Youth Congress, which has issued an ultimatum of a week to the company to restore the suspended accounts of its functionaries.AICC social media department chairperson Supriya Shrinate met Meta officials at the request of the company that owns Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp.Sources said Shrinate raised concerns over the growing suspension of accounts and removal of posts related to the opposition, even saying the company was interfering with the politics of the country.According to those present, Meta officials said the company was bound by India’s laws, and it had to take down posts within three hours of a government request. headline: Forus Health, Eyebetes Foundation work on AI-based diabetes screening - Mint
content: Mumbai’s Ganpati celebrations are synonymous with faith, community and public gatherings. This year, two of the city’s festival destinations became the setting for an initiative that brought an important conversation into the celebrations: preventive healthcare.Eyebetes Foundation, in collaboration with Forus Health, conducted a pilot retinal screening initiative at Siddhivinayak Temple and GSB Ganpati Mandal, exploring how retinal imaging and artificial intelligence could potentially support diabetes risk screening and generate insights associated with HbA1c levels.The initiative offered free screening activities to devotees and was designed to reach more than 15,000 people, bringing health awareness and preliminary screening closer to communities in an accessible environment.When the eye becomes a window to metabolic healthThe retina offers a distinctive view of the body’s microvascular system. Since diabetes can affect small blood vessels and cause changes in retinal structures, retinal imaging has attracted attention as a potential tool for identifying indicators associated with systemic health.At the Mumbai pilot, Forus Health explored this potential through AI-enabled retinal analysis, including its FH-POISE AI solutions. The technology uses retinal images to explore associations with diabetes risk and estimate HbA1c levels, offering a non-invasive screening pathway that does not initially require a blood sample or laboratory processing.“With FH-POISE AI solutions, we were exploring how a simple retinal image could provide insights that traditionally required a blood test. Our AI models could estimate HbA1c levels and flag diabetes risk from a single retinal image, without the need for a blood draw or laboratory processing. The retina gave us a unique, non-invasive view of the body’s microvascular health, and AI could help translate these insights into meaningful screening support,” said Srinivasan Venkatakrishnan, Chief Technology Officer and Head of Research & Development, Forus Health.The pilot demonstrated how technology can potentially bring preliminary health screening into settings beyond conventional hospitals and diagnostic centres.Taking screening where communities gatherOne of the takeaways from the initiative was the importance of accessibility. Diabetes screening often depends on an individual actively visiting a healthcare facility, undergoing testing and following up with a medical professional. Community-based initiatives can create an additional touchpoint by taking awareness and preliminary screening directly to people.Ganpati celebrations provided a significant setting for this approach. With thousands of devotees visiting the pandals, the initiative integrated health awareness into an existing community experience rather than requiring people to make a separate healthcare visit.Such models could have relevance for community health camps, workplaces, primary healthcare settings and mobile screening programmes, particularly where awareness or access to diagnostic facilities remains a challenge.Moving from screening to timely actionThe potential of AI-powered screening lies not simply in generating a digital insight, but in encouraging people to take the next step towards appropriate healthcare.An AI-generated estimate or risk indicator cannot replace conventional diagnostic testing. For individuals identified as potentially at risk, appropriate follow-up, including conventional HbA1c testing and consultation with a qualified healthcare professional, remains essential.“Diabetes was no longer only a metabolic concern; it was a major public health challenge with consequences that could affect the eyes, kidneys, heart, nerves and overall quality of life. What made AI-powered retinal screening particularly promising was its potential to make diabetes risk assessment quicker, non-invasive and more accessible, especially in communities where regular laboratory testing might not always be easy to access,” said Dr. Nishant Kumar, Consultant Ophthalmologist, Retina Surgeon and Uveitis Specialist, and Founder, Eyebetes Foundation.The collaboration highlighted the importance of developing datasets that represent Indian populations. Building Indian datasets and training AI models on relevant populations could play an important role in evaluating and refining the applicability of such technologies in the country.A broader role for AI in preventive healthcareThe Mumbai pilot reflects an evolution in healthcare, where artificial intelligence is being explored as a supporting tool for screening, risk identification and early intervention.For retinal healthcare, the possibilities extend beyond detecting eye conditions. The ability to examine retinal images for patterns associated with systemic health conditions could position the eye as an accessible entry point for preventive screening.However, responsible implementation remains central to this evolution. Clinical validation, representative datasets, appropriate referral pathways and clear communication about the limitations of AI-generated insights are critical to ensuring that technology complements rather than replaces established medical care.Bringing health awareness into everyday lifeThe collaboration between Forus Health and Eyebetes Foundation demonstrated an approach that combined technology, medical expertise and community engagement.By taking retinal screening to Siddhivinayak Temple and GSB Ganpati Mandal during one of Mumbai’s largest cultural celebrations, the initiative created an opportunity to connect preventive healthcare with everyday community life.Its significance extended beyond the screening activity itself. It opened a conversation around whether emerging technologies such as AI-powered retinal analysis could help make preliminary health screening more accessible, encourage earlier awareness and create links between communities and formal healthcare systems.The screening programme was intended for awareness and preliminary risk assessment. AI-generated health insights should not be considered a substitute for conventional HbA1c testing, clinical diagnosis or consultation with a qualified healthcare professional.Note to the Reader: This article is part of Mint's paid consumer connect initiative and is independently created by the brand. Mint assumes no editorial responsibility for the content.The information does not constitute medical/health advice. Readers are strongly advised to consult a registered medical practitioner.

headline: Consumer commission orders Amazon, seller to refund ₹68,990 with 9% interest after Hyderabad buyer receives second-hand gaming laptop instead of new one
content: Hyderabad: Ranga Reddy District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed Amazon Seller Services Pvt Ltd (Amazon India) and Clicktech Retail Pvt Ltd to refund ₹68,990 with 9% annual interest to a consumer who received a second-hand laptop instead of the brand-new gaming laptop he had ordered. The companies were also directed to pay ₹5,000 as compensation and ₹5,000 towards litigation costs.The complainant, Shaik Athar Hussain, said he ordered a brand-new gaming laptop on Amazon India on Oct 20, 2025, for ₹68,990 to gift his sister for educational purposes. The product was sold by Clicktech Retail and delivered four days later.As the delivery agent refused to allow an open-box inspection, Hussain recorded an unboxing video. On opening the package, he found an old, used laptop with scratches, worn-out keys and third-party repair stickers instead of the new gaming laptop.He immediately alerted the companies and sought a replacement or refund. Following his return request, he was assured that the laptop would be collected and a refund initiated. However, although the product was picked up on Oct 25, no refund was issued.After several email exchanges, Hussain received a communication on Nov 22 stating that an internal investigation had found no error on the companies’ part and that his refund could not be processed.Alleging financial loss, mental agony and inconvenience, he approached the consumer commission. Both companies, despite being served notices, failed to file their written versions and were set ex parte.The commission said the unboxing video, photographs and return collection receipt established that a second-hand, defective laptop had been delivered and subsequently returned.“Retaining the consumer money alongside the returned goods, coupled with an opaque, unsubstantiated refusal of a refund, amounts to deficiency of service and unfair trade practice on the part of the opposite parties,” the bench observed.Holding both companies liable, the commission directed them to refund ₹68,990 with 9% annual interest from Oct 20, 2025, until realisation, besides the compensation and litigation costs.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: Karnataka mandates menstrual health facilities in all schools, colleges
content: Bengaluru: The Department of School Education and Literacy has mandated all schools and colleges – government and otherwise – to ensure there are facilities for Menstrual Health Management (MHM) at their institutions..The directive enjoins on all institutions to ensure there are dedicated lavatories for girls, availability of free sanitary napkins, and the setting up of an MHM corner containing disposable bags, spare innerwear and uniforms..The department’s directive comes close on the heels of an order issued by a Supreme Court, which ruled on a PIL filed by activist Dr Jaya Thakur. The Supreme Court held menstrual hygiene to be a fundamental right under Article 21 of the Constitution..Subsequently, the department issued a detailed circular to all schools and colleges in both urban and rural areas obliging them to adhere to the stated guidelines laid down in accordance with the apex court’s order..Girls' education must not be hampered due to lack of sanitary napkins, gender-segregated toilets in schools: SC.Besides the instructions to secure girls’ menstrual health, the circular calls on all educational institutions to ensure the lavatories are disabled-friendly. They have also been asked to ensure availability of soap and water at all times..Students from classes six to second-year PU are to be provided biodegradable sanitary napkins conforming to the ASTM D-6954 standard free of cost. Machines that dispense sanitary napkins are to be installed inside toilets where possible. Furthermore, the napkins are to be distributed at designated places or by authorised personnel..Schools have further been asked to ensure that the sanitary napkins are responsibly disposed of, in keeping with the Solid Waste Management Rules. To that end, toilets are to have covered dustbins, which are to be cleaned regularly..The department has suggested conducting menstrual health awareness programmes to dispel myths and misconceptions surrounding menstruation and puberty..To ensure the order is enforced, nodal officers, preferably women, are to be appointed at district- and block-level. WhatsApp is to be used for co-ordinating operations, while Deputy Directors of Public Instruction too have been ordered to carry out inspections periodically. Feedback is to be collected from students, and reports must be submitted..Institutions failing to follow the department’s directive will invite disciplinary action, with headmasters of government schools, and management of private schools being held accountable for the lapse..1k govt schools don’t have a girls’ toilet.The Unified District Information System for Education Plus 2025-26 report found that 170 schools in the state do not have toilets, while 1,001 government schools did not have dedicated lavatories for girls.

headline: Congress wins majority of Zila Pramukh posts in Rajasthan polls
content: JAIPUR After its decisive victory in the last week’s Panchayati Raj elections, the Opposition Congress in Rajasthan on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) took control of 24 of the 37 zila parishads which elected their heads, while the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party secured 10 Zila Pramukh posts despite having a majority in just five rural district bodies. Also read | RLP’s emergence as strong third force in Rajasthan panchayat polls sends new signals https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/rajasthan/rlps-emergence-as-strong-third-force-in-rajasthan-panchayat-polls-sends-new-signals/article71728660.ece The Bharat Adivasi Party won tribal-dominated Banswara and Dungarpur, while Nagaur MP Hanuman Beniwal’s Rashtriya Loktantrik Party retained Nagaur. No independent candidate was elected Zila Pramukh in any district. The votes for panchayat samitis and zila parishads were counted on November 20 in 37 of the State’s 41 districts. Members elected in the panchayat polls voted on Wednesday to choose their respective heads, while the results in the remaining four districts – Kota, Baran, Karauli and Sriganganagar – will be declared in December. BJP’s urban gains fail to win rural support in Rajasthan panchayat polls BJP’s urban gains fail to win rural support in Rajasthan panchayat polls The outcome is particularly significant as several BJP ministers faced electoral setbacks in their areas of influence BJP’s urban gains fail to win rural support in Rajasthan panchayat polls storyline 1 The BJP pulled off a surprise victory in Churu, where the Congress had a clear majority, and secured five of the eight zila parishads where no party had an absolute majority. The Congress largely managed to keep its flock together, losing only one of the 23 rural bodies where it enjoyed majority. Congress candidate Mamta Gurjar defeated BJP’s Nirmala Rawat by just one vote in Beawar, despite the BJP having a majority. Renu Wala of Congress defeated BJP’s Pooja Jatav by 17 votes to 14 in Bharatpur, which is Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma’s home district. Among the zila parishads where no party had a clear majority, the BJP won Balotra, Didwana-Kuchaman, Deeg, Khairthal-Tijara and Pratapgarh, and the Congress won Salumbar. In Churu, where the Congress held 21 of the 39 seats against the BJP’s 17, ruling party candidate Kanika Singh, daughter-in-law of former Minister Rajendra Rathore, defeated Congress candidate Prakash Devi, indicating cross-voting. Congress candidate Nikita Dudi defeated party rebel Sarita Choudhary, who contested as an Independent, by 23 votes to 18 in Bikaner. Dissatisfaction over the party nomination had reportedly led to the rebellion, while the BJP had withdrawn its candidate in Bikaner. The Congress narrowly avoided an embarrassment in Dholpur despite holding 21 of the 29 seats, as its candidate Anisha Singh defeated her nearest rival by just one vote. The BJP also secured Balotra zila parishad by one vote. The Congress registered comfortable victories in several of its traditional strongholds, including Jaipur, Jodhpur, Alwar, Sikar and Bhilwara. Twenty-one-year-old Congress candidate Santosh Kumari was elected unopposed as Zila Pramukh in Jaisalmer. Ms. Kumari, who completed her class XII and is unmarried, belongs to a Scheduled Tribe community. Two other candidates elected unopposed were Beena Bairwa in Dausa and Asha Devi in Sawai Madhopur. Both of them were Congress candidates. There were stray incidents of arguments and jostling at some places during the election process. Tensions were reported in Jaipur, Bharatpur and Bhilwara, where workers and leaders of rival parties were involved in heated exchanges. Veteran Congress leader and former Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot congratulated the new elected Zila Pramukhs, saying the rural public had reposed faith in them by voting against the BJP government’s “misrule”. “I trust that you will become the voice of the villagers, farmers and livestock keepers,” Mr. Gehlot said.

headline: Delhi to Dhaka: Probe minority attacks, Hasina passport a separate issue
content: NEW DELHI: Amid reports of violence against minorities in Bangladesh, India urged Dhaka to investigate these cases and bring the perpetrators to justice. Government also said Wednesday officially that former PM Sheikh Hasina’s plea for a passport and Bangladesh’s extradition request are two distinct matters that should not be mixed up.“We understandably are concerned at the incidence of violence against minorities in Bangladesh. We urge the government of Bangladesh to thoroughly investigate these incidents and bring the perpetrators to justice,” said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal.The official reiterated India’s position on extradition that it is being examined in line with established processes. “The case of a citizen willing to return voluntarily to her country on a travel document is a matter separate from the extradition plea.”While government has refrained from commenting on the merits of Hasina’s passport application, it believes the case for extradition has weakened because of Hasina’s stated position that she wants to voluntarily return to Bangladesh. As far as India is concerned, the only thing preventing her return is the lack of a travel document.2 Indians injured in Riyadh attackStating that two Indians were injured in a Houthi attack on a Riyadh financial district tower, government has condemned such strikes, saying these seriously endanger civilian lives, violate the sovereignty of Saudi Arabia and undermine regional security and stability. “The Embassy of India in Riyadh is providing all possible assistance to the injured and their families,” MEA said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Bail to be granted under UAPA when there is delay in trial, says Supreme Court
content: NEW DELHI: At a time when differences of opinion among Supreme Court benches on bail jurisprudence have become regular, with contradictory orders being passed and matters being sent to larger benches for authoritative pronouncements, the apex court on Wednesday held that a constitutional court’s power to grant bail for violation of the fundamental right to speedy trial could not be taken away by the stringent provisions of special laws like UAPA.IT granted bail to a govt doctor who has been in jail for more than four years for alleged links with the Naxal movement. In another case, the court held that the severity of allegations could not be the sole ground to deny bail and keep an undertrial in jail for a long period and granted bail to senior govt officials in the multi-crore Jal Jeevan Mission scam in Rajasthan. Both the orders were passed by a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu.A difference of opinion has surfaced on the interpretation of the 2021 verdict of a three-judge bench in the Najeeb case, penned by CJI Surya Kant, in which it was held that the accused could not be kept in custody indefinitely and bail could be granted even under a special law like UAPA. “Courts are expected to appreciate the legislative policy against grant of bail but the rigours of such provisions will melt down where there is no likelihood of trial being completed within a reasonable time,” it had said.But a division bench of the court, while rejecting the bail plea of Delhi riots accused Umar Khalid, later said that, “The jurisprudence of this court does not support a construction whereby delay simpliciter eclipses a statutory regime enacted by Parliament to address offences of a special category.”Criticising it, another division bench said the Najeeb order, which was “the law of the land”, was not followed in the Khalid case. Taking exception to the criticism by a bench of the same strength, another division bench said, “Judgements of this court are not to be answered by counter-observations from another Bench of equal strength,” and referred the case to a larger bench.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Exporters in better position but brace for uncertainty
content: NEW DELHI: Indian exporters are now far better prepared to tackle US President Donald Trump’s tariff turbulence but are bracing for fresh uncertainty till a bilateral trade deal is finalised.“There will be two-three months of uncertainty while we finalise orders for next (2027) winter. Summer won’t be impacted so much as goods would have almost reached (US shores by February),” said Israr Ahmed, director at Farida Group, one of the largest footwear exporters, which has also reduced its exposure to the US.Although the proposed 25 per cent tariffs for structural excess capacity will put India at a disadvantage, exporters are confident that the bilateral trade deal with the US will be signed, reducing the additional burden to 17 per cent.“The proposed US tariff measures are a matter of concern for Indian exporters. The consultation window remains open, and the possibility of a lower tariff under a bilateral trade agreement provides a basis for constructive engagement. The exporting community is taking the development in its stride. Fieo (Federation of Indian Export Organisations) is confident that govt will make a strong case for India and work towards the best possible outcome for the country and its exporters,” said Fieo DG Ajay Sahai.While questioning the rationale of the USTR action, AEPC secretary general Mithileshwar Thakur said that there was no reason to panic. “We are again looking at an increase in tariffs from the US. However, thanks to our govt’s negotiation, we are in a better position compared to other competing manufacturing countries. India should be at 17 per cent (after signing the deal) as compared to 18 per cent for Bangladesh, Indonesia, and for Vietnam, potentially at 20 per cent, once they sign the deal. China has even higher penalties. Ensuring that India is not singled out with a higher penalty tariff is important for all of us,” added Pallab Banerjee, MD, Pearl Global Industries, one of the largest garment exporters.When it comes to business, exporters are likely to rush with consignments to beat the new tariff deadline so that their summer shipments stay unharmed by the latest USTR action.Of course, this is subject to ships and containers being available amid the disruption in global logistics. Since the Iran war started, exporters are opting for free-on-board or FOB shipping where the buyer bears the shipping cost.“The duties will not kick in at least until mid-Feb, which means exporters will rush their consignments, even if it means diverting some production meant for other markets,” said an industry veteran.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Agency officer can’t decide non-tribal land disputes: HC
content: Hyderabad: Telangana high court has ruled that merely because a land parcel falls in a scheduled area does not give an agency divisional officer jurisdiction to decide a dispute between non-tribals, holding that such disputes must be adjudicated by a regular civil court.Justice GM Mohiuddin made the ruling while setting aside orders passed by the agency divisional officer-cum-revenue divisional officer, Achampet, Nagarkurnool district, in a dispute over agricultural land.The RDO had on April 28 granted an ex parte ad-interim injunction restraining one of the parties from interfering with 36 guntas of agricultural land at Kondanagula village in Balmoor mandal. Police protection was subsequently granted on June 25 to enforce the injunction.Challenging the orders, the petitioners contended that the agency divisional officer had no jurisdiction to deal with the dispute as neither party belonged to a Scheduled Tribe.They relied on revenue records showing them as belonging to “BC-D” and the opposite party as “general”, besides citing a Supreme Court ruling in support of their contention.The respondent, however, argued that an earlier order dated April 29, 2023, had recognised her claim over the land and that the subsequent injunction was sought only to protect her possession from interference.After examining the rival submissions, the high court held that the special jurisdiction of Agency authorities was intended to protect tribal people, their property and customs.As no tribal interest was involved in the dispute, the court held that the matter had to be adjudicated by a regular civil court.The high court also found that the injunction order was cryptic, and that the subsequent order granting police protection was contrary to the principles of natural justice.While setting aside the orders, the court directed both parties to maintain status quo regarding the existing physical possession of the land.It clarified that the status quo direction was intended only to preserve the existing situation and should not be construed as a determination of either party’s title or possession over the property.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: Election Commission: Rectify wrong roll entries during SSR via Form
content: NEW DELHI: Through Form 8, meant for changes in particulars, the ongoing special summary revision (SSR) of electoral rolls across 24 states and UTs will offer an opportunity for rectification of any incorrect or erroneous entries in the existing electoral roll based on the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise undertaken earlier.EC Wednesday directed booth-level officers concerned to undertake a field verification where the particulars of an elector in the existing roll do not match the information collected during SIR. These particulars may include the elector’s name, date of birth, mobile number, photograph, among others.“Wherever any mismatch is noticed, the same shall be flagged for verification and for taking necessary corrective action,” EC said in a letter to chief electoral officers of the 24 states/UTs where SSR is being conducted.Sources told TOI that incorrect entries in the electoral roll published after SIR may be flagged by electors, booth-level agents or any other person. BLOs should not make changes solely on the basis of automated identification, an official said.“In respect of such flagged entries, the BLOs shall visit the electors concerned during the ongoing SSR to verify their particulars and obtain duly filled-in and signed Form 8, wherever required. The electoral registration officer (ERO) or assistant ERO shall examine and dispose of such applications in accordance with the prescribed procedure,” EC said.The poll body further instructed that the update of demographic particulars be effected only through Form 8, duly signed by the aggrieved elector and subject to verification and approval by the competent authority.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Women’s panel seeks special probe into interstate egg retrieval racket
content: Hyderabad: An alleged interstate network lured financially vulnerable women to Hyderabad with promises of jobs before persuading them to undergo egg retrieval, prompting the Telangana State Women’s Commission to seek a special investigation into those behind the operation.The commission on Wednesday called for a high-level committee to conduct an impartial probe across states. Citing gaps in the implementation of the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act, it also urged governor Shiv Pratap Shukla to recommend changes to the central law to better protect women’s health, safety and rights.Commission chairperson Nerella Sharada and member Uzma Shakeer raised the issue during a meeting with governor at Lok Bhavan. Sharada briefed him on the commission’s findings, information gathered from officials and the progress of the police investigation.Women promised jobsSharada said recruiters allegedly brought women from several states to Hyderabad with promises of employment, including work at events. After they arrived, the recruiters allegedly exploited their financial difficulties to persuade them to undergo egg retrieval. The commission said women from poor and middle-class families were particularly targeted.Malkajgiri police had earlier said agents recruited women from seven states, offering them ₹30,000 to ₹50,000 for egg donation. Police rescued 48 women during searches at hostels in Begumpet, Uppal and other areas and arrested eight agents.Governor seeks detailsSharada also briefed governor on the high court’s dismissal of anticipatory bail petitions filed by three doctors who run fertility centres in Hyderabad.According to the commission, Shukla sought more details and said he would discuss the case with departmental officials and consult the state govt on further action.Sharada said the commission would continue to pursue the matter until the investigation was completed and those responsible were brought to justice.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: Cabinet ministers advised to avoid foreign travel; Parliament session likely by December 15
content: NEW DELHI: Amid continuing suspense over the government’s plan to push the delimitation bill, Cabinet ministers have been asked to avoid planning overseas travel and engagements and remain prepared for Parliament to be convened at short notice, possibly anytime before mid-December.PM Narendra Modi is learnt to have hinted at the likelihood of a parliamentary session by December 15 at the Cabinet meeting chaired by him Wednesday. Government sources have maintained that the Constitution amendment bill to implement the women’s reservation law from the 2029 general elections and increase the strength of Lok Sabha by around 50 per cent is likely to be introduced in the next sitting of Parliament.The government’s decision not to prorogue the monsoon session, which was adjourned sine die on Aug 13, has also fuelled speculation that it’s meant to facilitate early resumption of Parliamentary proceedings. Keeping the session alive allows the parliamentary affairs ministry to reconvene both Houses at three days’ notice without going through the process of summoning a fresh session.Although NDA has maintained a tight lid on its legislative strategy, senior functionaries have expressed confidence that the government will secure the two-thirds majority required to pass the Constitution amendment bill. This is a significant challenge, given that the opposition’s united stand had thwarted the government’s attempt to get the legislation through when it was first introduced in April.The political landscape, however, has changed since then, with the INDIA bloc showing signs of fragmentation. The government is understood to be factoring in these developments while assessing its numbers and prospects of securing the required support.The proposed legislation seeks to link the implementation of women’s reservation with a delimitation exercise that would redraw parliamentary constituencies and substantially expand Lok Sabha’s strength. The proposed expansion and the methodology for delimitation have been among the principal points of contention, with opposition parties raising concerns over their potential implications for the political representation of states. However, the government has tried to assuage concerns by saying that each state‘s share of seats in the Lok Sabha will increase by 50 per cent.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Two-day consultation on One Health - Antimicrobial Resistance Action Plan for Tamil Nadu held
content: CHENNAI A total of 105 officials from 19 departments came together for a two-day consultation on the development of One Health - Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) Action Plan for Tamil Nadu. The consultation, which was organised by the Health department with technical support from the United Nations Development Programme, India, deliberated on various aspects of the action plan in alignment with the National AMR Action Plan 2.0. It was organised on November 23 and 24, according to a social media post by the Directorate of Public Health and Preventive Medicine. A. Somasundaram, Director of Public Health and Preventive Medicine, said the participants were from different departments, including directorates of Medical and Rural Health Services, Medical Education and Research, Public Health and Preventive Medicine, Forest, Fisheries, Tamil Nadu Water Supply and Drainage Board, Animal Husbandry, Surgery, Medicine, Microbiology, Pharmacology, Community medicine and Drugs Control, and the Tamil Nadu Veterinary and Animal Sciences University. As part of the stakeholder workshops, discussions on AMR surveillance and antibiograms, antimicrobial stewardship and antibiotic use, infection prevention and hospital practices, animal health, food safety and fisheries, environment, wastewater and safe disposal, awareness, capacity building, and responsible access were held. He said that rational use of drugs, prescription audits, antibiogram publication, public awareness and capacity building were among the main points of discussion.

headline: After 30 years in jail, former Punjab CM Beant Singh's assassin seeks parity with Rajiv Gandhi's killer in SC
content: NEW DELHI: Invoking the ground of parity with former PM Rajiv Gandhi killer AG Perarivalan, who was a death convict but was allowed to be released and is now a practising lawyer, Balwant Singh Rajoana, who has been in jail for over 30 years and is facing a death sentence for the assassination of former Punjab chief minister Beant Singh, requested the SC on Wednesday that the same reformative approach should be taken for him also and his sentence be commuted to life imprisonment. SC reserved its order.Appearing before a bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Aparesh Singh, senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, for Rajoana, said that he was a misguided youth at the time of the offence and he is now a reformed man. Rohatgi contended that Rajiv Gandhi killer Perarivalan is now a practising lawyer after his death sentence was commuted to life imprisonment and the sentence was later remitted by the apex court on the ground that he spent 30 years in jail. The senior advocate said his client also spent more than 30 years in jail and he should also be allowed the same relief.Opposing his plea, ASG KM Nataraj, appearing for the Centre, said that no relief should be extended to him as the convict had himself declared he did not have faith in the Constitution and judicial system. But Rohatgi said the statement was made 30 years ago during trial and that should not be a ground to deny him liberty after three decades.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Telangana high court allows JEE aspirant without Aadhaar to register for exam with CGHS card
content: Hyderabad: The Telangana high court has allowed a JEE Main 2027 aspirant without an Aadhaar card to use his Central Govt Health Scheme (CGHS) card as identity proof to register for the examination. The court directed the National Testing Agency (NTA) to facilitate the student’s application after he failed to complete the Aadhaar-based e-KYC process.Justice EV Venugopal passed the order on Nov 19 while hearing a petition filed by the minor student, who challenged the indirect requirement of Aadhaar for registering for JEE Main 2027 through the DigiLocker application.The petitioner argued that the requirement violated Articles 14, 16 and 21 of the Constitution, and sought directions to remove the mandatory Aadhaar requirement from the registration process.The student’s counsel, Bhuvan Deepak Pedapati, argued that educational bodies such as CBSE, NEET, JEE and UGC cannot make Aadhaar compulsory under Section 7 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016, and cited precedent apex court rulings in such matters.The petitioner said he could not complete the prescribed e-KYC formalities because he did not have an Aadhaar number. This prevented him from completing his JEE Main 2027 application.Appearing for the respondents, Central govt standing counsel Kalvala Sanjeev told the court that NTA had introduced DigiLocker-based registration with identity verification to simplify the application process.He said the system allows candidates to retrieve the required documents automatically and helps prevent impersonation during examinations. More than 10 lakh candidates had already completed registration through the prescribed process.The govt also informed the court that candidates could submit alternative identity documents, including a PAN card, driving licence or passport.Relying on precedent apex court rulings covering such matters, and considering that the petitioner did not possess a PAN card, driving licence or passport, the Telangana high court partly allowed the minor student’s petition.It directed NTA to facilitate his JEE Main 2027 registration by allowing him to submit the details of his CGHS card, issued by the competent statutory authority, as identity proof.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: TG RERA orders action against developer for selling flats before obtaining permits
content: Hyderabad: Three buyers paid ₹96 lakh in full for flats at Tulasi Bhagyanagar in Dundigal before the two blocks housing them had obtained building permits or RERA registration, the Telangana Real Estate Regulatory Authority found. In a Nov 25 order, the authority directed its secretary to initiate suo motu proceedings against Bhuvanteza Infra Projects Pvt Ltd and Green Metro Infratech Projects Pvt Ltd. It also awarded 10.85% annual interest for delayed possession to all four buyers who filed complaints.Permits came after sale agreementsD Srinivas Reddy and Sanganabatla Surender paid ₹28 lakh each for flats in Block E, while Supraja Godisela paid ₹40 lakh for a Block C flat. Bhuvanteza signed the sale agreements in Dec 2021. The blocks secured building permits on Jan 18, 2022, and RERA registration on Aug 23, 2022. Kotha Vijaya Laxmi, the fourth buyer, paid ₹40 lakh for a flat in Block A, which already had both approvals.Bhuvanteza described itself as a marketing agent and said police had frozen its accounts. Green Metro, the registered promoter, denied authorising the sales or receiving the money. The authority held both firms jointly and severally liable. It found that Bhuvanteza had collected the full price without registered sale agreements, while Green Metro produced no evidence that it had objected to the sales.Extension to 2028 did not shift buyers’ deadlineThe authority held that extending project registration to 2028 did not alter the agreed possession date. It directed the firms to pay accrued interest within 60 days and monthly interest thereafter until handover. They must complete the flats with the promised amenities, obtain an occupancy certificate, and register and hand over the flats within 60 days of obtaining it. headline: Missing businessman's non-bailable warrant cancelled in AJL case, ED to move high court
content: NEW DELHI: Surprised by an order of a special MP/MLA court in Rouse Avenue here cancelling the non-bailable warrant (NBW) against a wanted businessman who had been evading arrest for the last four years, the Enforcement Directorate is likely to move the Delhi high court challenging the grounds on which relief was granted to him in absentia.The case pertains to Dinesh Pandey of Saanag group in India and Somap group in Singapore, who was granted relief on Nov 14 by the special court, which cancelled the NBW against him.Sources said he is wanted in connection with the investigation into transfer of Rs 10.4 crore allegedly through a shell company to Associated Journals Ltd (AJL), a company which has since been taken over by Young Indian, controlled by Congress leaders Rahul and Sonia Gandhi.A senior ED official tracking the case said it was settled practice that warrants against an absconding accused were not cancelled so long as he stayed away and did not appear before the investigators.“The order also faults the investigating officer for placing part of the case diary before the court in a sealed cover, although sealing sensitive material for the court’s perusal is routine in serious economic offences,” the official said. headline: Supreme Court suggests referring KMC delimitation case back to High Court for fresh look
content: New Delhi The Supreme Court indicated orally on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) its inclination to set aside a Calcutta High Court order that put on hold the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) elections over a delimitation exercise, and requested the High Court to hear the dispute afresh. Bills for delimitation of Kolkata and Howrah municipal corporation passed in West Bengal Assembly storyline 1 A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant made the suggestion while hearing an appeal filed by the West Bengal government against the High Court order of November 6. The High Court had directed the West Bengal State Election Commission to not notify the elections until a petition challenging the delimitation of municipal wards was decided. Justice Surya Kant: Striking a balance in a divided nation storyline 1 Calcutta High Court restrains KMC polls until challenge on delimitation decided Calcutta High Court restrains KMC polls until challenge on delimitation decided The West Bengal government, through a delimitation, has increased the number of wards of KMC from 144 to 209. The petitioner argued that the State government and its agencies have resorted to gerrymandering in order to secure partisan advantage to the ruling political party in West Bengal on the premise of previous electoral results. Calcutta High Court restrains KMC polls until challenge on delimitation decided storyline 1 Chief Justice Kant said the apex court was inclined to set aside the order of the High Court after taking into consideration pertinent legal and factual issues raised by the State government. The writ petition could also be transferred from the Single Judge Bench to a Division Bench, which would consider the entire dispute afresh and pass appropriate orders. “And till the Division Bench forms a view the polls can be held off,” the court suggested orally. The lawyers for both the State and former CPI(M) councillor Dipu Das, who had filed the petition in the High Court against the delimitation exercise, sought time to take instructions. The court listed the case for further hearing on November 30. West Bengal government to appoint coordinators if stay on civic polls not lifted, says CM Adhikari West Bengal government to appoint coordinators if stay on civic polls not lifted, says CM Adhikari Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that his government would approach the Supreme Court with a Special Leave Petition (SLP) seeking that the stay on holding civic polls be lifted West Bengal government to appoint coordinators if stay on civic polls not lifted, says CM Adhikari storyline 1 The Bench reasoned that its proposed “ad-hoc arrangement” would place both parties on an “even keel” without the Supreme Court expressing any opinion on the merits of the dispute. The KMC had undertaken a revision of municipal ward boundaries ahead of the civic polls. As part of the plan, the number of wards in the civic body may rise to 209 from the current 144. A Division Bench of the High Court had stopped the State Election Commission from issuing the election notification till the Single Judge Bench hearing Mr. Das’s petition decided the legality of the ward delimitation exercise. West Bengal government to appoint coordinators for all 209 wards in Kolkata: Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar West Bengal government to appoint coordinators for all 209 wards in Kolkata: Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar This announcement comes as the Kolkata Corporation election remains stalled by the Calcutta High Court; Mamata-Trinamool says why not hold elections and appoint elected representatives West Bengal government to appoint coordinators for all 209 wards in Kolkata: Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar storyline 1 Mr. Das had questioned the delimitation, arguing that the expansion of the municipal wards was void. He had sought a quashing of the September 11 gazette notification on expansion of wards as bad in law. He had contended that the delimitation happened on the basis of electoral rolls instead of the actual population, resulting in the alleged exclusion of a substantial number of residents. After the Single Judge Bench had refused his pleas for an interim stay of the elections, Mr. Das had moved the High Court’s Division Bench.

headline: Governor seeks CM’s report on compliance with SC’s directions
content: Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar on Wednesday sought a comprehensive report from Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on whether the State government had complied with the Supreme Court’s November 20 order on the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam. The move comes in the wake of the ceremonial lamp being lit only at the traditional spot — the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipilliyar Temple — on Tuesday, defying the Supreme Court’s direction to light it on the deepathoon atop the Thirupparankundram hillock as a “limited one-time arrangement”. Sources told The Hindu that the Governor had sought a report from the Chief Minister under Article 167(b) of the Constitution, detailing the action taken by the authorities on the Supreme Court’s directions. It came on the heels of the Madurai Collector telling the Supreme Court, in a preliminary status report filed on Wednesday, that he had made every arrangement to comply with the court’s November 20 order to light the lamp on the deepathoon, but the Board of Trustees of the Arulmigu Subramaniyaswamy Temple had failed to authorise a lamp-lighting team.

headline: Supreme Court nixes Allahabad high court order for Rahul Gandhi’s assets probe
content: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday quashed an Allahabad HC order asking the CBI and ED to probe complaints about leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi’s alleged disproportionate assets and directed the HC to conduct a fresh hearing on the petition with an opportunity for him to oppose it.The top court principally set aside the order because of its ex parte nature, holding that not being given an opportunity to counter the allegations made in the PIL by Karnataka-based BJP worker Shishir Vignesh breached principles of natural justice.Allahabad high court to hear Rahul Gandhi’s plea against PIL: SCWhile the Supreme Court on Wednesday quashed Allahabad high court’s order directing a probe into the assets of the leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, it did not consider Rahul Gandhi’s plea for transfer of the PIL to any other HC or the SC.Senior advocate Kapil Sibal said HC adopted a process “completely unknown to law” while passing the impugned order as it did not even seek Gandhi’s response and permitted a witch-hunt without questioning the petitioner’s locus standi.The bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that HC, during the fresh hearing on Vignesh’s PIL, would hear Gandhi’s submissions against the petition, including the maintainability of such a petition before a constitutional court and the locus standi of the petitioner to raise such issues through a writ petition.On August 17, SC had barred CBI, ED or any other authority from filing any report before HC pursuant to its July 20 order and directed HC to defer the proceedings till further orders. For CBI, additional solicitor general S V Raju had told the court that CBI is only verifying the complaint and has not commenced a probe yet. “CBI has not registered even a preliminary enquiry. The complaint may be wrong or right on facts. If they are right, then it is a gross case of disproportionate assets,” he had said.CJI Kant had said, “In our understanding of the law, police or any probe agency, if they have prima facie material they can register a case, investigate it and can proceed against anyone. No permission is required from the accused. But what appears to us, subject to assistance from both sides, is that if the court wants to issue a direction, it is expected to follow principles of natural justice.”Gandhi, in his special leave petition, had said, “Since 2024, Shishir, who, it appears from public reporting, is a member of BJP — a party whose politics and ideology the Petitioner (Gandhi) and his party (Congress) vehemently contest — has instituted multiple proceedings before different forums, including successive PILs concerning the Petitioner’s alleged foreign citizenship and criminal proceedings seeking registration of an FIR...”Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Amritsar’s past needs to inspire roadmap for future growth: Guv Kataria
content: Guru Nanak Dev University (GNDU) on Tuesday announced an ‘Amritsar 2052 Vision Document’ to chart the city’s development over the next 25 years. Inaugurating the two-day international conclave, ‘Amritsar 450’, Punjab Governor Gulab Chand Kataria said the city’s 450-year journey must be linked with its future development, making the anniversary an opportunity to address contemporary challenges rather than merely celebrate the past.The conclave, themed ‘Remembering the Past, Understanding the Present and Envisioning the Future’, brought together scholars, policymakers and cultural figures to deliberate on the city’s historical legacy and development priorities.Kataria said Punjab’s identity was rooted in the teachings of the Sikh Gurus, which upheld humanity, equality, service and sacrifice. “With the need to preserve historical and religious heritage, we must prepare youth for emerging opportunities, with initiatives in education, research, agriculture and industry,” Kataria said.Agricultural diversification, food processing, water conservation, alternative energy and technological innovation were among the areas he identified as crucial for Punjab’s future.Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, who attended the conclave as a special guest, said the city’s development must remain connected with its spiritual and cultural identity.“Amritsar has evolved into a centre of spirituality, education and culture,” he said, stressing the need to preserve heritage buildings, old neighbourhoods and traditions alongside improving urban infrastructure and promoting tourism-led economic growth.“Linking education with skills and employment also addresses the need to ensure that the city’s young population benefits from its growth,” he said.GNDU Vice-Chancellor Prof Karamjeet Singh said the university had initiated projects, including the vision document and a digital repository of 450 oral-history videos capturing the memories of elderly residents.“The 450 oral-history videos are equally important as they would preserve the memories of residents as living heritage, beyond monuments and official records,” he said. US-based Sikh scholar Prof Gurinder Singh Mann called for an original approach to Sikh historiography rather than relying on Western methodologies.“Imitating Western approaches and methodologies has not benefited the understanding of Sikh history to a great extent. There is a need to develop an original approach to Sikh historiography based on Gurbani, Sikh philosophy and historical sources,” he said.The conclave also featured discussions on the city’s spiritual heritage, a panel discussion and a light-and-sound show, ‘Dastaan-e-Amritsar’.The proposed vision document could provide a long-term framework for urban planning, heritage conservation, tourism, infrastructure and employment, with the focus on modernising Amritsar while preserving its spiritual character and cultural fabric.

headline: Judge Clears New York City Rent Freeze Backed by Mayor Mamdani
content: (Bloomberg) -- A rent freeze backed by New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s administration was cleared by a state judge who dismissed a lawsuit filed by a group of landlords seeking to void the measure, which went into effect last month.The landlords sued the city’s Rent Guidelines Board in July, arguing that Mamdani improperly influenced the vote and ignored evidence of rising operating costs for building owners. A judge on Wednesday threw out the case, saying the decision to implement the freeze was not “unreasonable, arbitrary or capricious” and must be upheld.But the judge, Brendan T. Lantry, sharply criticized Mamdani’s campaign promises to freeze the rent. The mayor’s comments were “reckless and irresponsible” because only the board can raise, freeze or adjust the rent of stabilized units in the city, the judge wrote. Correspondence between the mayor’s office and the board about the measure was “troubling” and “puts a dark shadow over the purported ‘independence’ of the board,” but it doesn’t show that the mayor dictated the decision, Lantry said.“The court recognizes that political candidates routinely comment on prevalent policy issues while running for an elected position, but to guarantee a rent freeze to millions of New Yorkers without the authority to do so, is irresponsible and, quite frankly, invited” the lawsuit, the judge wrote. Still, there is “nothing to suggest the guideline-setting process was an orchestrated ‘sham process,” Lantry said.In a statement, Mamdani cheered the decision. “This is a victory for tenants, for affordability and for the principle that working New Yorkers deserve a city they can afford to live in,” he said. “Because housing is not a luxury. It is a basic necessity. This holiday weekend, more than two million New Yorkers can breathe a little easier.”Randy Mastro, a lawyer for the landlords and a former deputy mayor in the Giuliani administration who has also challenged the pied-a-terre tax backed by Mamdani, didn’t respond to a message seeking comment.The suit came weeks after the board voted for the first time ever to freeze rents for both one-year and two-year leases for roughly 1 million stabilized apartments. The last one-year rent freeze was during the pandemic in 2020.Courts have historically deferred to the Rent Guidelines Board. A state court judge dismissed a challenge by landlords to a 2016 rent freeze. While that lawsuit claimed the board didn’t account for finances of the building, this challenge focused on the mayor’s involvement. Mamdani made the freeze a centerpiece of his mayoral campaign, contending that tenants squeezed by years of rising housing costs needed immediate relief. After taking office, he appointed a majority of the board’s members. A member of the board who represented landlords, Christina Smyth, resigned in protest hours before the vote. Tenant advocates hailed the vote as a long-overdue reset after inflation and housing shortages left many renters facing mounting financial pressure. Landlord and housing industry groups have warned that the freeze will make it harder for owners to maintain aging buildings and finance fixes as insurance, taxes and repair costs have surged amid a tight rental market.The case is Kenilworth Holdings LLC v New York City Rent Guidelines Board, 453580/2026, New York State Supreme Court, New York County.--With assistance from Laura Nahmias.More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

headline: Cyberabad Municipal Corporation suspends official for use of ‘drainage water’ in green tankers, cancels contractor’s work order
content: Hyderabad: Cyberabad Municipal Corporation (CMC) has suspended an Urban Biodiversity (UBD) circle manager and initiated disciplinary action against other personnel after untreated drainage water was allegedly used to fill green water tankers meant to carry treated wastewater for watering plants along road medians.The action follows reports that water collected from drainage sources in Khajaguda was being supplied through green water tankers. Taking serious note of the violation, CMC commissioner G Srijana placed Vikram Chandra, circle manager of the UBD wing, Serilingampally, who is also in charge of the Narsingi and Patancheru circles, under suspension. Gopal, an outsourcing supervisor, has also been identified for disciplinary action. Separately, the civic body cancelled the work order issued to the contractor concerned.The incident came to light after a video showing the activity went viral on X on Wednesday. The video showed water from a nala being collected using high-power motors. “When contacted for an explanation, the official concerned defended the action, stating that water was collected from a nearby nala in an urgent situation to fill a tanker and use it for watering plants along road medians,” Srijana said.CMC has reiterated that only properly treated wastewater sourced from STPs should be supplied through green water tankers for designated non-potable purposes.
