headline: HC: Rent laws don’t give tenants a permanent right of occupation
content: Rent laws cannot be used to deny a landlord possession once a legal ground for eviction is established, the Punjab and Haryana High Court has ruled, observing that a tenant cannot claim continued occupation merely because of a long tenancy.“The protection afforded to a tenant under the rent control legislation is intended to safeguard him against arbitrary eviction and not to enable him to perpetuate his occupation notwithstanding the establishment of a statutory ground of eviction,” Justice Deepak Gupta observed. “Once such a ground stands established in accordance with law, the landlord cannot be deprived of possession of the premises merely on account of the length of the tenancy.”The ruling came while dismissing a tenant’s revision petition against concurrent eviction orders passed by the Rent Controller and Appellate Authority, Amritsar. Among other things, the Rent Controller upon appraisal of the evidence returned findings in the landlady’s favour “on the grounds of the demised premises having become unfit and unsafe for human habitation and bona fide personal necessity”.The ground regarding non-payment of house tax/property tax was, however, decided against the landlady. After adjusting the payments already made by the tenants, Rs 7,592 was found outstanding towards arrears of rent, for which two months was granted. “Independently thereof, an order of eviction was passed against the tenants on the other grounds established by the landlady,” the Bench noted.Taking up the matter, Justice Gupta held that a landlord need not wait for a dilapidated building to collapse or an accident involving loss of life or property before seeking eviction on the ground that the premises have become unfit and unsafe for human habitation.“It is also not necessary for the landlord to wait until the building actually collapses or some unfortunate incident involving loss of life or property takes place before seeking eviction on this statutory ground. The very object of the provision would stand defeated if the landlord were required to await the actual collapse of the building despite credible evidence of its unsafe condition,” Justice Gupta ruled.The Bench further clarified that Section 13(3)(a)(iii) of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, did not prescribe expert evidence as the exclusive mode of establishing structural unsafety. “Such a finding may be recorded on the basis of other reliable evidence, including the testimony of persons acquainted with the condition of the building and, more particularly, admissions made by the tenant himself,” Justice Gupta ruled.The court noted that the tenant had stated in earlier proceedings that “condition of roof of demised shop is dilapidated and it can fall also.” Justice Gupta asserted: The admission is of considerable importance, particularly because it emanates from the person, who is himself in occupation of the demised premises and is, therefore, well acquainted with its physical condition. Though an admission is not conclusive proof of the matter admitted, it constitutes substantive evidence against its maker and can legitimately form the basis of a finding unless satisfactorily explained or shown to be erroneous”.Holding that no perversity or illegality warranting interference had been established, Justice Gupta dismissed the revision petition.

headline: Stroke is treatable, but every minute matters: Neurologist
content: Stroke is one of the leading causes of death and long-term disability worldwide. However, timely recognition, appropriate treatment and effective prevention can save lives and significantly reduce its impact.A stroke occurs when the blood supply to a part of the brain is interrupted or a blood vessel ruptures, damaging brain cells. There are two main types — ischaemic stroke, caused by a blood clot blocking a blood vessel, and haemorrhagic stroke, caused by bleeding in or around the brain. Both require immediate medical attention.A common misconception is that stroke affects only older people. Young adults, including those in their twenties and thirties, can also experience a stroke. High blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, obesity, high cholesterol, heart disease and physical inactivity are major risk factors. Among younger individuals, certain heart conditions and blood vessel abnormalities can also increase the risk.Recognising the warning signs is crucial. The BE FAST approach helps identify symptoms — balance difficulties, eye or vision changes, facial drooping, arm weakness, speech difficulty and time to seek emergency medical care. Sudden numbness, confusion or a severe, unexplained headache may also indicate a stroke. Even if the symptoms disappear, immediate medical assessment is essential.Advances in treatment have transformed stroke care. Thrombolysis, or clot-busting therapy, is most effective when administered early and is generally considered within 4.5 hours of symptom onset in eligible patients with ischaemic stroke. Every minute of delay can reduce the chances of recovery.Mechanical thrombectomy is an advanced procedure in which specialists remove a clot from a blocked brain artery using catheter-based techniques. It is particularly beneficial for selected patients with large-vessel occlusion. The procedure should be performed as early as possible, with selected patients eligible for treatment up to 24 hours after they were last known to be well, depending on clinical assessment and advanced brain imaging. Both treatments require urgent specialist evaluation and are not suitable for every patient or for haemorrhagic stroke.Prevention remains our strongest defence. Maintaining healthy blood pressure, controlling diabetes and cholesterol, exercising regularly, eating a balanced diet, avoiding tobacco and managing heart conditions can substantially reduce the risk. Stroke should never be ignored or considered an inevitable consequence of ageing.

headline: Infrastructure works for Knowledge City under way, says T.N. Minister for Industries
content: Chennai Tamil Nadu Minister for Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce S. Keerthana on Tuesday said infrastructure works for Knowledge City is under way in the phase one construction of the project. She was speaking at the curtain raiser event of the India Global Education Summit 2027 (IGES) held in Chennai. The 872-acre Knowledge City is coming up in Tiruvallur district on the northern outskirts of Chennai where innovation, knowledge and research would be enhanced by bringing together universities, research labs, and research-oriented industries in a collaborative ecosystem. In the first phase, 413 acres are being developed. The Minister noted that plot allocation under this would begin by April 2027. Further, one-lakh-square-foot Knowledge Tower is also being built where plug-and-play facilities would be provided to enable foreign universities to function. Sources in Tamil Nadu Industrial Development Corporation Limited (TIDCO) noted that the tower would be ready by the later part of 2028. Speaking about the project, Ms. Keerthana said, “Institutions such as University of Melbourne and IIT Madras are already engaged with us. Further, five institutions have already signed memorandums of understanding to take up space there.” The second edition of the IGES will take place from February 3, 2027 to February 5, 2027 in Mamallapuram. The summit aims to discuss knowledge economy which includes artificial intelligence, skilling, among others. The summit will be hosted in partnership with National Indian Students and Alumni Union (NISAU), a UK body representing universities. Minister for Artificial Intelligence, Information Technology and Digital Services R. Kumar invited people, companies and institutions to invest in the AI city and Knowledge City that has been planned in the State. Electronics Corporation of Tamil Nadu Managing Director B. Vishnu Chandran, TIDCO Chairman and Managing Director D. Karthikeyan, IIT Madras Director V. Kamakoti, Data and AI director, Microsoft Cecil Sunder, Artificial Intelligence, Information Technology and Digital Services department Additional Chief Secretary Atul Anand and NISAU founder Sanam Arora also spoke at the event. headline: San Francisco Coastline Is Swamped by Record-High King Tides
content: (Bloomberg) -- Record flooding from king tides is inundating the California coast Wednesday, compounded by a Pacific storm that’s contributing to flight delays in San Francisco.Tuesday’s high tide of 8.23 feet (2.51 meters) was the largest ever recorded in the city during the month of November. Wednesday’s high tide may surpass it, said Sebastian Westerink, a US National Weather Service meteorologist in Monterey.“Today and tomorrow around noon are going to be the worst,” Westerink said. “Then it is going to start lowering from there.”About 145 flights through San Francisco International Airport were delayed Wednesday, according to FlightAware, a tracking site.Flood warnings remain across San Francisco, much of the Bay Area and the Pacific coastline. Gauges on Wednesday in Santa Barbara and San Diego recorded their highest tides ever, the weather service said, breaking records set about a month ago.Rough seas and dangerous swells have been spotted along California’s shores. Authorities in Marin County north of San Francisco issued a “shelter-in-place” order to residents in the Calles area of Stinson Beach as waves push past the beach. There’s also an evacuation warning in Stinson Beach — a community of 541 people — as large waves are expected through 2 p.m. local time.Evacuation warnings are in effect more than 300 miles (483 km) south in Ventura County. The alerts encompass waterfront neighborhoods recently fortified with protective berms.California’s king tides, the highest predicted tides of the year, recur when the sun, moon and Earth align and the moon is closest to Earth. This year, they’re arriving after El Niño helped raise sea levels and powerful waves battered the state’s coastline, damaging roads and destroying homes.Travel has become dangerous at times: King tides have forced road closures and shut down portions of the Pacific Coast Highway in Orange County, south of Los Angeles.--With assistance from Todd Woody.(Updates with flight delays in 4th paragraph. headline: The hands that healed, the wisdom that inspired generations
content: For generations of medical students and surgeons at Government Medical College (GMC), Amritsar, Dr Bhola Singh Sidhu was more than a teacher — he was a mentor who taught them to trust clinical judgement, put patients first and never give up on a difficult case.His sudden demise has left a void in the city’s medical fraternity. Dr Sidhu, an eminent surgeon and former Head of the Department of Surgery at GMC, died while on a morning walk on Monday.Professionally active and intellectually engaged well into his eighties, Dr Sidhu was remembered as an institution in himself — a pioneering surgeon, dedicated academician, researcher and mentor who shaped generations of medical professionals. He spent much of his professional career at GMC, Amritsar, from where he retired as Professor and Head of the Department of Surgery.Belonging to a generation of surgeons who relied heavily on clinical judgement and bedside examination, he adapted to changing medical practices and embraced laparoscopic surgery following its introduction. He went on to become one of the region’s prominent practitioners of minimally invasive surgery.Paying tributes, Dr Rakesh Sharma, his former student and a minimally invasive surgeon at GMC, said Dr Sidhu’s contributions to buttonhole surgery, hernia surgery and the management of complicated gall bladder cases remained particularly significant.“Teaching remained central to his life. He trained numerous postgraduate surgeons and taught generations of undergraduate medical students. He is remembered for his patience, discipline in clinical examination and insistence that the patient, rather than diagnostic investigations, should remain at the centre of medical practice,” he said.Dr Atul Kapoor, another former student, remembered him as an avid reader and prolific academician. He said Dr Sidhu remained a researcher throughout his life, publishing several papers in international journals. Even in his later years, his academic curiosity remained undiminished.Kapoor said their recent collaborative research with Dr Jasdeep Singh on the preoperative assessment of the gall bladder received the Best Research of the Year award from the Asia-Pacific and Taiwan Society of Ultrasound.Recalling his approach to complicated clinical cases, his students said he never gave up on a problem. He would often refer to his residency days when surgeons had limited diagnostic facilities and relied on patient examination, observation and clinical judgement to arrive at a diagnosis.Born in Jhakharwal village of Faridkot district, Dr Sidhu later made Amritsar his home. He joined GMC, Amritsar, in 1987 and retired in 2002. He is survived by his wife, Dr Amarjeet Sidhu, former Head of the Department of Dermatology and two children.

headline: Bus crash victims’ kin demand govt jobs
content: Families of those killed in the recent collision involving two buses operating under the Chief Minister Tirath Yatra Yojana, led by the Kirti Kisan Union, on Wednesday submitted a memorandum to Deputy Commissioner Dr Nirmal Ouseppachan, demanding compensation of Rs 30 lakh for each victim’s family.Nachhattar Singh Pannu, district president of the Kirti Kisan Union, who led the delegation, said families affected by a similar accident in Muktsar district had received Rs 18 lakh each, though Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann had announced compensation of Rs 5 lakh per family.Pannu said Narinder Singh, a resident of Chhajjalwadi village, was among those killed in the accident. He was driving one of the buses that was on its way to Amritsar. He said the compensation announced by the Chief Minister was inadequate in view of the loss suffered by the families. Besides providing Rs 30 lakh to each affected family, he demanded that one member of every victim’s family be given a government job.The Deputy Commissioner, while receiving the memorandum, assured the delegation that it would be forwarded to the Punjab Government for consideration. He said the state committee overseeing the Chief Minister’s Tirath Yatra Yojana would take further action on the matter.

headline: Karnal emerges bright spot in HPV vaccination push
content: Karnal has emerged as Haryana’s best-performing district in the ongoing Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination campaign, achieving 70% of its target, more than double the state’s overall coverage of 31%, according to Health Department data.Against a statewide target of 2.26 lakh adolescent girls in the 14-15 age group, 70,413 have received the vaccine so far. Launched on February 28 initially as a three-month campaign, the drive aims to protect adolescent girls against HPV infection, a major cause of cervical cancer. The campaign has subsequently been extended until December 31, 2026.Karnal leads the state with 8,610 girls vaccinated against a target of 12,352. Kaithal ranks second with 5,876 vaccinations, achieving 68% coverage, followed by Yamunanagar at 63%, with 5,908 beneficiaries vaccinated against a target of 9,398. Kurukshetra has achieved 59% coverage, while Panipat stands at 42%.At the other end of the performance chart, Jhajjar has recorded the lowest coverage at just 9%, with 677 girls vaccinated against a target of 7,272. Nuh stands at 13%, Hisar at 16% and Jind at 17%. Faridabad and Fatehabad have recorded 20% each.Charkhi Dadri and Sirsa have achieved 36% coverage each, followed by Mahendragarh and Palwal at 32%. Sonepat has recorded 30%, Panchkula 28%, Bhiwani 27% and Gurugram 26%.To improve coverage, Karnal health authorities have intensified door-to-door outreach and awareness activities to address misconceptions about the vaccine. On the directions of Deputy Commissioner Anand Kumar Sharma, teams are visiting government and private schools.The Health Department is also coordinating with the Education and Panchayati Raj departments, besides involving Anganwadi workers and ASHAs to reach eligible families. Civil Surgeon Dr Shashi Garg appealed to parents to ignore rumours and rely on medical advice. She said the department had directed its teams to reach out to families whose daughters were yet to be vaccinated. Dr Abhay Aggarwal, nodal officer for the campaign, said ASHAs and Anganwadi workers, along with auxiliary nurse midwives, were preparing lists of remaining beneficiaries.

headline: Haryana leaders welcome Guru Ravidas yatra at Kalanaur
content: Samrasta Sankalp Yatra, being organised to mark the 650th birth anniversary year of Guru Ravidas, entered the state on Wednesday.The yatra was welcomed by the BJP leaders, public representatives and members of various communities at Kalanaur village in Yamunanagar district, which is located on the border of Haryana and Uttar Pradesh.The yatra, which began on November 18 from Dera Sachkhand Ballan in Jalandhar (Punjab) will conclude on December 3 at Seer-Govardhanpur, the birthplace of Guru Ravidas in Varanasi.After the Kalanaur programme, the yatra proceeded towards Ambala district, passing through Barara and Ugla before reaching Kurukshetra.According to information, Haryana Development and Panchayat, Mines and Geology Minister Krishan Lal Panwar; Haryana Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shyam Singh Rana, Social Justice and Empowerment Minister Krishan Kumar Bedi; Indri MLA and government chief whip Ram Kumar Kashyap, former minister Kanwar Pal Gujjar, former BJP MP from Sirsa Sunita Duggal, state BJP president of BJP Scheduled Caste Morcha Ajay Khundia, BJP district president Rajesh Sapra, BJP state media in-charge Bhupeshwar Dayal, BJP district media in-charge Kapil Manish Garg and other BJP leaders gave a grand welcome to the Samrasta Sankalp Yatra.A grand programme was organised in Kalanaur village. Addressing the gathering, BJP National Secretary Bhola Singh said that on the call of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the sacred soil brought from Varanasi, the holy birthplace of Guru Ravidas, was distributed to every corner of the country. He said that now this Samrasta Sankalp Yatra had been started from Sachkhand Balla and would go to various states of the country.Panwar said that the 650th birth anniversary of Guru Ravidas was being celebrated in the country. Shyam Singh Rana said through this yatra, they learnt about the words of saints, the paths they show and their teachings. Krishan Bedi said that India’s strength lies in its spiritual consciousness, cultural diversity and unity.Kanwar Pal Gujjar said that the primary objective of this yatra was to spread Guru Ravidas’ message of social equality and to promote harmony in society.Welcoming the yatra at the event, BJP district president Rajesh Sapra said, “If we want to make our country a great and developed nation, we must follow the path shown by our saints.”

headline: Private schools’ body urges Haryana Government to clear reimbursements
content: The National Independent Schools Alliance (NISA) has urged the Haryana Government to immediately release pending reimbursement amounts under Rule 134-A, RTE and the CHEERAG scheme.NISA national president Kulbhushan Sharma said private schools had been implementing various student welfare schemes, but the schools were not getting the reimbursement in time. Reimbursement for teaching students belonging to the EWS category under Rule 134-A of the Haryana School Education Rules was the prime reason behind the dispute between the government and private schools. In 2022, Rule 134-A was omitted and the Right to Free and Compulsory Education Act was implemented, but the reimbursement issue remains, as students admitted under Rule 134-A are still studying in these schools.“The private schools in the state have been continuously providing education to the children belonging to economically weaker sections under Rule 134-A. The schools are also providing education to children under the RTE and CM Haryana Equal Education Relief Assistance and Grant (CHEERAG) scheme. However, despite implementing the government schemes, the private schools are not getting the reimbursement dues in time”, he said.Kulbhushan Sharma said, “We have been raising the issue of timely reimbursement with the department repeatedly and every time we are assured that the department will clear the dues in time, but the dues are yet to be cleared. Despite their limited financial capacity, the schools are striving to maintain children’s education, teachers’ salaries, and other educational programmes. Small and low-fee schools, in particular, have been facing financial hardship.”The president of the schools association said weak school finances will impact teachers, educational resources, and ultimately, the quality of education children receive.He said requests have been sent to Vijay Singh Dahiya, Principal Secretary, School Education Department, and the Director of Elementary Education Department, Manita Malik, in this regard.“We have requested the officials to get a complete review done of the pending payments at the Directorate level and issue instructions to the officials concerned to complete the payment process immediately. If it is not possible to pay all schools in one go, then priority should be given to smaller, low-fee schools”, he said.

headline: Exclusive: Angry Congress MP Repeats "Beggar" Jibe, Samajwadi Leader Slams "Ego"
content: Beggars. If one word has divided the country's most prominent opposition allies, it is this. Akhilesh Yadav's Samajwadi Party is reluctant to spare a lion's share to its ally, the Congress, in the upcoming assembly elections in UP. Its offer of at least 26 seats has come across as humiliation for the Congress. And the party's MP and UP working president Imran Masood has refused to 'beg' for its alliance share. Masood repeated the "beggar" remark for a second time while speaking to NDTV today, as he made his anger obvious and visible. The agitated Congress MP accused the SP of trying to dictate terms to his party. "Why should we fight (as per your terms) and spoil our strike rate. You want cream, but won't let us have even the buttermilk. We are not beggars that you will give us whatever you want," he said, before making a staunch declaration, "We don't need instructions from Akhilesh ji." READ | As An Angry Congress Breathes Fire, Samajwadi MP Calls Outburst "Personal" The Congress is understood to have first sought 181 seats in a state with 403 total constituencies. Given that was unlikely even in the best scenario for them, they trimmed the list to 131, and then to 110. But Samajwadi Party has offered just 26. The gap in the ask and the offer reflected a new reality in the alliance dynamics.

headline: Modern facilities to boost technical education in rural areas in Himachal: Minister
content: Education Minister Rohit Thakur today inaugurated a Government Industrial Training Institute (ITI) building, constructed at a cost of Rs 10.62 crore, and a lift drinking water scheme, built at a cost of Rs 1.04 crore, at the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Government Institute of Technology (ABVGIET) at Pragati Nagar in the Jubbal-Nawar-Kotkhai Assembly constituency of Shimla district.Speaking on the occasion, the minister said the state government was prioritising the expansion of educational infrastructure, improvement in the quality of education and employment-oriented technical education. He said the government was committed to providing students in rural and remote areas with better educational facilities and equal opportunities to excel.He added that efforts were underway to further improve facilities for students and faculty members at the institute.Thakur said the tender process for the construction of a Kendriya Vidyalaya in the Kotkhai area was underway. The technical tender would be opened on December 1, 2026, while the financial tender was expected to be opened on December 15, 2026. “It is also expected that Prime Minister Narendra Modi will lay its foundation stone virtually,” he added.The minister said projects worth Rs 100 crore were underway to strengthen educational infrastructure in the region, including Kotkhai and Gumma. He said the process of affiliating the Government School at Gumma with the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) had been affected due to inadequate infrastructure. The government would consider CBSE affiliation once the construction of the school building was completed, he added.Addressing the students, Thakur said their future achievements and contributions to society and nation-building would depend on their dedication, hard work and determination. He said the younger generation was the future of the state and the country and urged students to make the most of the improved educational environment and opportunities available to them to hone their skills and talents.

headline: Colleges must adjust to education shift: Himachal MLA Ashish Butail
content: The 27th National Conference on ‘Higher Education in the Era of Industry 6.0’, organised at Goswami Ganesh Dutt Sanatan Dharma (GGDSD) College, Rajpur, under the joint aegis of the Society for Education and Economic Development (SEED) and the Himachal Pradesh Chapter of the Indian Colleges Forum (ICF), concluded on a grand note.The three-day conference was inaugurated by Prof Lalit Kumar Awasthi, Vice-Chancellor of Sardar Patel University, Mandi. Addressing the gathering, chief guest Ashish Butail congratulated the college management, organisers and participants on the successful completion of the conference. Appreciating the rich legacy and academic contributions of GGDSD College, he emphasised the need for higher education institutions to adapt to the rapidly evolving educational landscape by providing students with greater practical exposure and wider opportunities.He highlighted the crucial role of higher education institutions in promoting quality education, innovation and skill development. He also noted that such academic platforms provide educators an opportunity to deliberate on policies and initiatives that can shape the future of young people.Dr GD Sharma, head of SEED and former UGC Secretary, outlined the genesis and objectives of SEED and the Indian Colleges Forum.

headline: Himachal’s Shimla gears up for winter, maps priority routes
content: To deal effectively with snowfall this winter, the Shimla district administration has divided the city into five sectors.Sector 1 covers Sanjauli, Chhota Shimla, Dhalli, Kufri, Naldehra, Mashobra and Baldeyan. Sector 2 covers the Dhalli-Sanjauli bypass, IGMC, Lakkar Bazaar to Victory Tunnel, Kaithu, Bharari, Chaura Maidan, AG Office, Annadale and Himachal Pradesh University (HPU), Summer Hill. Sector 3 covers Tutikandi Bypass to Shoghi, Chakkar, Baluganj, Totu, Jutogh, Nabha, Phagli, Khalini, BCS and Vikasnagar. Sector 4 covers the DC Office, Victory Tunnel to Cart Road to Chhota Shimla, Oak Over, US Club, the Ridge, Holly Lodge, Jakhu, Richmount, Ramchandra Chowk, Kamla Nehru Hospital and the High Court. Sector 5 covers the Himachal Pradesh Secretariat, Brockhurst, Mehli, Kasumpti, Panthaghati and Nav Bahar.Deputy Commissioner (DC) Anupam Kashyap, who is also chairman of the District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA), said this today while chairing a meeting with officials to review the administration’s winter preparedness.He told all departments concerned to ensure that no person, local or tourist, faced inconvenience during snowfall and to ensure a swift response to any emergency. He also urged all office heads and educational institutions in the district to conduct safety audits to prevent possible disasters.Several fire incidents had been reported in the district last year, the DC said, so a large-scale awareness campaign was needed to prevent such incidents.He directed all Sub-Divisional Magistrates (SDMs) to hold meetings in their areas, prepare contingency plans and coordinate with the Army, ITBP, NDRF, SDRF and ‘Aapda Mitras’ in their jurisdictions. He also asked all departments to prepare for the Winter Carnival to be held in Shimla from December 25 to 31.Kashyap said that the following routes should be restored on priority: Sanjauli to IGMC, the AIMSS hospital road, IGMC to the Cancer Hospital, KNH to Cart Road, Lok Bhavan to Oak Over, Holly Lodge to the Ridge, Richmount, US Club, Oak Over and the Secretariat, Boileauganj to Peterhoff to Chaura Maidan to AG Office, the Lift from the High Court to Oak Over to Chhota Shimla, Cart Road to Victory Tunnel to the Secretariat, Cart Road to Sanjauli via Victory Tunnel to Lakkar Bazaar, Kennedy Chowk to Annadale, Chhota Shimla to Kasumpti and Panthaghati, and Mehli to Shoghi via Tutikandi.

headline: Eight booked over ‘lapses’ in Jhajjar panchayat works
content: The police have registered an FIR against eight persons, including a village sarpanch, her husband, two contractors and four government officials, for their alleged involvement in financial irregularities and embezzlement of panchayat funds in Dujana village here.The case relates to two development projects undertaken during 2024-25 — construction of a boundary wall and tin shed at the village crematorium under the Shiv Dham Scheme and excavation and cleaning of Jhajhri Johad.According to a complaint filed by village panches Satya Parkash and Zorawar Singh Sharma, the crematorium project involved alleged excess billing of Rs 55,492. They claimed that the Junior Engineer had assessed the completed work at Rs 2,74,965, but an invoice of Rs 3,24,457 was generated by allegedly adding 18% GST again, resulting in excess payment.They alleged that inflated bills and duplicate GST claims were also made in connection with the excavation and cleaning of Jhajhri Johad, causing a loss of several lakhs of rupees to the panchayat.

headline: Rajbanshi language to be included in Eighth Schedule of Constitution: Suvendu Adhikari
content: Kolkata West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said that the Rajbanshi language will be included in the Eight Schedule of the Constitution, a promise that their party had made during their Assembly election campaign. During the inauguration of a festival in West Bengal’s Cooch Behar district, Mr Adhikari said that their government is taking complete care of the Rajbanshi community, including their language, culture, political aspirations, and financial security. BJP govt at Centre ‘deceived’ Rajbanshis by not delivering poll promises, says Abhishek Banerjee BJP govt at Centre ‘deceived’ Rajbanshis by not delivering poll promises, says Abhishek Banerjee TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee said the BJP at the Centre is yet to respond to the demand by the West Bengal government to recognise Rajbanshi language under the eighth schedule of the Constitution BJP govt at Centre ‘deceived’ Rajbanshis by not delivering poll promises, says Abhishek Banerjee storyline 1 He added that as promised in BJP’s West Bengal Assembly poll manifesto and reiterated by several top BJP leaders during the buildup to the elections, Rajbanshi language is set to be part of the Eight Schedule of the Constitution. “We raised the issue during a meeting with the Union home minister and the home secretary on November 19 that was attended by me and the state’s chief secretary,” Mr Adhikari told reporters before the inauguration of Ras Utsav (annual celebration of Radha-Krishna) festivities in Cooch Behar. WB govt made lot of efforts for classical language status to Bengali says Mamata WB govt made lot of efforts for classical language status to Bengali says Mamata WB CM took to social media and referred to the sacrifice made by ‘language martyrs’ of Bangladesh for Bengali language WB govt made lot of efforts for classical language status to Bengali says Mamata storyline 1 At Cooch Behar, Mr Adhikari was greeted by Cabinet minister Nisith Pramanik, a member of the Rajbanshi community. Later, the CM also took part in the festivities in the local area. Mr Adhikari also added that the Rajbanshi community expressed their dissatisfaction over losing their land ownership in the region as he held the Left Front government responsible for it. He also added that the previous governments in the State did not offer much participation of the Rajbanshi community in the cabinet and that their government has done more for the community since they came to power. The Rajbanshi community has always stood by us since 2019, Mr Adhikari added. In the recently concluded assembly polls, the BJP performed exceptionally well in north Bengal and won eight out of nine seats in the Cooch Behar district.

headline: Congress to stage protest outside Shahabad Sugar Mill on Dec 1
content: The Haryana Congress will stage a sit-in protest and strike outside the Shahabad Sugar Mill on December 1 in support of sugarcane farmers, Leader of Opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda said today.Addressing mediapersons after a meeting of the Congress Legislature Party (CLP) in Chandigarh, Hooda said the party would stand with farmers and intensify its agitation over their concerns.The CLP meeting was convened ahead of the one-day special session of the Haryana Legislative Assembly to mark Constitution Day. Congress state president Rao Narender Singh and party in-charge Sanjay Dutt were also present.Hooda said all Congress MLAs would attend the special session and raise issues concerning the state. He also announced that the Haryana Congress would organise a Constitution Protection March in Panchkula on November 26, in response to the nationwide call given by the Congress.The march will be held in Sector 26 and will witness participation by party leaders, workers and the public. Congress MLAs will also join the programme.Commenting on the political situation in Punjab, Hooda expressed confidence that the Congress would return to power in the state. He said the BJP-Akali Dal alliance would not influence the electoral outcome, claiming that voters had already given the Akali Dal, BJP and AAP opportunities to govern but remained disappointed with their performance.Meanwhile, a review meeting on development works was held at Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini’s residence in Chandigarh, with BJP MLAs and departmental secretaries in attendance.Four Congress-suspended MLAs — Jarnail Singh, Renu Bala, Shalley Chaudhary and Mohammad Israil — also attended the meeting. Chaudhary said the meeting concerned the implementation of the CM’s announcements.

headline: Governor bats for preservation of Himachal’s cultural heritage
content: Governor of Himachal Pradesh Kavinder Gupta on Wednesday underscored the need to preserve and promote the state’s centuries-old Dev Sanskriti and rich Sanatan traditions, describing them as the foundation of India’s spiritual strength, social harmony and cultural unity.Accompanied by Lady Governor Bindu Gupta, he visited the revered Shri Chhatrdhari Chalda Mahasu Maharaj temple at Pashmi village in the Shillai Assembly constituency of Sirmaur district and offered prayers for the peace, prosperity and well-being of the people of Himachal Pradesh and the country.Addressing devotees, Gupta said Shri Chhatrdhari Chalda Mahasu Maharaj, worshipped as a manifestation of Lord Shiva, symbolised truth, justice, righteousness and public welfare. He said the unique tradition of the deity travelling from village to village reflected collective faith, mutual respect and social cohesion.He observed that the shared Dev Sanskriti of Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand was a remarkable manifestation of India’s spiritual and cultural unity, transcending geographical boundaries and strengthening bonds of brotherhood and communal harmony.Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of “Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi”, the Governor said India was advancing rapidly on the path of modern development while simultaneously reclaiming and promoting its rich civilisational, cultural and spiritual heritage.He stressed that connecting the younger generation with Sanatan values, indigenous traditions and spiritual heritage was essential for building a morally strong and socially responsible society rooted in its cultural identity.Highlighting the potential of religious and spiritual tourism in Himachal Pradesh, Gupta said a sustainable approach to developing the sector could strengthen the rural economy, generate employment and self-employment opportunities for local youth, and give the state’s rich cultural heritage wider national and international recognition.He called upon people to work collectively towards building a drug-free, prosperous, culturally empowered and self-reliant Himachal Pradesh and contribute actively to realising the national vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.The Governor extended his greetings to the devotees and expressed hope that the blessings of Shri Chhatrdhari Chalda Mahasu Maharaj would continue to guide humanity.Industries Minister and Shillai MLA Harshwardhan Chauhan, former Shillai MLA Baldev Singh Tomar, Deputy Commissioner Priyanka Verma, Superintendent of Police Nishchint Singh Negi and other dignitaries were also present on the occasion.

headline: CM Saini to lead UK, Germany investment push
content: In a major push to attract global investment, Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini will lead a high-level delegation to the United Kingdom (UK) and Germany from November 28 to December 5 to explore opportunities for trade, industrial cooperation, education, skill development and artificial intelligence (AI).Industries and Commerce Minister Rao Narbir Singh and senior officials will accompany the CM. The delegation will hold meetings with global firms, investors, universities, research institutions and industry representatives to showcase Haryana as an attractive investment destination.During the UK leg, Saini will interact with business leaders, investors and a Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) delegation to discuss investment opportunities and industrial partnerships. He will also meet members of the Haryana diaspora and invite them to contribute to the state’s economic growth through investments.On November 30 and December 1, the Chief Minister is scheduled to hold one-to-one meetings with representatives of leading companies and educational institutions. Roundtable discussions will explore trade and investment opportunities under the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), with special focus on education, vocational training and skill development.His engagements will also include meetings with representatives of the Centre for Science and Policy at the University of Cambridge and Indian students at Oxford University. A visit to Queen Elizabeth’s School, Barnet, is planned to explore educational cooperation and the possibility of setting up an educational campus in Haryana.In Germany, a Haryana investment roadshow will be organised on December 2 to highlight the state’s industrial infrastructure, connectivity, skilled workforce and investor-friendly policies.On December 3, Saini will meet representatives of the Fraunhofer research and technology institution to discuss setting up a Centre of Excellence in Haryana. An MoU is also scheduled to be signed in this regard. The delegation will conclude its visit with meetings with leading German companies, industrialists and potential investors on December 4 and 5.Pilgrimage train to Varanasi to depart on Dec 15The Haryana Government will organise a free four-day pilgrimage to Varanasi for senior citizens under the Chief Minister Teerth Yatra Scheme from December 15.Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini will flag off a special train carrying the pilgrims. A portal has been opened to invite applications from eligible devotees. Senior citizens aged 60 and above will be eligible for the scheme.Registration is being carried out through the Antyodaya-SARAL portal at https://saralharyana.gov.in.‘Govt committed to creating equal opportunities for all’Kurukshetra: Saini said ensuring equal opportunities for every section of society and bringing the last person into the mainstream remained key priorities of his government. He was addressing a welcome ceremony for the Samrasta Sankalp Yatra at Umri here. The yatra is being organised to commemorate the 650th birth anniversary year of Guru Ravidas.

headline: US-based NRI honoured for his efforts to improve Amritsar’s international air connectivity
content: When a direct flight between London and Amritsar disappears from the aviation map, its impact is felt far beyond the airport terminal. For thousands of Punjabi families spread across continents, it means longer journeys, additional transit stops and higher travel costs. For Amritsar, it also means losing a vital link with one of its largest overseas communities.For Amritsar-born, US-based Sameep Singh Gumtala, this is precisely the kind of issue that demands sustained community advocacy. Rather than allowing the demand for better connectivity to remain a conversation among travellers, he has spent years helping take it to airlines, elected representatives and policy forums through the volunteer-led FlyAmritsar Initiative and the Amritsar Vikas Manch (AVM).His efforts recently received recognition in London, where SEVA Trust UK honoured him with the UK-India Impact Award during its 10th-anniversary celebrations held at the House of Commons recently. The award recognised his contribution to community support, charitable service and efforts to improve air connectivity to Amritsar.But the recognition comes with a renewed challenge. While direct Birmingham-Amritsar flights continue, the suspension of the London service has revived the campaign for a route that advocates say is important for Punjab’s diaspora, tourism and religious travel.Gumtala, who serves as Global Convener of FlyAmritsar and Overseas Secretary of Amritsar Vikas Manch AVM, has urged British MPs, particularly those representing constituencies with large Punjabi populations, to take up the issue and encourage airlines such as British Airways and Virgin Atlantic to explore direct flights to Amritsar.The campaign is built around a simple argument: Amritsar’s international connectivity should reflect its importance as a religious destination, a tourism centre and a gateway for a sizeable diaspora population. The demand extends beyond passengers from the city, with travellers from across Punjab and neighbouring regions relying on Amritsar airport for overseas journeys.Through FlyAmritsar and Gumtala has been involved in efforts to engage airlines, government representatives and community stakeholders to strengthen international connections from Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport. The campaign has mobilised support for routes and connectivity initiatives involving Birmingham, Kuala Lumpur and London, while continuing to push for better links with Canada, Europe, Australia and other destinations.The advocacy has also sought to move into political spaces where airline connectivity can be discussed. SEVA Trust UK, which has collaborated with FlyAmritsar on the UK-Amritsar connectivity issue, supported a campaign meeting at the Houses of Parliament in April 2018 to highlight the demand for a direct London route.The recent award ceremony, hosted and chaired by Bedford MP Mohammad Yasin, brought together parliamentarians, community leaders and volunteers from the UK, India and the US. Gumtala received the award from Smethwick MP Gurinder Singh Josan CBE, Professor Jagtar Singh CBE, Amritpal Singh Maan OBE and SEVA Trust UK founder and chairman Charan Kanwal Singh Sekhon MBE. Punjabi singer Channi Singh OBE was among others honoured for contributions to community service, education and culture.Gumtala described the recognition as an honour shared by the volunteers and community members who have worked to strengthen Amritsar’s international connectivity. He acknowledged SEVA Trust UK and the Punjabi community in Britain for their support of the campaign.

headline: Right to choose a partner is an aspect of constitutional freedom, not a privilege granted by a family, caste or community: Thirumavalavan
content: Chennai In his memorandum to Chairperson of Tamil Nadu Commission for the Prevention of Honour Killings, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi founder and Chidambaram MP, Thol. Thirumavalavan said, “the right to choose one’s partner is not a privilege granted by a family, caste or community” but “an aspect of the constitutional freedom and dignity of every individual”. In his request to the Commission headed by Justice K.N. Basha, Mr. Thirumavalavan said that the Commission should “recommend the enactment of a comprehensive Tamil Nadu law against honour killings and honour-based crimes, with a broad definition rooted in the right to choose a partner and individual autonomy”. He further urged the Commission to provide a framework to address “collective and mob-based honour violence”, which would ensure that “every person who intentionally participates in, instigates, facilitates or enables the crime can be held accountable under clearly defined standards of criminal responsibility”. The VCK leader further said that enforceable duties and penalties should be imposed on police and public officials who fail to protect couples despite credible threats, including wilful refusal to register complaints, disclosure of confidential information and dereliction of preventive duties. Mr. Thirumavalavan also demanded that there exist comprehensive protection for couples, survivors, witnesses and their families, including safehouses, relocation, legal aid, counselling, medical care, compensation and rehabilitation. He also appealed to the Commission to submit “a draft Bill and a time-bound implementation framework to the Government of Tamil Nadu, with budgetary allocations, monitoring arrangements and annual reporting to the Legislature”.

headline: Himachal’s Nauni varsity to set up digital horticulture hub
content: The Dr YS Parmar University of Horticulture and Forestry (UHF), Nauni, is set to collaborate with ITI Limited, a Government of India public sector enterprise, to establish a Centre of Excellence in Digital Horticulture and Drone Technology at an estimated cost of Rs 350 crore.The memorandum of understanding (MoU) between the two institutions will be signed on December 1, coinciding with the university’s Foundation Day.The proposed centre will focus on integrating emerging technologies into horticulture, with facilities for precision farming, drone-based crop monitoring, digital advisory services for farmers, pesticide residue testing and digital tracking of produce from farms to markets. Apple, pomegranate and other major horticultural crops of Himachal Pradesh will be covered in the initial phase.Under the first phase, ITI Limited will mobilise the required financial resources and provide equipment, infrastructure, technical manpower and operational support for establishing the facilities at the university.Vice-Chancellor HS Baweja said the collaboration would provide an institutional platform for advancing precision horticulture, digital innovation, technology demonstration and skill development. He said the initiative would strengthen the university’s research and technological capabilities while helping make Himachal’s horticulture sector more competitive, sustainable and technology-driven.Director of Research Devina Vaidya said the partnership would facilitate research and the transfer of emerging technologies to farmers. Facilities for drone-based agriculture, data analysis, pesticide residue testing and digital traceability would benefit scientists, students, farmers and entrepreneurs, she added.

headline: NSS volunteers hold cleanliness campaign at 11,965-ft Churdhar in Himachal
content: At an altitude of 11,965 ft, National Service Scheme (NSS) volunteers of Government Senior Secondary School, Sarain, undertook a cleanliness drive at Churdhar, the highest peak in Sirmaur district. They collected plastic waste and other discarded material along the pedestrian route leading to the revered Churdhar Temple.The initiative was part of a seven-day special NSS camp held from November 18 to 24, during which the volunteers focused on environmental conservation, cleanliness and creating awareness against drug abuse.The volunteers collected plastic waste scattered along the trekking route, which witnesses a massive influx of devotees every year. Lakhs of pilgrims undertake the arduous uphill journey to pay obeisance at the Churdhar Temple, making responsible waste disposal essential to protecting the fragile mountain ecosystem.The cleanliness drive highlighted the need to protect Churdhar’s pristine surroundings from the growing threat of plastic pollution. The volunteers also sought to sensitise pilgrims and local stakeholders about maintaining cleanliness along the religious pilgrimage route and preventing waste from entering the surrounding forests and natural habitats.The seven-day camp also featured interactions with officials, educationists, religious figures and members of the local community. They shared their experiences and encouraged the students to contribute to environmental protection and social welfare.At the concluding ceremony, Agriculture Development Officer, Chopal, Kanwar Singh, appreciated the efforts of the volunteers and programme officer Lalit Kumar Himta. He particularly lauded their initiatives in environmental conservation, sanitation and creating awareness against drug abuse, including the menace of chitta. He said such efforts had helped the school earn recognition beyond the state.School Principal Pratap Singh Negi thanked the guests, local residents and all those who had contributed to the successful conduct of the camp.

headline: Haryana: 20 yrs on, NDRI’s high-yielding goats ready for national recognition
content: Nearly two decades after developing two high-yielding synthetic goat breeds, scientists at the ICAR-National Dairy Research Institute (NDRI), Karnal, have standardised them and are now preparing to seek their national registration. The move is expected to give the breeds wider recognition, facilitate their inclusion in state breeding programmes and help farmers access improved milch goats.The two breeds were developed in 2006 by crossing Punjab’s indigenous Beetal goat with Saanen goats from Switzerland and Alpine goats from North America. The achievement followed decades of research that began in 1971, involving multiple breeding experiments and evaluations across generations.NDRI Director Dr Dheer Singh said the institute had initiated goat-breeding research with the objective of developing superior milch goats for the country. After years of experimentation, scientists succeeded in developing the two crossbred varieties in 2006.A goat developed by crossing Saanen and Beetal breeds.Both breeds have demonstrated a milk yield of around 400-450 litres during a lactation period of approximately 150 days, considerably higher than the 150-170 litres generally produced by indigenous goats, he said.“Goat milk has considerable nutritional and health benefits and also offers opportunities for livestock-based entrepreneurship. The registration of these improved breeds will provide them national recognition and make them accessible to farmers across the country,” Dr Singh said.A team led by Dr Vikas Vohra, Head of the Animal Breeding Department, along with Principal Scientists Dr Nitin Tyagi, Dr Gopal Gowani and Dr TV Raja, senior scientist Dr Rani and other researchers, worked on standardising the breeds and evaluating their performance.Dr Vohra said the institute had conducted research at its campus and on farms over the past 20 years to assess the goats’ milk-producing potential under different conditions. Breeding bucks and goats were also provided to progressive farmers to evaluate their adaptability and performance.He said the improved breeds could fetch farmers an additional benefit of up to Rs 7,000 per goat, owing to their higher milk production and prolific breeding capacity.The institute will showcase the two breeds at its three-day National Dairy Mela, scheduled to be held on its campus from November 26 to 28, to familiarise farmers with their potential.NDRI has earlier developed the synthetic Karan Fries cattle breed, which was registered decades after its development and standardisation.

headline: Dharampur MLA calls off protest on highway safety
content: Dharampur MLA Chander Shekhar on Wednesday called off his dharna at Kumharada in Mandi district after the Project Director of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) assured him that necessary measures would be taken to address concerns over highway construction and the safety of residential and commercial properties along the Hamirpur-Mandi highway via Dharampur and Sarkaghat.The MLA had staged the protest on Tuesday at Same Ka Tharu village in Kumharada panchayat, alongside a family whose house was reportedly affected by National Highway construction work. Alleging negligence by construction companies and a lack of accountability among officials, he had given the authorities a 24-hour ultimatum to submit a detailed report on action taken at vulnerable locations along the highway.On Wednesday, Mandi Deputy Commissioner Apoorv Devgan, the MoRTH Project Director and other officials reached the protest site and held discussions with the MLA. Following assurances from the Project Director, Chander Shekhar decided to withdraw his protest.The MLA had demanded that officials and representatives of the construction company personally inspect all identified vulnerable locations instead of limiting the exercise to office-level discussions. He also sought a comprehensive report, backed by documents and records, detailing the safeguards implemented and the proposed measures to address risks to residents.A key demand concerned the 187 vulnerable locations identified along the Avahdevi-Sinhan stretch during a meeting held at the district headquarters on December 25, 2025. The meeting was attended by the district administration, MLAs from Mandi, Sarkaghat and Dharampur, and officials of the National Highway authorities and MoRTH. Chander Shekhar sought details of the action taken over the past year and a clear plan for addressing the identified risks.He also raised concerns over houses and commercial establishments situated outside the Right of Way (ROW) boundary, alleging that several properties remained exposed to construction-related risks despite falling outside the designated corridor.

headline: Kallakurichi TVK MLA Arul Vignesh summoned for questioning in harassment case
content: KALLAKURICHI The Kallakurichi All Women Police on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) served summons on Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh directing him to appear for questioning in connection with a harassment case registered against him on a complaint lodged by a woman IAS officer. Inspector Bhuvaneshwari attached to the All Women Police station visited the MLA’s house in Kallakurichi and handed the summons to him in person. The police also questioned Arul Vignesh at the house. The woman IAS officer had submitted a formal complaint to the Kallakurichi district Superintendent of Police on Monday (November 23), accusing the MLA of making inappropriate advances and sending unwarranted messages. The police have booked a case against the MLA invoking provisions of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and Sections 75, 78 and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Police sources said that Tiruppur Superintendent of Police Shristi Singh, who has been appointed as the Investigating Officer in the criminal case, began preliminary investigation into the incident on Wednesday after receiving the inquiry report from Kallakurichi Superintendent of Police I. Shahnaz at the All Women Police Station. Inspector General of Police (Administration) N. Kamini has been appointed to supervise the investigation. The National Commission for Women had earlier taken suo moto cognisance of the allegations and asked the Tamil Nadu Director General of Police to conduct an impartial inquiry. In the morning, more than 30 Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) activists were arrested when they attempted to lay siege to the office of Kallakurichi TVK MLA, demanding his resignation over the allegations against him. The protesters raised slogans alleging lack of safety for women. The DMK’s women wing also staged a demonstration at the Four Roads junction in Kallakurichi demanding the arrest of the MLA. They burnt the effigy of the MLA and raised slogans against him. Meanwhile, police personnel have been deployed in strength at the MLA’s office in Kallakurichi.

headline: Sukhraj Randhawa appointed honorary member of Punjab State Commission  for NRIs
content: Sukhraj Singh Randhawa, an Australia-based Non-Resident Indian (NRI), has been appointed as an honorary member of the Punjab State Commission for NRIs.He is a member of the AAP and has been working towards increasing the party’s outreach in Australia and New Zealand. The body protects the rights of NRIs and Overseas Citizens of India (OCI).Sukhraj recently returned from Australia to solve the problems of NRIs. He originally belongs to Amritsar.The Commission exercises the powers to summon witnesses, examine evidence under oath, requisition public records and seek status reports from district administrations and police departments. The body also recommends administrative and police action against erring local officials.“I have been regularly supporting Indian students living in Australia. Since 2009, I have been helping newly arrived Indian students settle down in Australia by guiding them on legal matters, documentation and job opportunities. My main aim is to strengthen the bond between the Punjabi diaspora and Punjab,” he says.Randhawa has built a wide network of NRIs and has continuously supported them.

headline: Haryana: Charuni, Tikait factions of BKU unite for protest over cane price
content: The Bharatiya Kisan Union (Charuni) and the BKU (Tikait) have joined hands to demand an increase in sugarcane prices to Rs 600 per quintal in Haryana.Leaders of the BKU (Tikait) lifted their dharna outside the residence of Haryana Agriculture Minister Shyam Singh Rana in Radaur, Yamunanagar district, and extended support to the protest organised by the BKU (Charuni) at the cane yard of the Saraswati Sugar Mill here.The BKU (Charuni) has been holding an indefinite dharna at the mill’s cane yard since November 15, while the BKU (Tikait) had been protesting outside the minister’s residence since November 21.District president of the Charuni faction, Sanju Gundiana, said both unions would now gherao the residence of Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini in Kurukshetra on December 2. Earlier, the agitation had been planned by the BKU (Tikait) alone.Gundiana said both farmer organisations had started preparations at the district, tehsil and village levels to ensure the success of the proposed agitation.“All farmers’ organisations in the state have come together to form the Haryana Sanjha Sangharsh Morcha to lead the agitation over sugarcane prices. Now, representatives of all farmers’ organisations will gather in Kurukshetra to gherao the Haryana Chief Minister’s residence on December 2,” Gundiana said.Farmers have been demanding an increase in the sugarcane price to Rs 600 per quintal.The Haryana Government has increased the State Advised Price (SAP) of sugarcane by Rs 15 per quintal for the 2026-27 crushing season, raising it from Rs 415 to Rs 430 per quintal.They had also threatened to prevent sugar mills in the state from starting crushing operations if their demand was not met. The inauguration of the 43rd crushing season at the Shahabad Cooperative Sugar Mill on Tuesday had turned into a show of protest, with agitating farmers confronting the police, opposing the virtual participation of a BJP minister and reiterating their demand for a higher sugarcane price.

headline: Lost minutes: 44% snakebite patients visit faith healers before hospitals in Himachal
content: A five-year study of snakebite patients at Civil Hospital, Nurpur, has exposed gaps in emergency response and treatment-seeking behaviour in Kangra district. It found that nearly 44 per cent of the patients whose health-seeking history was documented had visited a faith healer or temple before reaching the hospital. All 13 patients recorded as arriving more than six hours after a bite were either brought dead or died shortly after arrival.The research article, titled “Pre-Hospital Delay Due to Faith Healers, Consultation Had Adverse Impact on Outcomes in Snakebite Patients”, analysed 222 cases treated at the hospital between January 2021 and December 2025. It was published in 2026 in the International Journal of Preventive, Curative and Community Medicine. The study recorded 16 deaths, a crude case fatality ratio of 7.2 per cent. Its findings raise questions about reliance on traditional healing, and also about ambulance availability, referral arrangements and the quality of hospital records in remote hill areas.The study was conducted under the Snakebite Awareness, Response, Prevention and Action (SARPA) project of the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) by a seven-member team led by Dr Nikunj Kankodia, Project Technical Support, SARPA. Of the 103 patients whose health-seeking behaviour was documented, 45 (43.7 per cent) had consulted a faith healer or visited a temple before reaching the hospital, with delays of one to seven hours recorded in some cases. Many patients sought prayers or rituals instead of medical care. Tourniquet use was documented in six cases, and one patient reportedly received herbal treatment.The paper, a copy of which is with The Tribune, also describes a local practice of applying a mixture of sacred soil and temple water to the bitten part and giving it orally. It notes that strong community faith in such treatment, coupled with doubts about hospital care, can shape a patient’s first response to a snakebite. The researchers, however, acknowledge that the study was retrospective and that the records do not establish that visits to faith healers directly caused the deaths.The delay figures are a concern. Among 106 patients whose time of arrival was recorded, 19 reached the hospital within an hour, 54 in one to three hours, 20 in three to six hours and 13 after more than six hours. All 13 in the last group were dead on arrival or died shortly after treatment began. No deaths were recorded in the one-to-three-hour group. Admission-time data were unavailable for 116 patients, which limits a complete assessment.Another finding is the geographical concentration of deaths. Eight of the 16 deceased (50 per cent) came from villages around the Pong Dam reservoir in the Nurpur, Fatehpur and Jawali blocks. Dr Kankodia said this belt had been identified as a potential ecological mortality hotspot, and recommended focused surveillance and awareness campaigns in the adjoining villages.The study found that 82.4 per cent of cases occurred in the monsoon months, when farm work, flooding and changes in snake habitats can raise human exposure. Lower limbs were the most common bite site, at 52.3 per cent. Among the 49 cases in which the snake species was identified, Russell’s viper accounted for 33.The study also points to a gap in emergency transport. Ambulances were used in only 11 cases, about five per cent of the total.Health-seeking behaviour was recorded for only 103 of the 222 patients, and the time taken to reach the hospital was unavailable for more than half. “Such missing information makes it difficult to establish the full extent of treatment delays and their contribution to poor outcomes,” Dr Kankodia said. The researchers have recommended community awareness programmes, particularly for farm workers in the buffer villages of Pong Dam, systematic recording of pre-hospital delays and stronger emergency referral arrangements.

headline: Hours after woman’s death, two shooters held in encounter
content: The police have arrested two alleged shooters, identified as Harmanpreet Singh, alias Rapper, of Kot Khalsa area and Jagroop Singh of Guru Nanak Wada, after an exchange of fire in connection with the murder of Dalbir Kaur, who was killed in a firing incident in which another man, Simranjit Singh, was injured. The incident had occurred in the Guru Ki Wadali area falling under the Chheharta police station here.Sharing the details, Police Commissioner Harmanbir Singh Gill said that Dalbir Kaur was caught in the line of fire when the assailants allegedly opened fire on Simranjit. A gunshot fired at him reportedly hit him before striking the deceased in the chest. She was rushed to a hospital but later succumbed to her injuries.A massive hunt was launched, with several police teams, led by SHO Balwinder Singh under the supervision of Jaskiran Singh Teja, Deputy Commissioner of Police (city), pressed into service to trace the assailants.During the operation, the police intercepted the two suspects. However, they allegedly opened fire at the police party, triggering an exchange of gunfire. The suspects fired three rounds, while the police retaliated with five rounds. Both Harmanpreet and Jagroop sustained injuries and were taken to the Civil Hospital.The police recovered a 9mm pistol from the spot, besides two live cartridges and three empty cartridges.Preliminary investigation suggests that the accused were allegedly working for gangster Ankush Baman, who had reportedly assigned them a contract to eliminate another person and given Rs 20,000 for the same.He said the firing at Simranjit was linked to an earlier enmity over the removal of the turban of Harmanpreet by Simranjit.The police are now tracking Ankush Baman, who is reportedly operating from outside the country. His associates and relatives will also be questioned to establish the wider conspiracy and identify others involved in the crime.The police said further arrests would be made if the involvement of other persons emerged during the investigation.

headline: Choose careers according to your strengths: Dharmani to students in Himachal
content: Technical Education Minister Rajesh Dharmani said every student had immense potential and that identifying their interests, capabilities and talents was essential to achieving success. He was addressing students at the annual prize distribution function of Government Senior Secondary School, Dangar, in the Ghumarwin Assembly constituency of Bilaspur district today.He advised students to choose their future paths according to their individual strengths rather than follow others or succumb to social pressure. He encouraged them to move forward with consistent hard work, patience and dedication to achieve their goals.The minister urged teachers to recognise that their responsibility extended beyond completing the syllabus or teaching from textbooks. They had an important role in bringing about positive changes in every student’s life, he said. He added that teachers should make efforts to understand each student’s interests, capabilities, strengths and weaknesses and provide individual guidance accordingly.He also stressed the need to provide better educational infrastructure. He announced that Rs 30 lakh would be released soon to complete the construction of the school’s unfinished building, which would help provide students with a better academic environment. Dharmani said basic infrastructure in Gram Panchayat Dangar was being strengthened through development projects worth more than Rs 5.17 crore. These included projects related to roads, education, healthcare, drinking water, electricity and community facilities.He said Rs 105.59 lakh had been spent on the construction of infrastructure at Government Senior Secondary School, Chokhna, Rs 22 lakh on improvements to the building of Government Sanskrit College, Dangar, and Rs 7.50 lakh on the construction of a football stadium and playground at Government Primary School, Dakhyut.Dharmani gave away prizes to students for their achievements in various fields, including academics, sports and extracurricular activities.

headline: Sukhbir calls pact ‘lokan da gathbandhan’, predicts ruling AAP tally below 10
content: A day after the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the BJP revived their alliance in Punjab, SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal on Wednesday described the tie-up as a people’s alliance, calling it “lokan da gathbandhan”.Addressing traders and industrialists at Raman Mandi, Bhucho Mandi and Bathinda city under his “Vision Sukhbir Da” programme, Sukhbir expressed confidence in the alliance’s electoral prospects and targeted the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and the Congress.Photographs of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and former Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal featured on the stages at the Bathinda city venues. BJP district urban president Sarup Chand Singla and other BJP leaders shared the platform with SAD leaders.Interacting with mediapersons, Sukhbir took a dig at former Punjab Congress president Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, claiming that his “Insaaf March” was aimed at seeking justice for himself after his removal from the party president’s post.Targeting the AAP, he claimed its leaders would face public anger in their respective constituencies and that the party would be reduced to fewer than 10 seats in the upcoming Assembly elections.“Why are they not saying ‘Ek hor mauka Kejriwal nu’ (one more chance to Kejriwal), as they did during the previous Assembly elections? Why does he not write ‘Give us one more chance’ on the posters now?” Sukhbir said.Responding to remarks by former CM Charanjit Singh Channi, Sukhbir alleged the Congress had no moral right to question other parties, holding it responsible for the attack on Darbar Sahib and the killing of a large number of Sikhs.During his interactions with traders and industrialists, some participants referred to Sukhbir as the future CM. When traders expressed hope for a “double-engine government”, he responded that Punjab would have a “double jet engine government”.Sukhbir promised to develop the Talwandi Sabo-Bhucho Mandi belt into a textile and spinning hub and said Bathinda would also emerge as a textile hub. He claimed the Jamnagar highway project had been approved due to his efforts and said an SAD-BJP government would focus on food processing.

headline: Sirsa panchayat accounts lose Rs 1.74 crore;  reports sought
content: Around Rs 1.74 crore has been withdrawn from the bank accounts of two panchayat samitis and five gram panchayats in Sirsa district, affecting routine transactions and potentially delaying payments for development works.The withdrawals include Rs 1.11 crore from the Sirsa Panchayat Samiti account and Rs 29.51 lakh from the Rania Panchayat Samiti account.Five gram panchayats have also reported withdrawals totalling Rs 33.11 lakh.District Development and Panchayat Officer Anoop Singh said reports had been received from around six gram panchayats and two panchayat samitis. The matter had been brought to the notice of the headquarters, and the department had sought reports to ascertain how the money was withdrawn and whether the transactions were authorised. Further action will follow the investigation.

headline: Himachal Pradesh Agricultural University pensioners await Rs120-cr retirement dues
content: Retirement has become a period of financial uncertainty for former employees of CSK Himachal Pradesh Agricultural University (HPAU), with outstanding pension benefits and other dues mounting to nearly Rs 120 crore. The HP Agriculture University Pensioners’ Sabha has urged the state government to provide special financial assistance to the university to clear these long-pending liabilities.Addressing a press conference here, Dr SP Sharma, president of the Sabha, said employees who had devoted their entire working lives to the university were being forced to struggle for their legitimate dues even after retirement.He said routine medical reimbursement claims had not been cleared since December 2022, causing hardship to retired employees, including those suffering from serious ailments. Citing the case of a pensioner who undergoes dialysis twice a week at a monthly cost of around Rs 16,000, he said even critical medical claims remained unsettled.Dr Sharma said lifetime pension arrears amounting to Rs 41.45 lakh had remained unpaid since 2018. Outstanding liabilities towards pension allowance and its arrears stood at approximately Rs 1.47 crore and Rs 1.50 crore, respectively.Payments against leave encashment had also been pending since February 2022, despite directions from the Himachal Pradesh High Court to clear the dues with six per cent interest. Execution petitions had subsequently been filed before the court.The Sabha also raised the issue of pending pay revision benefits, revision of pensions of teachers who retired before January 1, 2016, in accordance with UGC guidelines, and pension commutation dues outstanding since March 2022.Highlighting the university’s financial constraints, Dr Sharma said its annual expenditure on salaries and pensions was around Rs 158 crore, against a government grant-in-aid of Rs 122 crore, leaving an annual deficit of nearly Rs 36 crore.He said the Sabha had approached Governor-cum-Chancellor of the university Kavinder Gupta, Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu and MP Anurag Sharma, seeking their intervention. The pensioners’ body appealed to the government to release additional funds, clear retirement benefits on priority and implement court orders without further delay.Dr Sharma said pensioners deserved dignity and financial security after decades of service to the university. Dr Hirday Paul Singh, JP Thakur, Sant Kumar, Suman Thakur and Manohar Lal were also present.

headline: Red maize dominates govt procurement in Chamba, Himachal
content: Government procurement of naturally grown maize in Chamba district has reached 337.24 quintals, with 112 farmers selling their produce at the state-fixed minimum support price of Rs 5,000 per quintal. Red maize accounts for the bulk of the procurement at 301.195 quintals, while the remaining 36.045 quintals comprise white maize.The procurement drive is being conducted at designated centres in Chamba, Tissa, Salooni, Bharmour, Chowari and Banikhet. Farmers are being paid Rs 50 per kg for their produce, following the state government’s decision to increase the support price from Rs 40 per kg this year.Tissa has emerged as the largest contributor, with 24 farmers selling 161.69 quintals of maize. In Chamba block, 38 farmers have supplied 51.11 quintals, while 19 farmers in Salooni have sold 60.67 quintals.In Bhattiyat, 25 farmers have sold 42.92 quintals, while six farmers in Bharmour have supplied 20.85 quintals. Interestingly, all the maize procured in Bharmour is white maize, making the block the largest contributor to white maize procurement in the district.Two procurement centres have been established in Bhattiyat, at Chowari and Banikhet. The remaining development blocks have one procurement centre each at their respective headquarters.Nitin Sharma, Project Director of the Agriculture Technology Management Agency (ATMA), Chamba, said procurement would continue at the designated centres till November 30, 2026. He clarified that the government was purchasing only maize grown from traditional seeds.The state government has also fixed support prices for other naturally grown crops. Barley in the tribal subdivision of Pangi and wheat will fetch Rs 80 per kg, ginger Rs 40 per kg and raw turmeric Rs 150 per kg.The enhanced support price is aimed at encouraging farmers to adopt natural farming by assuring them remunerative returns for their traditional produce.

headline: Claimants galore, Cong faces ticket dilemma in Amritsar
content: With the Congress yet to convene its selection committee meeting for the 2027 Assembly elections, the party faces a tough task of finalising candidates for five urban constituencies in Amritsar. With multiple leaders staking claim to tickets, particularly in the urban constituencies of Amritsar (North, East and West), the exercise is likely to trigger factionalism and infighting within the party.In Amritsar North, at least four prominent leaders are in the race. These include former Punjab Cabinet Minister Anil Joshi, who represented the constituency twice during the SAD-BJP regime, in 2007 and 2012, and former MLA Sunil Datti, who won the seat in 2017. Congress councillor Rajkanwal Preet Pal Singh Lucky and former District Urban Congress president Ashwani Pappu are also aspiring for the ticket.The constituency is currently represented by the BJP’s Kunwar Vijay Partap Singh, who won on an AAP ticket in 2022. The former IPS officer was suspended by the AAP for five years over alleged anti-party activities and recently joined the BJP.A Hindu-dominated constituency, Amritsar North has traditionally been a Congress stronghold, with the party winning it around six times, followed by the BJP.Amritsar East, currently represented by AAP MLA Jeevan Jyot Kaur, has several Congress aspirants. Former MP Jasbir Singh Dimpa, who is also the party’s constituency in-charge, is among the contenders. Dinesh Bassi, a former chairman of the Amritsar Improvement Trust, who has been seeking the ticket for several years, is another aspirant. He has remained active in the area and regularly raised issues concerning residents.Senior Congress leader Mamta Datta, former president of the Punjab Mahila Congress and former chairperson of the Punjab Khadi and Village Industries Board, is also in the race. She has been holding ward-level meetings and organising voter-list campaigns to consolidate her support.Interestingly, Dr Navjot Kaur Sidhu, who was suspended by the Congress, has also been holding meetings in different parts of the constituency.The seat had witnessed a high-profile contest in the 2022 Assembly elections when Jeevan Jyot Kaur defeated Congress leader Navjot Singh Sidhu and SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia.In Amritsar West, senior Congress leader Raj Kumar Verka remains a prominent face, but he is not the only aspirant. Babbi Pehalwan and former Senior Deputy Mayor Yonus Masih are also seeking the party ticket.Once a prominent industrial constituency and a stronghold of the Left, Amritsar West gradually shifted towards the Congress as the communists lost ground. The Congress has won the seat five times. Former Deputy Chief Minister Om Parkash Soni also represented it twice as an Independent before joining the Congress.In the 2022 elections, AAP candidate Dr Jasbir Singh Sandhu defeated Verka, a former MLA and Cabinet Minister, by a substantial margin. Verka had represented the constituency twice.In Amritsar South, currently represented by AAP MLA Dr Inderbir Singh Nijjar, former three-time MLA Inderbir Singh Bolaria is among the prominent Congress aspirants. Bolaria won the seat twice during the SAD-BJP regime and once on a Congress ticket.
