Rinku Narula, who is also believed to have considerable influence in the constituency, is another contender.The Congress and the SAD have won the Amritsar South seat four times each.In Amritsar Central constituency, former Deputy Chief Minister Om Parkash Soni also remains a prominent Congress face in the area and is considered a strong contender.In Ajnala, the contest for the Congress ticket is likely to be between former two-time MLA Harpartap Singh Ajnala and Sukh Ajnala, brother of Amritsar MP Gurjeet Singh Aujla.Recently, when Punjab Congress in-charge Sachin Pilot visited the city and met senior party leaders, the party showed a united face. Nevertheless, ticket aspirants from various constituencies also present there and met him to present their case.With several leaders already making efforts to strengthen their claims, the party high command will have to tread carefully while selecting candidates, said a senior Congress leader wishing not to be named. Apart from assessing electoral prospects, the party will also have to ensure that ticket aspirants who miss out do not turn into rebels and damage its prospects in the forthcoming Assembly elections, he pointed out.

headline: Rohtak varsity bags award for excellence in public relations
content: Maharshi Dayanand University (MDU) has been conferred ‘Best Public Sector Organisation Implementing PR’ award at the 10th National Media Conclave-2026, held in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. The university’s Director Public Relations Sunit Mukherjee received the award, comprising a trophy and certificate of appreciation, on behalf of the university.Vice-Chancellor Prof Milap Punia said effective public relations were integral to building an institution’s reputation and strengthening its connect with society. “The award is a recognition of MDU’s collective efforts to promote academic excellence, institutional achievements and a positive university image. Transparent communication and meaningful engagement with the media are essential for enhancing public trust in higher education institutions,” he added.Dean Academic Affairs Prof Randeep Rana said the honour reflected the university’s efforts to ensure that its academic and research accomplishments received wider public recognition.

headline: Jagadhri Civil Hospital soon to get AIIMS-backed de-addiction centre
content: In a significant step towards strengthening healthcare facilities for people struggling with drug addiction, a de-addiction treatment centre is set to be started at the Subdivisional Civil Hospital in Jagadhri. Following the successful operation of a similar centre at Mukand Lal District Civil Hospital in Yamunanagar, preparations are now underway to extend the facility to Jagadhri, providing patients with access to better treatment closer to their homes.The proposed Addiction Treatment Facility (ATF) will offer medical treatment, counselling and rehabilitation-related support to people suffering from substance addiction. Patients will be treated under the supervision of experienced doctors and specialists while the functioning of the centre will be monitored by the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS). The maintenance expenses of the centre will also be borne by AIIMS.At present, a 20-bed ATF centre is operational at Mukand Lal District Civil Hospital in Yamunanagar. The facility is witnessing a considerable number of patients seeking treatment for drug addiction. According to information, the centre’s beds generally remain occupied, indicating the growing demand for de-addiction services in the district. Apart from the treatment facility, separate outpatient department (OPD) services are also being provided for people suffering from mental health problems and those struggling with substance addiction in the ATF of Yamunanagar. The patients requiring admission are also being provided treatment at the hospital. About 4,000 patients have so far received treatment through the OPD services at this district hospital’s mental health and de-addiction facilities. Of these about 30 per cent have reportedly given up their addiction, while about 50 per cent have stopped consuming alcohol. These figures reflect the positive impact of medical intervention, counselling and continuous follow up in helping patients overcome addiction.The increasing number of people approaching treatment facilities has also encouraged the Health Department to expand the services to Jagadhri. The availability of an ATF centre in Jagadhri is expected to benefit the residents of Jagadhri and surrounding rural areas, who otherwise have to travel to Yamunanagar for specialised treatment.The number of people affected by drug addiction is a growing concern in Yamunanagar district. In coordination with the Police Department and other agencies concerned, information about people suffering from addiction was collected and compiled. During this exercise, nearly 1,000 drug addicts were identified in the district. However, the officials of the Health Department believe that the actual number could be higher. The identification of such a large number of people has highlighted the need for accessible treatment facilities, awareness campaigns and counselling services. The proposed centre at Jagadhri is expected to strengthen the district’s efforts to tackle the problem through medical intervention rather than limiting the approach to enforcement measures alone.“To ensure that the new centre functions effectively from the beginning, four doctors have been provided specialised training. Psychiatric specialists Priya, Ajit, Lavisha and Raksha have received training to treat patients suffering from addiction-related problems. The Health Department has already initiated the process in coordination with AIIMS,” said Officiating Civil Surgeon Dr Divya Mangla.She said preparations were underway to start the ATF facility in Jagadhri. “The department has contacted AIIMS and initiated the necessary formalities. The doctors are also available for the centre, and they have been given separate training to handle patients requiring de-addiction treatment,” said Dr Divya Mangla.

headline: 7,950 NDPS cases filed in four years: CM Sukhu
content: In a crackdown against drug trafficking, 7,950 NDPS cases were filed and illegal assets worth around Rs 92 crore have been seized in Himachal over the past four years.Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Tuesday said that the battle against drugs could not be won through the efforts of the government or the police alone, as active participation of every section of society was essential. A total of 12,302 accused persons had been arrested and large quantities of narcotic substances, including 1,384 kg of charas and 59 kg of chitta, had been seized, he added.He said that since the implementation of the PIT-NDPS Act in 2023, a total of 225 drug traffickers had been detained, including 159 in 2026 alone. Himachal Pradesh ranked second in the country in terms of preventive detention under this Act, he added.Sukhu said that 86 properties involving encroachments and illegal constructions on government land by persons accused under the NDPS Act had been identified and the demolition and eviction proceedings had been completed against 22.Over the past three and a half years, the state government had seized assets worth around Rs 92 crore acquired through drug trafficking. For the first time in the state, property worth Rs 48 lakh, acquired through ill-gotten drug money, had been transferred in the name of the government, he added.Sukhu appealed to the youth, ‘mahila mandals’, ‘yuvak mandals’, teachers, parents, voluntary organisations and the public to transform the anti-chitta campaign into a mass movement.TheCM said the state government was committed to making Himachal a drug-free, safe and prosperous state.Sukhu said that walkathons were being organised in various districts and students, teachers, ‘mahila mandals’, ‘yuvak mandals’ and citizens were enthusiastically participating in them. A total of 246 highly drug-affected panchayats had been identified and placed under special monitoring, he added.

headline: Himachal’s MLA Kewal Singh Pathania backs move for HC bench in Dharamsala
content: Shahpur MLA Kewal Singh Pathania has welcomed the state government’s proposal to establish a permanent bench of the Himachal Pradesh High Court in Dharamsala, describing it as a historic decision that would make justice more accessible to people in lower Himachal.Pathania said Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu had taken several far-reaching decisions aimed at ensuring balanced regional development and public welfare. He said the proposal, passed by the Himachal Pradesh Assembly during the winter session, would particularly benefit residents of Kangra, Chamba, Hamirpur, Una, Mandi and Kullu districts, who currently have to travel to Shimla for judicial proceedings.The establishment of a permanent bench in Dharamsala would save litigants considerable time and travel expenses, besides making access to justice more convenient, he said. He added that the move reflected the government’s commitment to ensuring regional balance and bringing public facilities closer to people’s homes.Pathania also highlighted various projects being undertaken in line with the government’s vision of developing Kangra as the state’s tourism capital. These include the expansion of Kangra airport, which would improve air connectivity, boost tourism and create new employment opportunities in the region.He further said the Rs 619-crore Durgesh Aranya International Zoological Park was being developed at Bankhandi in the Dehra subdivision. The project is expected to emerge as a major tourist attraction while promoting wildlife conservation and environmental awareness.Another major initiative, he said, was the Rs 300-crore modern milk processing plant coming up at Dagwar in Kangra. The facility would initially process 1.5 lakh litres of milk daily, with the capacity to be increased to three lakh litres. It would benefit thousands of milk producers and livestock farmers in Kangra and neighbouring districts.

headline: Abrego Garcia Can ‘Breathe Freely’ After He Arrives in Spain
content: (Bloomberg) -- Kilmar Abrego Garcia, the Salvadoran man deported to a notorious prison in El Salvador in what US officials called an “administrative error,” said he “can breathe freely” after arriving to Spain.“Today we celebrate because I not only feel victorious and we won the fight,” Abrego Garcia said at press conference Wednesday. “This time because I’m leaving with my freedom, not like before when they took me out inhumanely.”Abrego Garcia’s battle was one of several high-profile legal disputes over the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown. He was mistakenly deported last year to CECOT, a notorious Salvadoran mega-prison, only to be brought back to face criminal charges after the US Supreme Court ordered the government to facilitate his return to the US.He arrived in Madrid Wednesday after the 18-month legal battle where the government had sought to deport him to African countries, including Liberia. He had also faced a US human smuggling prosecution until a US judge in May dismissed the charges, concluding the government brought the case in retaliation for his fight against deportation.“We are going to continue to fight for all the people that are experiencing an injustice,” Abrego Garcia said. “Clearly the government did not decide where my story continues. My family and I decide where my story goes from here.”In 2019, an immigration court issued an order prohibiting the government from removing him to El Salvador after the court found he faced danger from a gang that had targeted his family.Simon Sandoval-Moshenberg, his American attorney, said Wednesday that Abrego Garcia traveled to Spain under a tourist visa for a “short term” stay. The US government was required by court order to lift “all impediments” that barred Abrego Garcia from leaving the country, including removing him from a no-fly list.Abrego Garcia, whose wife and son are American citizens, could be eligible to return to the US as a legal permanent resident. But, he will need waivers from the State Department, which Secretary of State Marco Rubio will not grant, Sandoval-Moshenberg said. “It is going to be up to the next administration to reunite this family as quickly as possible,” he said. Senator Chris Van Hollen, a Democrat from Maryland who met with Abrego Garcia in the Salvadoran prison last year, said the Trump administration had engaged in a “vendetta” against him.“Kilmar and his family are relieved that he is now in a place of his choosing, a free man and living with dignity,” Van Hollen said. “I think the message for all of us is that it’s never wrong to stand up for our Constitution. It’s never wrong to stand up for the rule of law.”Both immigration advocates and the Trump administration said that Abrego Garcia’s departure was a win. Ama Frimpong, chief of services and legal advocacy at We Are CASA, said rather than being deported, Abrego Garcia made the “choice” in where he went.“This is what we fight form the freedom to choose how we live with safety and dignity,” she said.Meanwhile, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin issued a statement taking credit for Abrego Garcia’s exit. He labeled Abrego Garcia as a “human trafficker” and “MS-13 gang member.”Abrego Garcia has denied the government’s allegations.More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

headline: Kullu village women declare war on illicit liquor, fix Rs 5,000 fine
content: In a strong show of grassroots activism against alcohol abuse, the Mahila Mandal of Balu village in Karshaigad panchayat of Anni subdivision in Kullu has resolved to impose a fine of Rs 5,000 on anyone caught selling illicit liquor in the village.The decision was taken at a meeting on Tuesday amid growing concern over the spread of illegal liquor trade and its impact on both young people and the elderly. The women said alcohol had become a serious problem, affecting households across the village and fuelling the need for collective action.Karshaigad panchayat vice-president Paras Ram confirmed that although there was no licensed liquor shop in the area, some individuals were allegedly selling illicit liquor. Responding to the Mahila Mandal’s demand, the panchayat passed a resolution providing for a Rs 5,000 fine and strict legal action against anyone caught selling illegal liquor.The initiative adds to a growing trend of community-led efforts to curb alcohol and substance abuse across Kullu district. In 2021, the Mahila Mandal of Karshaigad gram panchayat had launched a similar campaign, forming ward-level committees to keep a check on drug abuse and illegal liquor sales.The Mahila Mandal of Dayar panchayat in Bhuntar subdivision has also imposed a fine of Rs 25,000 on those found consuming liquor or engaging in gambling. In several villages, such restrictions draw strength from traditional institutions and the directives of local deities, which continue to play an influential role in regulating community life. Malana, for instance, enforces a complete prohibition on liquor following a decree attributed to its presiding deity, Jamlu Devta.Restrictions have also extended to social functions, particularly weddings. Several panchayats in Kullu have imposed penalties of up to Rs 50,000 on hosts serving beer or liquor at marriage ceremonies, viewing such practices as contributing to wider substance abuse.

headline: Boundary wall broken, villagers dump garbage on CHC premises in Rewari district
content: Inadequate infrastructure, lack of blood bank, insufficient OPD space and number of beds for admitted patients and residential quarters for the staff members have been ailing the Community Health Centre (CHC) at Meerpur village in Rewari district.The CHC, which was upgraded from a Primary Health Centre (PHC) long ago, is still functioning from the same old building which often needs repairs and maintenance.Sources point out that the CHC building underwent special repairs recently as the roof used to leak badly.“However, proper electric fittings have not been made after the special repairs, due to which we face frequent power outages and short-circuits,” maintains a doctor serving at the government hospital.The doctors lament that the infrastructure of the hospital is inadequate for the patients coming for treatment on a daily basis as well as the staff members serving here.“The CHC should have 30 beds, but it has only nine. The space for OPD patients is also insufficient. There are no residential quarters for the doctors and other staff members,” states another staffer.The inadequacy of resources can be gauged from the fact that ideally, there should be a CHC on a population of 1 lakh residents, but this CHC has been catering to a population of nearly 2.5 lakh.Strangely, the neighbouring town of Dharuhera, which is a major hub of industry and real estate sector and houses big manufacturing, storage/supply and other units of Hero MotoCorp, Jtekt India, Lumax Industries, Rico Auto Industries, Amul dairy plant, Carlsberg and Indian Oil Corporation, merely has a primary health centre (PHC). Indira Gandhi University (IGU) is also located in Meerpur village.On the other hand, the building of the Meerpur CHC is in such a dilapidated condition that its boundary wall is broken and the compound has been reduced to a garbage-dumping ground by the local residents.“Taking advantage of the broken boundary wall, villagers dump their domestic waste in the hospital compound. Stray animals like cattle and dogs also enter the hospital premises,” laments an employee.The hospital runs OPDs and emergency services and also admits patients, but those requiring blood have to be referred to the Civil Hospital as there is no blood bank at the CHC.The hospital also faces a shortage of staff. Of the 140 sanctioned posts of all categories 32 are lying vacant.Contacted for her comments, Dr Saroj Ranga, Senior Medical Officer in charge of the CHC, said the authorities concerned have been apprised of the constraints.

headline: Congress to hold Constitution march in Shimla today
content: The Himachal Pradesh Congress will organise a Constitution protection march in Shimla on Thursday to mark Constitution Day, with the party expecting 10,000 to 15,000 workers from across the state to participate.The march will begin at the statue of Dr BR Ambedkar at Chaura Maidan and culminate at the statue of Mahatma Gandhi on the Ridge, where participants will collectively read the Preamble to the Constitution. State Congress president Vinay Kumar will lead the march.State Congress organisation general secretary Vinod Zinta said preparations were reviewed at a meeting with party leaders and office-bearers on Wednesday. He said the programme was being organised on the call of the All India Congress Committee as part of its nationwide campaign to highlight the need to protect the Constitution.Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri, state Congress in-charge Rajni Patil and newly appointed AICC secretaries and co-in-charges for Himachal Pradesh, Kamal Kant Sharma and Rahul Rajbhar, will participate.

headline: 1,600 women turn entrepreneurs in Jakhal through self-help groups
content: Rural women in Jakhal block of Fatehabad district are taking steps towards financial independence through self-employment initiatives under the Haryana State Rural Livelihoods Mission. Around 1,600 women associated with the mission are running small businesses, increasing their income and supporting their families financially.Sunil Nagar, Block Programme Manager of the mission, said 426 self-help groups (SHGs) are currently active in Jakhal block. To strengthen their functioning, 43 village organisations and two cluster federations have also been formed.Through these groups, women are being connected with savings schemes, banking facilities and income-generating activities.Nagar said the mission was also helping women access bank loans to start their own businesses. During the current financial year, 35 self-help groups had received loans worth around Rs 1.90 crore for self-employment activities.The women associated with the groups are exploring different business opportunities according to their interests and skills. Some are running beauty parlours, while others are preparing pickles and food products.Several women have also taken up businesses such as flour mills, bag-making, traditional footwear manufacturing and fast food ventures.Sandeep Kaur, who has become financially independent through self-employment, is one example of the change being brought about by the initiative.Nagar said the mission is working under the leadership of Fatehabad District in-charge Sanjay Kumar to expand its activities. Efforts are being made to bring more rural women into self-help groups and provide them with opportunities to earn a livelihood and become financially self-reliant.The initiative is helping rural women move beyond traditional household responsibilities and become active contributors to their families’ income, Nagar added.

headline: Jai Ram slams Cong over closed institutions, eyes ’27 comeback
content: Leader of Opposition Jai Ram Thakur on Wednesday launched a fresh attack on the Congress government, accusing it of shutting down nearly 2,500 government institutions opened by the previous BJP regime in public interest.Addressing a function at Kotli village in Arki, Solan district, organised to felicitate representatives elected in the recent panchayat and urban local body polls, Thakur said the Congress government had begun its tenure by closing institutions instead of initiating new development projects. BJP state president Rajeev Bindal, MP Suresh Kashyap and several senior party leaders and local representatives attended the event.“Nearly 2,500 institutions across the state, which were started in public interest by the previous government, were closed. It is unfortunate that a government elected to serve the people began its tenure by shutting down institutions,” he said.Questioning the government’s functioning, Thakur said the Chief Minister and Deputy Chief Minister had decided to close hundreds of institutions even before the Cabinet was expanded.He also accused the state government of failing to acknowledge the Centre’s contribution to Himachal’s development, claiming that Prime Minister Narendra Modi considered the state his home and that several development initiatives depended on Central funding.Targeting the Congress over its electoral promises, Thakur said every section of society was suffering due to what he termed anti-people policies, hollow assurances and unfulfilled guarantees. He claimed the promises made before the 2022 Assembly elections had been exposed and asserted that voters would no longer be misled by them.Expressing confidence in the BJP’s prospects, Thakur said the trend of Congress defeats and BJP victories would continue and predicted that the party would return to power with a landslide majority in the 2027 Assembly elections.

headline: No permission sought for November 26 anti-SIR march, Delhi Police say; organisers say ‘intimation’ sent
content: NEW DELHI No permission has been sought from the Delhi Police for a protest march against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, scheduled for November 26, senior New Delhi police officials said. The organisers, however, maintained that they had intimated the police about the proposed demonstration. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/special-intensive-revision-of-electoral-rolls/ Anti-SIR platform calls for mass agitation from November 26 to December 20 storyline 1 United stand: Editorial on protests against SIR https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/editorial/united-stand-on-protests-against-sir/article71658203.ece The Delhi wing of the People Against SIR platform has called for a march on Constitution Day from Valmiki Sadan on Mandir Marg towards Jantar Mantar. The protesters are demanding the scrapping of SIR and the restoration of Jantar Mantar as a designated site for peaceful protests, among other demands. An email dated November 23, 2026, seen by The Hindu, was sent to the Delhi Police to inform them about the proposed programme. Ms. Mollah claimed that the police had acknowledged the intimation and subsequently sought further details, including the proposed route and the expected number of participants expected. These details, she said, were shared with the police over a telephone conversation. The organisers have also announced plans to burn copies of the SIR notification during the demonstration. headline: As 2027 race gathers steam, AAP to sound poll bugle from Moga today
content: Moga has emerged as the centre of political activity in Punjab as parties step up preparations for the 2027 Vidhan Sabha elections, with the ruling AAP and the revived SAD-BJP alliance choosing the district to launch their respective election campaigns.Located in the heart of the politically crucial Malwa region, Moga is set to witness back-to-back campaign launches.Malwa accounts for 69 of the 117 Assembly segments and is widely seen as the region that determines which party forms the government in the state. Moga’s location ensures easy access for people from all regions, including Doaba and Majha.AAP will formally kick-start its 2027 election campaign with a mega rally, titled ‘Khushhal Punjab’, in Moga on Thursday. The rally will also provide an opportunity for the Bhagwant Mann-led government to present its five-year report card to the people, highlighting its achievements and seeking to consolidate support ahead of the Assembly elections.AAP general secretary Baltej Pannu said the rally would showcase the government’s work over the past five years, reflect public support for the party and set the direction for the 2027 Vidhan Sabha elections. He described the event as the beginning of a new chapter in Punjab politics, adding that the party would take its five-year report card directly to the people.The party plans to highlight the provision of more than 78,000 government jobs on merit, its claim that nearly 90 per cent of households are receiving zero electricity bills, and the expansion of canal irrigation coverage from 22-23 per cent to nearly 88 per cent under the Mann government.The SAD-BJP alliance is also preparing to launch its joint election campaign from Moga on December 8. The Shiromani Akali Dal has often regarded Moga as a lucky starting point, having launched its election campaigns from the district in 1996, 2006 and 2011 before returning to power in 1997, 2007 and 2012, respectively.AAP, too, has used the district for major political announcements in the past. In September 2016, the party held a rally at Baghapurana in Moga during the run-up to the 2017 Assembly elections. It had then released its manifesto for farmers in the district.Moga’s political significance extends beyond electoral calculations. The district has a legacy of participation in the freedom struggle, with freedom fighter Lala Lajpat Rai hailing from Dhudike village. The student movement of 1972 also brought the region into political prominence.Meanwhile, the Enforcement Directorate has summoned AAP’s Moga MLA Dr Amandeep Kaur Arora on Thursday, while the party’s Dharamkot MLA Devinderjeet Singh Laddi Dhos has been summoned on Friday.Mann, Kejriwal meet jailed minister Arora’s familyChief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann and AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal today met the family of jailed AAP minister Sanjeev Arora at their residence in Ludhiana this evening.As Arora has been declared AAP candidate from the Ludhiana (West) segment, both Kejriwal and Mann spent around 15 minutes with the family.“The leaders motivated the entire family to work hard in the absence of Arora and extended all support. We are thankful to both the leaders for visiting us and boosting our morale,” said Sandhya Arora, his wife.As AAP holds “Khushhal Punjab” rally in Moga tomorrow, the district administration and police have been on their toes as both CM Mann and Kejriwal will stay overnight in Ludhiana before leaving for the rally.A well-placed source said the rally would formally kick-start the AAP’s election campaign in Punjab. “We cannot take it lightly. Chief Secretary KAP Sinha and DGP Gaurav Yadav had already visited Moga on November 23 to review the arrangements,” the source said.

headline: Teachers to become first line  of defence against child abuse in Amritsar
content: Over 1,000 teachers in Amritsar were sensitised to child protection during a workshop organised by the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA). Held under the Pan-India Surakshit Bachpan Abhiyan (Phase-II) at Madhav Vidya Niketan Senior Secondary School, Ranjit Avenue, the workshop focused on equipping teachers to identify signs of abuse, respond sensitively and ensure timely legal intervention.The initiative assumes significance as teachers are often among the first adults to notice behavioural changes, unexplained fear, withdrawal or other signs of distress among children. Recognising these warning signs and taking appropriate action can help protect vulnerable children.The workshop was organised in collaboration with the Education Department under the leadership of District and Sessions Judge-cum-DLSA Chairperson Jatinder Kaur and Civil Judge (Senior Division)-cum-DLSA Secretary Amardeep Singh Bains.Panel advocates Kirpal Kaur and Sandeep Singh Randhawa, along with Education Department coordinator Harpreet Singh, sensitised teachers to child rights, safety protocols and mandatory reporting provisions under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012.The speakers emphasised that child protection was not merely a legal responsibility but also a collective social duty. Teachers were urged to create a supportive environment where children could report abuse without fear or stigma. Participants were also informed about free legal aid services and emergency helplines, including Child Helpline (1098), National Legal Aid Helpline (15100), Cybercrime Helpline (1930).

headline: No pandit, no pheras: Sirmaur couple takes wedding vows with hands on Constitution
content: In a wedding that broke away from traditional rituals to embrace constitutional values, a couple in Sirmaur exchanged marriage vows with their hands placed on the Constitution of India instead of taking the customary pheras around a sacred fire.Surender Singh Dharma, a resident of Dharma village, married Hemlata, who hails from Tandai village in Kupvi tehsil of Shimla district, in a ceremony held on November 22 in Dharma village of Kamrau tehsil. The marriage was solemnised under a constitutional framework introduced by the newly formed Samta Vivah Samiti (SVS HP), an organisation working towards gender and social equality. Its president, Arjun Ranta, acted as the authorised solemniser.The wedding retained the warmth and celebrations of a traditional ceremony, with the bride and groom dressed in customary attire and family members, relatives and friends gathering for the occasion. However, there were no priests chanting mantras or conventional wedding rituals.Instead, portraits of Gautam Buddha, Sant Kabir, Guru Ravidas, Jyotiba Phule, Periyar, Dr BR Ambedkar, Kanshi Ram and Bhagat Singh adorned the venue, reflecting the social reformers and leaders whose ideas inspired the ceremony.The proceedings began with the collective recitation of the Preamble to the Constitution. The couple then took their marriage vows while placing their hands on the Constitution, with the bride being given the first opportunity to take the oath as a symbolic assertion of gender equality. Before entering their new home, the newlyweds also paid their respects to the Preamble.Two witnesses each from the bride’s and groom’s families signed a marriage declaration, which was authenticated with the committee’s official seal and signatures of its office-bearers. Copies were handed over to the couple for further formalities.The ceremony has drawn attention against the backdrop of another unusual marriage in Sirmaur’s Shillai area in July 2025, when Sunita Chauhan married two brothers, Pradeep and Kapil Negi, under the traditional Jodidara or Jajda practice of the Hatti community.However, the two ceremonies represent distinctly different practices. While the Shillai wedding followed an established community custom, the latest one sought to foreground constitutional principles of equality, dignity and mutual respect.There is, however, no separate statutory category of marriage called a ‘constitutional marriage’ under Indian law. While Articles 14, 15 and 21 of the Constitution guarantee equality, non-discrimination, liberty and dignity, the legal validity of a marriage depends on compliance with applicable marriage legislation. The vows and declaration facilitated by the committee do not, by themselves, amount to statutory marriage registration.

headline: Himachal Pradesh University explores research ties with Norway varsities
content: Himachal Pradesh University (HPU) is making concerted efforts to strengthen its international academic and research collaborations with leading universities and research institutions in Norway, with the aim of emerging as one of the country’’s leading universities.Under this initiative, the university is identifying areas of mutual research interest, joint research projects, faculty and student exchange programmes, collaborative PhD supervision and other academic activities.Taking the initiative forward, a university delegation led by Vice-Chancellor Prof Mahavir Singh visited Norway in October 2026 to explore international academic and research partnerships. During the visit, the delegation interacted with representatives of the Western Norway University of Applied Sciences, Oslo Metropolitan University (OsloMet) and the Institute for Energy Technology (IFE), among other institutions, to explore opportunities for collaborative research, academic exchange and institutional partnerships.A major outcome of the visit was the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with OsloMet, Norway. The agreement seeks to explore several areas of academic cooperation, including joint research projects, collaborative publications, exchange of students and faculty members, joint supervision of research scholars and the development of potential joint PhD programmes, subject to mutual agreement and applicable academic and regulatory requirements.Taking the collaboration forward, Prof Maneesh Singh of the Western Norway University of Applied Sciences, Bergen, visited HPU on November 18 for a three-day visit. During his stay, he interacted with Vice-Chancellor Prof Mahavir Singh, Dean of Studies Prof BK Shivram and deans and chairpersons of various teaching departments to discuss ways to strengthen academic and research collaboration.The discussions focused on identifying specific interdisciplinary research areas and potential international research funding programmes under which HPU faculty members could submit joint research proposals.

headline: Face-off between Hisar lawyers, traffic police takes legal turn
content: The confrontation between traffic police personnel and lawyers over the stopping of a car at Jindal Chowk in Hisar has escalated, with the police registering FIRs against both sides.After registering a case against two lawyers on Tuesday night, the police on Wednesday booked Home Guard personnel Rajbir and others on the basis of a complaint filed by the lawyers. The second FIR was registered ahead of the 3 pm deadline set by the Bar Association, which had threatened further action if the police personnel involved in the incident were not booked.The controversy erupted on Tuesday evening when a Home Guard jawan and advocate Vishal Yadav allegedly clashed over the stopping of a car at Jindal Chowk.Acting on the Home Guard jawan’s complaint, the police registered an FIR against advocates Vishal Yadav and Suraj Yadav under six sections, including assault, tearing of uniform, obstructing a public servant from discharging official duty and criminal intimidation.In response, Bar Association president Pradeep Singh Bajia and other office-bearers met SP Siddhant Jain and demanded action against the police personnel.Bar Association joint secretary Sahil Maderna said the lawyers had submitted the names of seven to eight police personnel to the SP. The police subsequently registered a case against three to four personnel and others on the basis of their complaint. Following the registration of the counter-FIR, the Bar Association withdrew its decision to convene a general house meeting.Maderna alleged that Vishal Yadav had returned to the spot after dropping his family home, where 10 to 12 police personnel assaulted him.

headline: Amritsar: Beautification or bottleneck? Court Road project faces flak
content: City residents, particularly daily commuters, are questioning the ongoing beautification work on Court Road, alleging that it is reducing road space and adding to traffic congestion.Objecting to the project, several residents have been uploading videos of the civil work on social media, drawing strong reactions from netizens, many of whom have criticised the initiative.As part of the beautification project, nearly two-foot-high semi-circular brick structures have been constructed along the road. Filled with loose soil, these structures appear to have been designed for plantation purposes. However, residents say the structures, built adjacent to footpaths, are reducing the operational width of the road and shrinking the available parking space. Each structure occupies approximately four square feet. Gurdeep Singh, a resident, said Court Road witnesses heavy vehicular traffic throughout the day.A considerable stretch on both sides of the road, connecting Railway Link Road to Court Chowk, is routinely used for parking vehicles. Before implementing any development project, the authorities should assess its likely impact and practical implications, he added.Residents also pointed to a similar project undertaken on the Circular Road. Conceived to attract tourists and ease traffic congestion, the 7.4-km stretch connecting the walled city’s 12 historic gates was developed at a cost of Rs 125 crore under the Smart City Mission between 2020 and 2025. However, they claim the project has failed to achieve its objectives, with encroachments and illegal parking continuing to plague the area.Social activist Pawandeep Sharma said the nearly eight-foot-wide elevated side lanes created for cycling eventually narrowed the functional width of the road. Instead of serving cyclists, many of these stretches were encroached upon by vendors selling a variety of items. He said traffic congestion on such roads would remain a recurring problem as long as infrastructure projects created localised bottlenecks without addressing parking and encroachment issues.

headline: BJP targets AAP over drugs, gangsterism in Punjab
content: The BJP on Wednesday accused the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab of failing to curb drug trafficking, gangsterism and extortion. Delhi minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa alleged that criminal networks were operating under political protection.Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Sirsa warned that AAP leaders allegedly accepting money from drug smugglers or protecting criminal networks would face imprisonment if the NDA formed the next government in Punjab. He specifically named senior AAP leaders Manish Sisodia and Satyendar Jain, asserting that political influence would not shield anyone from action.Questioning the effectiveness of the Mann government’s anti-drug campaign, Sirsa cited figures released by the AAP government claiming that 94,746 arrests had been made in 632 days. He compared this figure with Punjab’s reported prison capacity of around 26,000 inmates and questioned how such a large number of accused persons could have been detained.He alleged that cases were being registered under less stringent provisions of the law, enabling accused persons to secure bail instead of ensuring sustained action against drug trafficking networks.Sirsa also referred to the killing of Punjab Police Sub-Inspector Iqbal Singh in Tarn Taran and a reported police advisory against off-duty personnel travelling in uniform. He argued that the incidents reflected growing concerns over the safety of police personnel.Accusing the AAP government of worsening Punjab’s financial position, Sirsa claimed that the state’s debt had increased from Rs 2.5 lakh crore to Rs 5 lakh crore during its tenure.

headline: Special session of Haryana Assembly today to mark Constitution Day
content: The Haryana Legislative Assembly will hold a special session on Thursday to mark Constitution Day, with a programme highlighting the making of the Constitution and the values enshrined in it.The proceedings will begin at 11 am with obituary references. At 11.30 am, a special programme dedicated to the Constitution will be organised near the Ceremonial Gate outside the Vidhan Bhawan.A documentary showcasing the historical journey of Constitution-making, the contributions of its framers and the principles underlying the Constitution will also be screened.On the occasion, the Assembly Speaker will present Hindi and English editions of the Constitution to all members of the House.The proceedings of the Assembly will resume after the special programme.

headline: BJP slams Sukhu govt over internal rift and administrative breakdown in Himachal
content: BJP state chief spokesperson Rajinder Rana today accused the Congress government in Himachal Pradesh of being mired in factionalism, corruption and administrative chaos. Addressing mediapersons here, he said the situation had reached a stage where even Congress MLAs and ministers had started questioning the government.Targeting Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, Rana alleged that MLAs were being misled over ministerial positions, even as the state Congress in-charge had clarified that no names had been recommended to the party high command.Rana also alleged serious financial irregularities in the construction of the Hamirpur bus stand. He said a tender worth more than Rs 45 crore was floated in March 2024 and subsequently awarded for approximately Rs 34 crore. Despite the project exceeding its 18-month completion deadline, no penalty had been imposed for the delay, he alleged. He further claimed that the project cost had increased to Rs 123 crore without inviting a fresh tender, while nearly Rs 100 crore had already been paid to the construction company.Rana alleged that the government was registering FIRs against opposition leaders whenever they raised questions about corruption. However, he asserted that the BJP would not remain silent on such issues. He also criticised the government for withholding MLA development funds while allegedly providing funds through the “backdoor” to select MLAs.He questioned the delay in holding Hamirpur Municipal Corporation elections, which he said had been pending for two years. He also raised concerns over the processing of 70 tenders through the offline mode, alleging a lack of transparency in the process.Clarifying the BJP’s stand on the political developments in the state, Rana said the party had never attempted to topple the government. Instead, he said, it had extended support to a leader from Himachal Pradesh during the Rajya Sabha elections.Describing the proposed celebration of the Congress government’s four years in power, Rana termed it a festival of debt, plunder and broken promises made in the party’s election manifesto.

headline: NDRI’s three-day National Dairy Mela & Agri Expo begins from Nov 26
content: The Indian Council of Agricultural Research - National Dairy Research Institute (ICAR-NDRI) will organise a three-day National Dairy Mela and Agri Expo from November 26 to 28, bringing together livestock farmers, dairy entrepreneurs, scientists, experts and milk producers from across the country.The programme aims to promote the adoption of modern technologies in the dairy sector, enhance farmers’ income and encourage innovation in milk production and processing. Advanced dairy technologies, improved animal breeds, scientific research and innovations in agriculture and dairy entrepreneurship will be among the key attractions.This was stated by ICAR-NDRI Director Dr Dheer Singh while interacting with media persons on Wednesday at a conference hall of the institute. This year’s mela is expected to witness the participation of more than 400 livestock farmers whose animals will participate in beauty and milking contests. Special invitations have also been given to goat farmers to highlight the growing opportunities in goat rearing and milk production.He said that for the first time, the institute will display all its technologies, which are under process with already developed technologies, so that the young brains can get benefits of these technologies in dairy and food processing.“This mela would provide a valuable platform for farmers and livestock owners to learn about scientific advancements and technologies developed by the institute. The primary objective is to take the research and scientific technologies developed at NDRI directly to farmers and livestock owners. This year, we will also showcase technologies that have already been developed and are ready for commercial adoption,” he said.Meanwhile, the Director also announced that the NDRI will now organise the National Dairy Mela every year on November 26 to mark National Milk Day.Accompanied by Joint Director Dr Rajan Sharma, Dr Gopal Sankhla, Dr Ajay Dang, Director Dr Singh said that the institute would extend all possible support to young entrepreneurs interested in adopting these technologies and establishing start-ups. Several former NDRI students, he said, had already made a mark in business and entrepreneurship.Highlighting the institute’s research achievements, the Director said India had made considerable progress in dairy processing, while NDRI continued its efforts to improve the productivity of milch animals.He highlighted the success of the ovum pick-up (OPU) technology, which enables the production of multiple elite animals from a single animal through advanced reproductive techniques.“The ovum pick-up technology has emerged as an important achievement. It helps produce multiple animals from a single donor animal, and people from the private sector are also adopting this technology,” Dr Singh said.India produces around 247 million tonnes of milk annually, accounting for nearly 25 per cent of global milk production and making it the world’s leading milk-producing country.

headline: Pawan Sharma takes charge as new VC of Central University
content: Prof Pawan Kumar Sharma has assumed charge as the Vice-Chancellor of the Central University of Haryana, Mahendragarh, succeeding Prof (Dr) Tankeshwar Kumar, whose tenure of over five years has ended.The Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, Government of India, issued the appointment order on November 25 following approval by President of India and university Chancellor Droupadi Murmu.Prof Sharma is a distinguished scientist and academician with over 30 years of university teaching experience and more than 35 years of research experience. Before taking up the new assignment, he served as Professor of Chemistry at Kurukshetra University for over 25 years.During 2023-24, he was a Fulbright Scholar-in-Residence and Visiting Professor at Wesleyan University in Connecticut, US. In 2019, under the Fulbright-Nehru International Education Administrators Award, he visited 17 prestigious universities in the US.Prof Sharma has published 156 research papers in international journals and holds several patents. His research credentials include an h-index of 40 and an i10-index of 114. He has also maintained a long-standing research collaboration with the Nucleic Acid Center in Denmark.His contributions to science have earned him several prestigious honours, including the Srinivasa Ramanujan Birth Centenary Award Gold Medal, the Bronze Medal of the Chemical Research Society of India and the National Award of the Indian Chemical Society. He is also a recipient of the Youth Red Cross Award.

headline: 19 arrests, 6 FIRs, no convictions under Himachal’s anti-conversion law
content: Nearly four years after Himachal Pradesh enacted its anti-conversion law, not a single case registered under the legislation has resulted in a conviction, despite 19 arrests and six FIRs.Between 2023 and November 1, 2026, the state received 15 complaints under the Himachal Pradesh Freedom of Religion Act, 2019, as amended in 2022. Of these, only six were converted into FIRs, leading to the arrest of 19 persons. The details were disclosed in a written reply tabled in the Himachal Pradesh Assembly during its recent winter session.Kangra accounted for the highest number of complaints, with eight cases reported from the district. However, none resulted in an FIR, and all eight complaints were disposed of by the police. Kullu received two complaints, of which one led to an FIR, while the other remains under preliminary inquiry. Dehra, Hamirpur, Mandi, Shimla and Una each registered one FIR. No complaints were reported from the remaining police districts.The year-wise breakup shows that the state received eight complaints in 2023, three in 2024, one in 2025 and three up to November 1, 2026.Shimla recorded the highest number of arrests, with 11 accused, followed by Una with four, Kullu with three and Hamirpur with one. Police have completed investigations in all six FIRs and filed chargesheets in four of them. However, none of the cases has reached a judicial conclusion.Of the six cases, four — registered in Hamirpur, Kullu, Shimla and Una — are pending trial before courts. In the remaining two cases, registered in Dehra and Mandi, the police have submitted cancellation reports before the respective courts. The government confirmed that no court had pronounced either a conviction or an acquittal in any of the cases.The government also shared details of complaints involving allegations of religious conversion through allurement, coercion or concealment of religious identity for marriage. One case each was registered in Nirmand, Haroli and Mandi. Chargesheets have been filed in the Nirmand and Haroli cases, both of which are pending before courts, while a cancellation report has been submitted in the Mandi case.Despite the complaints and arrests, the state government has ruled out establishing a dedicated monitoring or grievance redressal mechanism to deal with such cases. It maintained that the existing policing arrangements were adequate to address the issue.As part of the existing system, Superintendents of Police conduct monthly crime review meetings, while cases are also monitored at police headquarters. The government further cited intensified patrolling in sensitive areas, the emergency helpline 112 and women’s help desks as measures available to address complaints.The Himachal Pradesh Freedom of Religion Act, 2019, was enacted to prohibit religious conversions through misrepresentation, force, fraud, undue influence, coercion, inducement or marriage. It replaced the 2006 Act. The legislation was further strengthened through a 2022 amendment, which introduced a prohibition on mass conversions and increased the maximum punishment for unlawful conversion from seven to 10 years.

headline: Kangra warehouses well stocked for PDS supply
content: Kangra district has adequate stocks of pulses, edible oil and other essential food commodities to ensure uninterrupted supplies through the public distribution system (PDS), with substantial reserves available in government warehouses.As of November 21, a total of 5,904 quintals of pulses had been supplied to 1,165 fair price shops across the district under the Himachal Pradesh State Special Subsidised Scheme. An additional 3,453 quintals of pulses are available in the wholesale warehouses of the HP State Civil Supplies Corporation.Similarly, 5,61,516 litres of edible oil have been supplied to fair price shops during November, while another 2,73,238 litres are available in the corporation’s wholesale warehouses.District Controller, Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs, Kangra, Purushottam Singh, said adequate stocks of flour, rice, salt and sugar were also available in wholesale warehouses. He said the department was ensuring regular replenishment of fair price shops so that eligible beneficiaries received essential commodities on time.Kangra has 1,165 fair price shops catering to consumers under the Public Distribution System and the state government’s special subsidised scheme. The scheme provides essential commodities, including pulses, salt, sugar and edible oil, at rates considerably lower than prevailing market prices. Singh said the subsidised rates were helping households save on essential purchases.

headline: Rohtak’s activity-based learning initiative picked for national award
content: Rohtak district’s innovative initiative ‘Nipunvatika’ has been selected for the SKOCH Award in recognition of its contribution to education and grassroots-level innovation.The nomination successfully cleared all stages of the rigorous and independent, outcome-based evaluation process. The ADC has been invited to attend the award ceremony during the 111th SKOCH Summit in New Delhi on December 19. The summit’s theme is ‘Growth, Prosperity and Resilience’.SKOCH Group Managing Director informed the Additional Deputy Commissioner (ADC) Narendra Kumar about the selection through an official communication on Tuesday.‘Nipunvatika’ was conceptualised by the ADC with the objective of creating an innovative, child-friendly learning environment in government schools, particularly for children at the foundational stage of education.The initiative sought to supplement conventional classroom teaching with activity-based and experiential learning, enabling children to acquire foundational literacy and numeracy skills through play, exploration and practical activities.“Nipunvatika has emerged as a model initiative, prompting the state government to adopt the concept for establishing a Model Balvatika in every district during the 2026–27 academic year. Established in September last year, Nipunvatika provides a creative, activity-based learning environment where children learn through educational toys, interactive tools and hands-on activities,” the ADC pointed out.Explaining the concept, Kumar said the initiative aims to make learning joyful, experiential and concept-oriented, enabling children to develop a strong academic foundation during their formative years.“Activities have been designed in accordance with child psychology and age-appropriate pedagogy, encouraging learning through observation, exploration and experimentation rather than rote memorisation. The first-of-its-kind initiative in Haryana was developed with the support of corporate social responsibility (CSR) funding, which helped translate the concept into reality,” he added.Kumar claimed that the initiative had already received appreciation from Haryana Governor Prof Ashim Kumar Ghosh and Haryana Education Minister Mahipal Dhanda.“Winning the SKOCH Award is a significant milestone for Rohtak. The journey of Nipunvatika, from its conceptualisation in the district to its adoption as a reference model across Haryana and now its recognition at the national level, demonstrates the potential of locally developed educational innovations to create wider and sustainable impact,” the ADC added.

headline: Panchkula police reunite lost child with family after three-hour search
content: Two Panchkula police constables reunited a three-year-old child, who was found wandering alone in the middle of a road, with his family after nearly three hours of sustained efforts.According to DCP Amarinder Singh, constables Ajeeb and Gaurav were on patrol near Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar Chowk in Sector 25 around 4 pm on November 24 when they spotted the child wandering alone on the road.The policemen immediately took the child into safe custody and tried to ask him about his parents and home, but he was unable to provide any information.To trace his family, they questioned nearby street vendors and shopkeepers, but no one could identify the child. The boy was then taken to the Sector 25 police outpost.Under the supervision of outpost in-charge Ramu Swami, a police team launched a search for the child’s family and made inquiries in Sector 26, but initially found no leads.Undeterred, the team continued its efforts. During the search, a woman in Ashiana, B Block, Sector 26, recognised the child and informed the police that she knew his family. She then guided the team to the child’s home, where they met his parents.After nearly three hours of continuous efforts, the police safely reunited the child with his parents around 7 pm. The family thanked the Panchkula police and appreciated the prompt and sensitive response of the officials.Police Commissioner Pankaj Nain said the role of the police extended beyond crime prevention and maintaining law and order to helping citizens in times of need. He added that the safety of children and senior citizens remained a priority for the force.He commended constables Ajeeb and Gaurav for their sensitivity, responsibility and dedication in reuniting the child with his family, adding that the Panchkula police personnel were always ready to assist and protect the public.

headline: Himachal’s Justice Thakur picked Tripura CJ
content: The Supreme Court Collegium has recommended the appointment of Himachal HC Judge Vivek Singh Thakur as the Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court. A native of Bilaspur district, Justice Thakur is currently the senior-most judge of the Himachal Pradesh High Court. He will succeed Justice MS Ramachandra Rao, who has been transferred as Chief Justice of the Karnataka HC.Born on April 16, 1966, Justice Thakur completed his LLB from Himachal Pradesh University and LLM from Kurukshetra University. He enrolled as an advocate with the Himachal Pradesh Bar Council in 1990 and practised extensively in constitutional, civil, arbitration, taxation, criminal and service matters.He served as Assistant Advocate General of Himachal Pradesh from 1998 to 2003, Additional Advocate General from 2008 to 2013 and Senior Panel Counsel for the Union of India before being elevated to the Himachal Pradesh High Court in 2016.Justice Thakur has also held various administrative positions in the State Legal Services Authority and the Judicial Academy.

headline: Fog alert: Fatehabad officials told to tighten road safety measures
content: With winter fog increasing the risk of road accidents, the Fatehabad administration has directed officials to strengthen road safety measures across the district, especially on national highways, state highways and other major roads.Additional Deputy Commissioner (ADC) Anurag Dhalia instructed the officials to ensure that no vehicle was parked illegally along roadsides, warning that such vehicles could cause serious accidents during foggy conditions and at night.The directions were issued while reviewing the implementation of instructions given by Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini during a video conference. Dhalia stressed the need for regular monitoring and coordination among departments to prevent accidents and loss of life and property.The ADC directed officials to complete white line markings on all roads on priority. He also asked them to keep road blinkers functional and install warning and information boards at accident-prone spots, sharp turns and other sensitive locations.Officials were told to inspect roads regularly, repair safety-related shortcomings and close illegal road openings. The administration also directed the departments to ensure reflective tapes on tractor-trailers, trucks and other vehicles and launch awareness campaigns for drivers. The Forest Department was asked to trim tree branches along roads to improve visibility.Dhalia also called for special attention to accidents caused by stray animals in urban and rural areas. The officials were directed to move such animals to safe places and keep a close watch on accident-prone locations.‘Mhari Sadak’ complaints to be resolved on timeThe ADC asked officials to ensure timely disposal of complaints registered on the ‘Mhari Sadak’ app, adding that no complaint should remain pending. He also appealed to the people to follow traffic rules during foggy weather and avoid overspeeding.

headline: 'Koi Cinema Thodi Hai': Anant Singh Turns Daughter's Wedding Into Fair
content: Waving an orange gamcha, Anant Singh rose through the sunroof of an SUV as a sea of supporters pressed in around it. The Mokama MLA, known across Bihar as 'Chhote Sarkar', was arriving for his daughter's wedding, and he did it in a style that would upstage any groom. Today, his younger daughter Shivangi Singh is getting married in his ancestral home in Patna's Nadawan village. Her father has thrown the doors open to everyone, and it looks as if everyone has turned up. By Wednesday afternoon, Nadawan had run out of room. The narrow road leading in was packed from one end to the other. As more than five lakh people poured in, according to local estimates, the traffic jam stretched for anywhere between five and 10 km. They came in cars, on tractors and on foot. Food stalls popped up by the roadside. Loudspeakers blared from rooftops. It looked like a fair. Some of the best seats were on the electricity pylons. Young men had climbed the steel towers, and from up there they could see horses kicking up dust on a 12-bigha track, a wall of spectators on every side, and a brand-new Mahindra Thar waiting for whoever crossed the line first. Fifty-two horses had been brought in, with riders from Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, Rajasthan and other states. As the contest neared its end, the crowd took over. People pushed past the edges and spilled on to the track, forcing the organisers to halt the event and clear the ground. The grand finale will now be held on Thursday.

headline: G.O. issued on CAS for teachers of aided arts and science colleges
content: Chennai Keeping up with its announcement made during the demand for grant on August 24, the Tamil Nadu Higher Education Department issued a Government Order (G.O.) on Tuesday, awarding Career Advancement Scheme (CAS) monetary benefits to teachers of government-aided Arts and Science colleges. According to the G.O., the government has sanctioned ₹11.75 crore as recurring monthly expenditure for awarding CAS to eligible teachers, with effect from September 1. A total of 6,116 teachers will benefit from the scheme. According to the G.O., the eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented “in strict adherence” to guidelines issued through a G.O. of January 11, 2021. The scheme would be implemented only after proper verification of the eligibility of each teacher. A screening and selection committee will scrutinise promotion requests and applications, and the Regional Joint Director will forward the minutes and recommendations to the Director of Collegiate Education. After being vetted, the files would be sent back to the Regional Joint Director who would forward the same, along with service records, to audit teams nominated by the Director-General of Audit. After receiving the observations from the audit teams, the Regional Joint Director would issue relevant CAS orders. The G.O. warns that the responsibility of any miscalculation or error would fall squarely on the officer who issues the CAS order. The excess amount paid will be recovered from the teacher, while action will be initiated against erring officials.

headline: Vande Mataram at J&K waqf event sparks row
content: SRINAGAR: Several Muslim clerics who attended a J&K Waqf Board function where Vande Mataram was played in full expressed regret and said they had prayed for repentance, as the national song triggered a religious controversy in Kashmir.The clerics, who attended Monday’s Waqf Day event in Srinagar, said they had neither endorsed the song in their hearts nor through their words. “Since we attended the gathering, if our participation has hurt anyone’s religious sentiments, we sincerely repent before Allah and pray that He accepts our repentance,” they said in a statement on Wednesday.The function was attended by Union minority affairs minister Kiren Rijiju, waqf board chairperson and senior BJP politician Dr Darakhshan Andrabi, Lok Sabha MP Mian Altaf Ahmad and other dignitaries.All six stanzas of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay’s 1875 poem Vande Mataram were played at the event in accordance with a Union home ministry protocol directive issued earlier this year that mandated the full version at state functions, official events and legislature sessions.In August, the President cleared the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, putting Vande Mataram on a par with the national anthem. The amendment did not alter the stanzas, but made disrespect or disruption punishable.Adopted as a slogan during the freedom movement, the poem was abridged in 1937 when the Congress Working Committee approved only its first two stanzas to respect religious diversity.Mirwaiz Umar Farooq-led Mutahida Majlis-e-Ulama (MMU), an amalgam of religious organisations and institutions, said there was no legal obligation to play the song at an official function, and criticised the waqf board for playing it at an event organised by an institution entrusted with safeguarding Muslim religious endowments.It said playing Vande Mataram at the event conflicted with Islam’s principle of Tawheed, or absolute oneness of Allah. “While Islam encourages love for one’s homeland, it draws a clear distinction between love for one’s homeland and its worship. Any expression or practice that attributes divinity to the motherland is contrary to the fundamental Islamic belief of Tawheed and is, therefore, un-Islamic and impermissible for Muslims,” MMU said.It said it was considering legal advice and urged Muslims entrusted with religious responsibilities to uphold their beliefs without compromise. Andrabi was not available for comment.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Omar government breaks silence on Sheshnag row, says lake safe
content: SRINAGAR: The J&K government Wednesday said Sheshnag Lake was completely safe and dismissed allegations of construction near the high-altitude lake by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) that were triggered by a video showing heavy machinery operating near the water body.Forest minister Altaf Kaloo said the earthmover seen in the viral video was operating 200 to 300 feet away from the lake and at a higher elevation. He said not even a grain of soil had entered the lake.The minister, who was scheduled to visit the lake for an on-the-spot inspection on Tuesday, said he could not reach the site due to security concerns. “I had to visit the lake today on the directions of CM Omar Abdullah, but I could not proceed further beyond a certain point as security arrangements were not in place there. Being a protected person, I was advised by the police not to go ahead. I returned and held another detailed meeting with my department,” he said.Kaloo said a 12-member team comprising officials from the departments concerned inspected the area and submitted its findings. “The team reported to me that Sheshnag is completely safe. BRO has not tampered with the track along the lake,” he said.“It is a very holy place for Muslims, Hindus and Sikhs. We respect it, and everybody respects it,” he said.The minister said the BRO was carrying out routine maintenance of the track before and after the annual Amarnath Yatra, including repairing tiles and strengthening its edges, as this work could not be undertaken during the pilgrimage.Kaloo also defended the MOU between the J&K government and the BRO signed early this year under which the organisation was assigned maintenance work of the track.He accused BJP and PDP of politicising the issue ahead of elections in Uttar Pradesh.“There is no track beyond 12 feet of width. The width has to be maintained at 12 feet as per the Supreme Court’s directions. It is meant for pilgrims and horsemen, with six feet for movement in each direction,” he said.PDP‘s Iltija Mufti, however, countered Kaloo, saying that if everything is fine in Sheshnag as claimed by the forest minister, why PDP president Mehbooba Mufti isn’t being allowed to visit the site.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
