headline: Three persons killed in accident in Tiruvannamalai
content: TIRUVANNAMALAI A family of three persons were killed in a road accident after a two-wheeler that they were travelling was hit by a car on Chittoor–Cuddalore High Road near Kalasapakkam town in Tiruvannamalai on Wednesday. Police identified the deceased as S. Yoganatham, 38; Deepa, 34; and Durga, 6. Injured son was identified as Bharani Kumar, 9. Yoganatham worked as a teacher at a private school near Adukkamparai village in Vellore and his deceased wife Deepa was also teacher at a government school in the area. Initial inquiry revealed that the family was travelling on the two-wheeler to Tiruvannamalai town when a car, which was coming in the opposite direction, hit their vehicle. Four pilgrims, including the driver, were present in the car at the time of the accident, which occurred around 5.30 a.m. Police said in the impact, Yoganatham and his daughter were thrown away from the two-wheeler and died on the spot. Immediately, passersby and other motorists rescued injured persons, including four pilgrims, and admitted them at Government Medical College Hospital in Tiruvannamalai, where doctors said that Deepa was brought dead. Police said that the region has been witnessing strong showers for the past two days. It has turned the busy stretch wet and slippery, risking road users. A case was registered and further probe is under way.

headline: Burglars decamp with 15 sovereigns of gold, cash from house near Jolarpet
content: TIRUPATTUR Burglars decamped with 15 sovereigns of gold jewellery, and around ₹1.2 lakh in cash from the house of a tribal family near Jolarpet town in Tirupattur on Wednesday. Police identified the victim as R. Siva, who belongs to the Irular community. He was living with his wife and son on the outskirts of the town. Siva went to Tiruvannamalai town for Maha Deepam day as part of Karthigai Deepam festival. When he returned home around 2 a.m., Siva opened the main entrance of the house and found cupboards in the living room and the bedroom door were broken. Police said that gold ornaments and cash kept in the cupboards were missing. The rear door of the house was damaged to gain access to the house. Based on the alert, the Jolarpet police inspected the spot. Police said sniffer dogs and fingerprint experts were roped. Footage from CCTV cameras in the house and on the route were taken to identify suspects. A case was registered and special teams were formed to nab the suspects. Further probe is under way.

headline: Over 600 tonnes of waste generated on Maha Deepam day removed in Tiruvannamalai
content: TIRUVANNAMALAI The temple town of Tiruvannamalai has become clean again as More than 2,400 sanitary workers removed over 600 tonnes of garbage that was generated on Maha Deepam day. Officials of Tiruvannamalai Corporation said that apart from the civic body, sanitary workers of District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) were also roped in for the mammoth exercise, which was started on Monday, a day before Maha Deepam as the town witnessed steady flow of pilgrims. “Rain also delayed removal of garbage on streets and the Girivalam Path. Nonetheless, sanitary workers worked round-the-clock, in shifts, to keep the town clean of wastes,” K. Balasubramanian, Corporation Commissioner, told The Hindu. Apart from sanitary staff from Tiruvannamalai Corporation, civic workers from big municipalities such as Ambur, Arcot, Arani, Arakkonam, Polur, Vandavasi, Vaniyambadi, and Gudiyatham were also roped in for the purpose. Along with Corporation Commissioner Mr. Balasubramanian, Collector Vandhana Garg inspected the work and interacted with sanitary workers. Corporation officials said that waste generated on Maha Deepam day this year was the highest (600 metric tonnes) as against that generated in 2025 (450 metric tonnes), 2024 (350 metric tonnes), and 2023 (210 metric tonnes), due to increase in footfall. Around 45 lakh devotees visited the town on Maha Deepam day. Disposable food plates formed the majority of waste, followed by those of sugarcane and sweet corn. District administration has allowed 250 individuals and organisations for annadhanam (free food). that will benefit at least 30 lakh devotees on Maha Deepam day. Many volunteers and groups were also provided free food on the day. Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site of the civic body near the Girivalam path. Food and other organic wastes would be recycled to make manure for farming and terrace gardens in Tiruvannamalai. Every day, on an average, 60-70 metric tonnes of wastes are generated in Tiruvannamalai town, which has over 1,200 streets in its 39 wards. (PHOTOS AVAILABLE)

headline: Supreme Court's Deepam Order Flouted, How TVK Approach Differs From MK Stalin
content: The failure to light the Karthigai Deepam at the hilltop stone pillar near the Thiruparankundram Dargah, as directed by the Supreme Court as a one-time measure, has brought into focus the contrasting approaches of the previous DMK government and the present TVK government. While the DMK government had openly opposed the lighting at the disputed location last year, citing tradition, the nature of the pillar and law-and-order concerns, the TVK government has maintained that it made all arrangements to implement the Supreme Court's order, but the exercise could not be completed because the temple trustees did not authorise a team to light the lamp. The preliminary status report filed by Madurai Collector Nishant Krishna before the Supreme Court offers a detailed account of the TVK government's handling of the issue, placing the responsibility for the non-execution of the order primarily on the temple administration's Board of Trustees. Last year, the DMK government had challenged the order of the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court, permitting the lighting of the lamp at the hilltop pillar. From the outset, the government made its opposition clear, citing several reasons, including the absence of an established tradition of lighting the lamp at that location, the more than century-old practice of lighting the Mahadeepam near the Uchipillaiyar Temple, and questions over the nature of the pillar, which officials argued was a survey pillar. Law-and-order concerns were also repeatedly cited by the Collector and the Police Commissioner as reasons why the order could not be implemented. The lamp was not lit at the disputed location last year either. The TVK government's approach, as reflected in the Collector's latest report, presents a different picture. Rather than making the State's opposition to the proposed lighting the central explanation, the Collector maintains that the district administration was prepared to implement the Supreme Court's order and that the final obstacle was the temple administration's failure to authorise the team.

headline: Farmers stage protests; seek waiver of loans
content: Chennai Farmers across 35 districts under the Tamizhaga Vivasayigal Padhukappu Sangam staged a protest demanding that the State government waive agricultural loans in cooperative banks. Members of the 50 associations led by Easan Murugasamy said that farmers were only reminding the TVK government of its poll promise of complete waiver of farm loans. The government had recently urged farmers to repay their loans availed at cooperative banks by November 30, so that they may avail fresh loans from December 1.

headline: AI’s trillion-dollar infrastructure bet: Why tech companies face mounting pressure to turn data centres into revenue
content: The global artificial intelligence (AI) industry is approaching a critical phase as technology companies face growing pressure to convert massive investments in data centres and computing infrastructure into measurable business returns. While spending on AI infrastructure is expected to remain a major driver of corporate investment, the focus is gradually shifting towards deploying the technology across businesses and generating revenue from it, according to a JPMorgan report on the global economic outlook for 2027. The bank maintained a positive outlook on AI, identifying it as an important driver of corporate earnings growth in the coming year. However, it has cautioned that the transition from building AI infrastructure to rolling out the technology commercially would make the winners and losers in the industry increasingly apparent. "We remain constructive on AI as a key driver of 2027 earnings growth. But as attention shifts from the build-out of the technology to the rollout, the relative winners and losers will become more apparent," the report said. The shift comes as technology companies continue to commit substantial capital towards data centres, computing capacity and other infrastructure needed to support the expansion of AI. Why AI infrastructure spending is becoming a concern for bond markets The scale of borrowing required to finance AI infrastructure is emerging as an important consideration for global financial markets. According to JPMorgan, competition for capital is intensifying as governments increase borrowing while major technology companies, often referred to as hyperscalers, raise debt to finance their AI investments. This combination of government borrowing and AI-related corporate debt issuance has become a defining theme in fixed-income markets, shifting bargaining power towards bond investors. The bank expects elevated debt issuance to continue in 2027, even as inflation moderates and bond yields remain relatively stable at attractive levels. It noted that financial markets were becoming better prepared to absorb fresh debt supply, although competition for capital would remain an important risk.Global growth could support corporate earnings in 2027 JPMorgan expects global economic growth to remain robust in 2027, with expansion broadening across sectors and regions. Government and corporate spending are expected to support economic activity, while easing inflation could help revive consumer spending. "We expect government and corporate spending to keep global growth robust in 2027. With inflation set to soften we also see consumer spending recovering, broadening the expansion," the report said. However, inflationary pressures are expected to persist in early 2027, particularly in Europe, where disruptions to refined petroleum supplies, especially diesel, could push prices higher. The report said disruptions to shipments from the Middle East, alongside falling Russian exports following Ukrainian attacks on refineries, had removed around 30% of seaborne diesel exports that influence global prices. Higher US production has helped offset some of the supply constraints, but refinery utilisation above 90% leaves limited additional capacity. JPMorgan's outlook suggests that while AI will remain an important source of corporate growth, the next phase will reveal which companies can successfully turn infrastructure spending into commercial returns.As borrowing requirements rise and investors compete for capital, the ability to demonstrate tangible returns could become increasingly important for the technology industry's biggest AI investors.With inputs from ANI.

headline: Large-sized pancreatic stones removed via keyhole surgery
content: CHENNAI A 41-year-old male patient got relief from debilitating pain after large-sized pancreatic stones measuring up to 3 cm were removed through laparoscopic surgery at a city hospital. The patient, who was diagnosed with acute-on-chronic calcific pancreatitis accompanied by pancreatic diabetes, had severely atrophic pancreas. A team of surgeons led by surgical gastroenterologist and director at GEM Hospital P. Senthilnathan extracted the calculi with zero abdominal scars or stitches. The patient was discharged just four days after the surgery. Speaking to presspersons on Wednesday, he said that in chronic calcific pancreatitis, stones accumulate in the central duct and cause severe blockages, excruciating pain, and secondary diabetes. “If left untreated, chronic inflammation can even increase the risk of pancreatic cancer. While smaller stones can be managed medically or endoscopically, large stones require surgery.“ The pancreas was choked with dozens of stones, including giant calculi measuring 3 cm x 1 cm lodged across the head, neck, and tail of the main pancreatic duct, and stones up to 2 cm x 2 cm trapped inside the minor duct, he added. As these stones sit dangerously close to major blood vessels, they must be extracted intact without fracturing or damaging the surrounding tissue, which is why such cases are almost universally managed through traditional open surgery, Dr. Senthilnathan added.

headline: Women’s Commission urges Telangana Governor to recommend special investigation into illegal oocyte racket
content: HYDERABAD Telangana State Women’s Commission urged Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla to recommend a special investigation to uncover the network behind the illegal oocyte (egg) collection racket — that was busted in Hyderabad a few weeks ago. A high-level committee to ensure a comprehensive and impartial investigation too was sought. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/43-women-rescued-in-illegal-human-egg-harvesting-racket-in-hyderabad/article71650084.ece The Commission’s Chairperson Nerella Sharada, along with its Member Uzma Shakeer, met the Governor at Lok Bhavan in the city on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) and apprised him of the racket involving alleged exploitation of poor and middle-class women. Malkajgiri Commissionerate Police in October last week said that they have busted an illegal human egg harvesting racket. The police arrested eight people, and 43 women from Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Maharashtra and other States were rescued from four premises in Hyderabad. Why are fertility centres in Hyderabad in crosshairs over human egg harvesting? | Explained Why are fertility centres in Hyderabad in crosshairs over human egg harvesting? | Explained The police have arrested a number of people including the persons who had rented the premises and were liaisoning with the fertility centres. The Health and Medical Department has issued notices to 13 ART centres out of the 44 identified facilities Why are fertility centres in Hyderabad in crosshairs over human egg harvesting? | Explained storyline 1 The Chairperson apprised the Governor on the findings of the inquiry conducted by the Women’s Commission, information gathered from officials concerned, police investigation and legal developments. Ms. Sharada explained that women from different States were allegedly brought to Hyderabad on the pretext of employment and subsequently lured them into illegal retrieval of oocytes, exploiting their financial vulnerabilities. Considering the inter-State connection and wider ramifications of the racket, the Commission urged for the special investigation. Highlighting “loopholes and shortcomings” in the implementation of the Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) Act, it has urged the Governor to recommend necessary amendments to strengthen the legislation and ensure better protection of women’s rights, health and safety. The Governor responded positively to the representations made by the Commission and sought detailed information about the matter, as per a press note. The Commission has earlier issued notices to eight ART centres and egg banks over suspected irregularities. Around 10 days ago, the Police sought documents from 14 fertility centres, including consent forms, and electronic records pertaining to egg donation procedures to find the number of women who were approached, how frequently they underwent the procedure and whether required consent was obtained. https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Hyderabad/telangana-womens-commission-issues-notices-to-eight-art-centres-in-illegal-oocyte-racket-case/article71698872.ece https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/oocyte-racket-police-seek-records-from-14-fertility-centres-probe-financial-trail/article71708947.ece

headline: ‘Ensure fair inquiry into complaint by IAS officer’
content: CHENNAI The Tamil Nadu IAS officers’ Association has presented a representation to Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar, seeking a fair inquiry into a case of sexual harassment involving a lady woman IAS officer. Multiple sources confirmed that the representation from the TNIASOA was presented to the Chief Secretary on November 24. The representation referred to a complaint made by the IAS officer and demanded a fair inquiry. When asked whether action was being taken, a senior official said an FIR had been registered based on a request made by the IAS officer on November 23. An Internal Complaints Committee was formed by the State government on November 24, he said. The Tamil Nadu police on November 24 informed the Madras High Court that they had registered a FIR against Kallakurichi Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA C. Arul Vignesh on Monday for allegedly misbehaving with a woman IAS officer.

headline: PM Modi wants ITI courses aligned with industry needs, jobs closer to home
content: NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi on Wednesday called for public sector undertakings (PSUs) to strengthen their links with Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) for training and recruitment of youth, pitching a ‘Classroom–Company–Career’ approach to bridge the gap between skilling and employment and create job opportunities closer to home, which will help address migration to some extent as well.Chairing the monthly PRAGATI meeting, PM suggested that PSUs should assess their future manpower requirements and partner with ITIs to train and recruit candidates in relevant trades. He also encouraged them to support practical training and apprenticeships and give greater priority to hiring trained ITI graduates.While reviewing the ITI ecosystem and the implementation of PM-SETU, PM Modi called upon chief ministers and chief secretaries to provide leadership in strengthening ITIs and deepening industry participation under PM-SETU. Officials said the PM threw a challenge to chief secretaries to set up five clusters across big states, three in small states and one in UTs in the next three months.Under PM-SETU (Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs), a “cluster” refers to a group of govt ITIs linked through a hub-and-spoke model, with one major ITI serving as the hub and several smaller ITIs functioning as spokes.Reviewing a power project, PM Modi suggested exploring innovative models for decentralised solar and wind power projects. He said that such projects should be developed closer to centres of consumption wherever feasible, taking into account local resource availability and demand. These efforts should aim to improve the availability of reliable and affordable power and ease pressure on transmission infrastructure.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: T.N. opposes ad hoc release of only 2,000 cusecs at Biligundlu
content: CHENNAI The Tamil Nadu government recorded its dissent at the 62nd meeting of the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) in New Delhi on Wednesday, against the “ad hoc decision” of the 147th meeting of the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) that directed Karnataka to ensure a flow of only 2,000 cusecs at Biligundlu for 16 days, without considering the plea of Tamil Nadu. The dissent note pointed out that the decision of the CWRC and the CMWA did not co-relate with the final award, the judgment, or with the data collected by them, Secretary of the Water Resources Department said. In years of deficit, the percentage of deficit must be calculated on the basis of the yield assessment, as specified in the Gazette notification of the Government of India dated June 1, 2018. “Since it was not done, the upper riparian State, Karnataka, is allowed to enjoy more flows than its due share this distress year, pushing Tamil Nadu’s Cauvery delta farmers into misery.” As per the judgment, in distress years, the allocated shares to party States must be reduced on a pro-rata basis. Though the deficit percentage was assessed and the pro-rata share of Tamil Nadu at Biligundlu was estimated, Karnataka was not directed to ensure that quantity, the note further said. This contention is without prejudice to the contention that the method of assessment distress percentage is not acceptable, it noted.

headline: SpaceX Receives Government Approval to Launch Space Data Centers
content: (Bloomberg) -- The US Federal Communications Commission approved SpaceX’s request to launch as many as 1 million satellites for Elon Musk’s vision to build a network of data centers in orbit for complex artificial intelligence computing. In a statement, FCC Chairman Brendan Carr wrote that the commission was supercharging the US’s ambitions in AI by granting authorization for orbital data centers for the first time.“By moving compute capacity beyond Earth, SpaceX and the many competitors working on their own orbital data centers are meeting the moment,” Carr added. The approval clears a regulatory hurdle and brings SpaceX one step closer to its ambitious yet unproven plan for orbital data centers, which the company says can serve as lower-cost and more environmentally friendly alternatives to land-based data centers. Orbital data centers are also key to SpaceX’s future ambitions in AI, which the company pinned its future growth upon during a blockbuster IPO in June.SpaceX’s request to launch its orbital data centers, filed in January, included details about the company’s plans for the new network. Instead of requiring cooling systems that use large volumes of water, the network would rely on radiative cooling that occurs in space, allowing for the dissipation of heat. It would also reduce the need to rely on batteries, since it would acquire energy from the sun, according to the filing.The satellites, which will use laser links to communicate with each other, will be launched between an altitude of 500 kilometers (311 miles) and 2,000 km in an orbit that would provide them near constant access to the sun, according to the filing. SpaceX’s plans to launch so many satellites, however, have raised concerns from scientists and others in the space industry who worry that the tremendous size of the proposed network will overcrowd Earth’s orbit, increase satellite collisions and decrease the visibility of stars for astronomers. The proposal received over 1,500 public comments, with stakeholders including the American Astronomical Society urging the FCC to deny the application.Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin has also requested permission with the FCC to launch its own orbital data centers, although that it still awaiting regulatory approval. --With assistance from Kelcee Griffis.More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

headline: Now, Noel wants revision of Tata Sons board agenda, pushes restructuring
content: After seeking a change in the date of the Tata Sons board meeting, Noel Tata, chairman of Tata Trusts and nominee director, is learnt to have objected to the order of the meeting agenda. He has asked for a revision of the agenda. Earlier this week, Tata Sons shifted the board meeting date from November 26 to November 30 as Noel pressed for a mandatory seven-day notice period. The board agenda was circulated to the directors on November 22 for a meeting four days later. In his latest communication to Tata Sons, Noel has reportedly said that the issues listed by him should be discussed first at the board meeting. While the Tata Sons board is expected to focus on taking forward the listing of the holding company, Noel has stressed the need to deliberate on the alternative plan to restructure Tata Sons as a priority so that it remains privately held. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on November 16 reiterated that Tata Sons must comply with the regulations applicable to upper-layer non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), pointing out that listing the company was the way forward. Noel, who became chairman of Tata Trusts after Ratan Tata (his half-brother) died in October 2024, is believed to have given notice to the board to discuss the proposal to restructure Tata Sons as well as disclosures related to business ties between nominee director Venu Srinivasan’s company TVS Motor and Hanno One Warehousing. According to media reports, Hanno One is owned by the family of Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran. He is also keen to discuss a funding request by the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, the second-largest shareholder of Tata Sons with an 18 per cent stake. Tata Trusts is the largest shareholder with a 66 per cent stake in Tata Sons, the holding company of the conglomerate. The items mentioned by him have not been given due importance, Noel seemed to have suggested in his communication to Tata Sons. He has asked for a revision of the agenda, citing the requirement under Article 121B of the Articles of Association of Tata Sons. In the latest communication, Noel again demanded recordings and documents related to the September 17 board meeting, which had turned into a corporate battleground over two issues — granting a third term to Chandrasekaran as chairman and the listing of Tata Sons. He reiterated that Chandrasekaran should not sign the record of the meeting as it concerns his own reappointment. At the September 17 board meeting, the discussion on Chandrasekaran’s third term was conducted by Harish Manwani, independent director, as Chandrasekaran had recused himself from that part of the meeting. The Tata Sons board, barring Noel, backed a third term for Chandrasekaran. As the two nominee directors (Venu Srinivasan and Noel Tata) voted for and against Chandrasekaran’s third term, the casting vote came from Manwani to settle the matter.

headline: Electronics exports from India to cross $60 bn in FY27: Meity official
content: India's electronics exports are expected to reach USD 60 billion (about Rs 5.5 lakh crore) by the end of this fiscal year, a senior government official said on Wednesday.Electronics exports have crossed USD 38.4 billion (about Rs 3.54 lakh crore) in the first seven months of the current fiscal year, with record performance in October, Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Electronics and IT, Sushil Pal, said at the CII Electronics Summit. "Electronics exports have reached USD 38.4 billion. November figures have not been updated yet. The good thing is that, out of the USD 38.4 billion, USD 20 (billion) is mobile and about USD 18 (billion) is non-smartphone," Pal said. In FY26, electronics production in the country had crossed USD 116 billion (about Rs 13.11 Lakh crore) and exports touched USD 48 billion (around Rs 4.24 lakh crore). Pal said the electronics exports from the country in the non-smartphone category have already achieved the numbers of the past financial year in the first seven months of the current fiscal. "We are confident that this year we are expecting to cross USD 60 billion for sure," he said. He said that electronic manufacturing in the country is on the rise and achieving more depth day by day. Pal said that electronics manufacturers in the country have not only seen a shortage of chips but also non-semiconductor components. "It is indicative of the fact that this boom in electronic manufacturing is also travelling to the constraints in the supply chain, not only in silicon or in memory, but also in a lot of other non-silicon components like substrate or a PCB(printed circuit board). The government is actually following a very targeted policy on the silicon side," he said. PTI PRS MR

headline: Akbaruddin Owaisi questions low spending, high dropouts in minority schools
content: HYDERABAD All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) legislator Akbaruddin Owaisi on Wednesday flagged low utilisation of funds by the Minorities Welfare Department, shortfall in minority student enrolment in welfare schools and delays in processing overseas scholarship applications, even as he called for corrective measures to address the gaps. Raising these concerns at a meeting of the Joint Committee for Welfare of Minorities in the Legislative Assembly, Mr. Owaisi questioned why admissions of students from minority communities in schools run by the Telangana Minorities Residential Educational Institutions Society (TGMREIS) were falling short of the prescribed quota. The Society has reserved 75% of seats for students from minority communities and 25% for others. However, of the approximately 85,000 students enrolled, around 56,000 belonged to minority communities and 29,000 to non-minority communities, accounting for about 66% and 34%, respectively. He expressed concern over the shortfall in minority enrolment and the high dropout rate, and called for systematic measures to address the issue. To check dropouts, Mr. Owaisi suggested that the State government introduce its own pre-matric scholarship scheme, irrespective of the Centre’s decision to discontinue its scheme. He also proposed using data from the Unified District Information System for Education (UDISE) to analyse dropout rates and identify the reasons behind them. While welcoming the proposed constitution of a Sikh Minority Finance Corporation, a promise in the Congress’s Minority Declaration ahead of the Assembly elections, he pointed out that a Christian Minorities Finance Corporation was already in existence. He suggested renaming the State Minorities Finance Corporation as the Muslim Finance Corporation. On the Chief Minister’s Overseas Scholarship Scheme, Mr. Owaisi questioned the delay in verifying applications and sought clarity on the pending reimbursement of tuition fees and maintenance of tuition fees. The outstanding dues for the period from 2019-20 to 2025-26 stood at ₹1,273 crore. Asking who would bear the financial burden, he cautioned that students would ultimately suffer. He also expressed concern over the department’s low fund utilisation. Against a budgetary allocation of ₹3,768 crore, the Minorities Welfare Department had spent only around ₹1,013 crore, he said. The department and its allied agencies and institutions have a sanctioned strength of 6,986 employees, but only 4,028 posts were filled. Mr. Owaisi said the large number of vacancies could affect the department’s efficiency and delivery of services. He said the department and its allied agencies and institutions are functioning with a large number of vacancies, raising concerns about the department’s efficiency and service delivery.

headline: Free train travel facility extended to all trains for Chakra awardees
content: New Delhi The Ministry of Railways, in consultation with the Ministry of Defence, has extended the complimentary train travel facility for Chakra-series gallantry awardees to all trains, including the Vande Bharat Express. The government provides complimentary rail travel in First Class and AC 2-Tier to recipients of the Param Vir Chakra, Ashoka Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra, Kirti Chakra, Vir Chakra, and Shaurya Chakra. The facility is also available to widows of posthumous award recipients, along with a companion. The initiative is aimed at recognising the courage, sacrifice, and service of gallantry awardees and honouring their contribution to the nation. The first three gallantry awards — the Param Vir Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra, and Vir Chakra — were instituted on January 26, 1950, with retrospective effect from August 15, 1947. Subsequently, the Ashoka Chakra, Kirti Chakra, and Shaurya Chakra were instituted. The order of precedence for the six awards is Param Vir Chakra, Ashoka Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra, Kirti Chakra, Vir Chakra, and Shaurya Chakra.

headline: IIMBAA to bring 500 alumni, 115 CXOs and 21 management institutions together for sports fest in Bengaluru
content: Bengaluru The IIM Bangalore Alumni Association (IIMBAA), to bring together some of India’s management institutions on a common sporting platform, is hosting a two-day inter-institutional alumni sports festival in Bengaluru, with participation from 21 premier institutions, including alumni communities from IIM, ISB and XLRI. The event, scheduled to be held between November 28 (Saturday) and November 29 (Sunday), is expected to bring together approximately 500 alumni participants and 300 visitors, making it a significant gathering of India’s management alumni community, as per a statement. "The event is distinctive for the participation of more than 115 senior corporate leaders, founders, CXOs, partners and Vice Presidents from leading organisations, who will step away from their boardrooms and business responsibilities to compete alongside fellow alumni on the sports field,’’ IIMBAA said. The participating institutions include IIM Ahmedabad, IIM Amritsar, IIM Bangalore, IIM Bodh Gaya, IIM Calcutta, IIM Indore, IIM Jammu, IIM Kozhikode, IIM Lucknow, IIM Mumbai, IIM Raipur, IIM Ranchi, IIM Rohtak, IIM Sambalpur, IIM Shillong, IIM Sirmaur, IIM Tiruchirappalli, IIM Udaipur, IIM Visakhapatnam, the Indian School of Business (ISB) and XLRI Jamshedpur. According to the statement, the event would be part of IIMBAA’s initiatives towards building bridges across various management institutions in the country. "By leading the conceptualisation, organisation, and convening of alumni communities from 21 premier management institutions, IIMBAA is creating a distinctive platform for inter-institutional engagement through sport,’’ it said.

headline: 'Katha Won't Help You Win': Sachin Pilot Slams AAP After Hindu Preacher Dhirendra Shastri's Punjab Event
content: Congress general secretary Sachin Pilot, in charge of the state unit in poll-bound Punjab, on Wednesday attacked the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), taking a dig at its alleged political misuse of religion by organising a 'katha' by popular Hindu preacher Dhirendra Krishna Shastri in Pathankot earlier this week. "Elections are no longer won by organising such a 'katha' (religious storytelling)," Pilot said in a media interaction, referring to the presence of AAP leadership at the event headlined by Shastri, who heads Bageshwar Dham, a temple dedicated to Lord Hanuman in Chhatarpur district of Madhya Pradesh. The event, held by a local organisation, was overseen by AAP's candidate from Sujanpur Assembly segment, prominent businessman Swaran Singh Salaria. Pilot further said Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, a former comic artiste, was "still busy with comedy" while the state's law-and-order situation "keeps worsening". Pathankot, Punjab: At Bageshwar Dham Peethadhishwar Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri's programme, AAP Punjab in-charge Manish Sisodia says, "Today, I had come to meet Shastri ji. Regarding the country, the country's education- so that every child can get a good education- and so that politics moves in the right direction, uniting the country to build a Viksit Bharat, we need everyone's blessings for this. We need the blessings of all saints and the support of all people in this. On behalf of the Aam Aadmi Party, we are doing whatever we can. And in the coming times, if everyone's blessings remain with us, Punjab will prosper further. Just as the Bhagwant Mann government has worked for every household in Punjab- worked on schools, worked for hospitals, worked on jobs, worked for farmers, worked for traders, and provided an honest government with a farsighted vision- may Bhagwant Mann Sahab and the Aam Aadmi Party receive the blessings of all saints, and may we take Punjab and the country forward; that is my prayer." The three-day 'Shri Hanumant Katha' and 'Divya Darbar' were held at Lamini Stadium in Pathankot from November 22 to 24. AAP's Punjab in-charge Manish Sisodia attended on the final day and welcomed Shastri on stage, sought his blessings for the Bhagwant Mann government, and passed on greetings from party boss Arvind Kejriwal and Mann. Leaders from the BJP and the Congress also attended, including Punjab BJP working president and Pathankot MLA Ashwani Sharma and former Pathankot MLA Amit Vij of the Congress.

headline: At least 30 killed in blaze after vehicle overturns in Egypt, health ministry says
content: Nov 25 (Reuters) – At least 30 people were killed and 15 injured when a vehicle carrying petroleum products overturned and caught fire on a major ring road in Egypt, the health ministry said on Wednesday. The ring road connects key highways across Greater Cairo, linking the governorates of Cairo, Giza and Qalyubia. The fire broke out above a tunnel in Giza’s Al-Warraq district, the ministry said. Local media reported that firefighters had brought the blaze under control. Road accidents are common in Egypt due to factors including speeding, weak enforcement of traffic regulations and poor road conditions. In recent years, Egypt has expanded its road network with new highways and bridges under a broader infrastructure programme aimed at easing congestion and accommodating rapid population growth and urban expansion. While the projects have improved traffic flow in some areas, concerns over road safety persist. (Reporting by Yomna Ehab and Enas Alashray. Editing by Timothy Heritage and Mark Potter)

headline: Akal Takht panel accuses Punjab govt committee of misleading people, invites it for talks
content: Amritsar: An expert committee constituted by Akal Takht to examine the Punjab govt’s ‘Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026’ has accused the govt’s coordination committee of misleading the Sikh sangat over Akal Takht’s directives and invited it for discussions at Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib in Anandpur Sahib on Nov 30.The meeting has been scheduled for 11am, according to a release issued by the Akal Takht secretariat on Wednesday. Expert committee coordinator Lakhvir Singh said he had written to the nodal officer of the govt’s coordination committee.The expert committee said it had discussed the news conference held after the govt coordination committee’s Nov 23 meeting in Amritsar and subsequent statements. In its letter, it expressed concern over what it described as misleading remarks made at the news conference by two people who were not members of the govt committee, and the disregard shown towards objections raised in letters sent by the expert panel.“The expert committee has asked the Punjab government’s coordination committee not to mislead the Sikh Sangat regarding the directives of Akal Takht Sahib,” Lakhvir Singh alleged.The expert committee said the proposed meeting was in the interest of Panthic unity and to prevent the public from being misled on the issue. It said discussions would be held in the light of Akal Takht’s directives.The letter stated that only nominated members of the two committees would be allowed to attend the joint meeting. The expert committee meeting was attended by Justice (retd) Rupinder Singh Sodhi, Justice (retd) Mohinder Mohan Singh Bedi, senior advocate Puran Singh Hundal, Dr Kehar Singh, Prof Jagmohan Singh and coordinator Lakhvir Singh.

headline: Transfer assumption: On the SAD(B)-BJP alliance in Punjab
content: Few parties understand the arithmetic of the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system, and the necessity for alliances in States where they are minor players, better than the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The BJP has never shied away from partnerships with little ideological cohesion if they keep it electorally relevant. India’s FPTP system is unforgiving to smaller parties in a crowded polity if their support base is limited and dispersed. Votes translate into seats only if the support crosses a certain threshold. In Punjab, the BJP, despite its best efforts, has remained confined to sections of urban Hindu voters. Even after years of poaching leaders from the perennially fractious Congress, and after polling nearly a fifth of the vote in the 2024 general election without winning a seat, it realises that it cannot be relevant without a partner with a wider rural base. The Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) walked out of the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance in 2020 over the Centre’s farm laws, which were later repealed, as the farmers’ agitation threatened its base in rural Punjab. But much water has flowed down the many rivers of the northern State since then. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has consolidated its hold in a crowded political space and is set to complete a full term. The Panthic vote, which used to be the SAD(B)’s core support base, has now fragmented. The SAD(B) appears to believe that it can regain ground only by expanding beyond its Panthic and rural constituencies, and that the farmers’ anger against the BJP is baggage from the past. It is this expedient calculation that now binds the two parties, despite six years of bitter attacks against each other. And it is also why the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has pointedly called the SAD(B) the “big brother” in Punjab after sealing the alliance. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/bharatiya-janata-party/ https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/punjab/ https://www.thehindu.com/topic/indian-national-congress/ NDA-SAD reunion: Why the Akali Dal severed ties with BJP 6 years ago storyline 1 https://www.thehindu.com/topic/aam-aadmi-party/ After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance for Punjab Assembly election storyline 1 The SAD(B)’s calculation may not work out as well as it hopes it would. Farmers’ anger against the BJP-led Centre has not entirely dissipated in rural Punjab. In earlier alliances, the two parties transferred votes to each other effectively, partly because their voters had fewer alternatives. But a revived Congress and an entrenched AAP have shown that they can win over urban Hindu voters wary of the Akalis and rural voters who are not inclined to back parties allied with the BJP. That these two sections will simply add up for the alliance is not certain. At best, the alliance consolidates enough of the anti-AAP vote to make this a clear three-cornered contest. Punjab is a sensitive border State and one of India’s granaries. It is also among India’s most indebted States, with a stagnating agrarian economy and a government that has expanded welfare expenditure despite strained finances. It needs a serious competition of ideas on what welfare it can afford and how to revive growth. The SAD(B)-BJP alliance, with its Panthic appeal on one side and Hindu consolidation on the other, instead offers a rehash of familiar identity politics. With AAP failing to deliver on governance, and the Congress stuck in its old ways, Punjab’s voters will have to decide who they dislike the least. headline: GAIL’s Faridabad Data Centre Plan Explained
content: GAIL is proposing to enter India’s data-centre market through an equal joint venture with an established operator, beginning with a facility of at least 5 MW in Faridabad, Haryana. The plan would use a GAIL-owned land parcel and its optical-fibre network, while the proposed joint venture would arrange power and water and develop, operate and commercialise the facility, according to an expression of interest reported by Economic Times. The state-run gas transporter is also evaluating the possibility of developing additional data centres in Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Maharashtra. Any expansion would depend on the performance of the Faridabad facility and techno-economic assessments of other sites, the report said. GAIL’s proposal reflects the growing importance of land, connectivity and energy in data-centre development. The company operates around 15,800 km of optical-fibre cable along its cross-country natural-gas and LPG pipelines, connecting more than 100 towns and cities. It also has land parcels at pipeline terminals and compressor stations across several states, which could be considered for future facilities. For the first project, GAIL would contribute the land and access to its fibre network. The selected partner would be responsible for arranging the remaining infrastructure and for establishing and running the centre. The prospective partner must have at least one operational data centre with a capacity of 1 MW to qualify for the bid. The selection process will assign weight to an applicant’s data-centre portfolio, the capacity of its largest facility, its commitment to book capacity in the proposed Faridabad centre and its revenue over the previous three financial years, according to the report. Data centres are power-intensive facilities, making electricity supply a central consideration in their planning and operation. GAIL’s access to natural gas is identified in the proposal as another potential asset because gas could fuel generators supplying electricity to the facilities. However, the proposed joint venture, rather than GAIL alone, would be responsible for arranging the power and water needed for the Faridabad unit.

headline: HP to get 50% free power royalty from central PSUs after 40 years
content: Shimla: To augment the state’s revenue, the Himachal Pradesh govt has amended the Swaran Jayanti Energy Policy-2021 to increase free power royalty from hydroelectric projects operated by central public sector undertakings (CPSUs) to 50% after completion of 40 years of commissioning.Chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said hydropower was a major source of revenue for Himachal Pradesh and the state must receive its rightful share from projects utilising its water resources.He said the enhanced royalty would strengthen the state’s financial position and generate additional resources for development and welfare activities.Govt is committed to protecting the state’s interests and ensuring that its natural resources generate equitable returns for its people, Sukhu added.Under the amended provisions, projects operated by the NHPC, SJVN and the NTPC will have to provide 50% of their power generation to the state as free power royalty for the first 10 years after completing 40 years of commissioning.After 50 years, these projects will revert to the state govt. Separate agreements will be signed with the concerned CPSUs to implement the provisions. Currently, Himachal receives free power royalty at 12% for the first 12 years, 18% for the next 18 years and 30% for the remaining 10 years of the agreement period.The amendment will cover major hydropower projects, including Baira Siul, Chamera-I, II and III, Parbati Stage-II and III of NHPC; Nathpa Jhakri and Rampur projects of SJVN; and Kol Dam of NTPC.Baira Siul, commissioned in 1982, has already operated for more than four decades. The state govt recognises water as one of Himachal’s most valuable natural resources and seeks to secure greater economic benefits from long-operational hydropower projects.

headline: Justice Vivek Singh Thakur of Himachal Pradesh recommended as Tripura chief justice
content: Shimla: The Supreme Court collegium has recommended the appointment of Justice Vivek Singh Thakur of Himachal Pradesh high court as the chief justice of Tripura high court.The elevation, recommended on Tuesday, will be consequent upon the transfer of the incumbent chief justice of Tripura , Justice MS Ramachandra Rao, as chief justice of Karnataka.Justice Rao had also earlier served as the chief justice of Himachal Pradesh from May 30, 2023 to Sept 25, 2024. Justice Thakur took oath as a judge of Himachal Pradesh high court on April 12, 2016.A native of Lanjata village in Ghumarwin tehsil of Bilaspur district, Justice Thakur completed his schooling and BSc from Bilaspur before pursuing LLB and BJMC from Himachal Pradesh University, Shimla. He enrolled as an advocate with Himachal Pradesh Bar Council in 1990 and practised before various legal forums, including Himachal Pradesh high court.His areas of practice included revenue, civil, criminal, constitutional, service, arbitration and taxation matters. He also served as legal adviser to several organisations.Before his elevation to the high court, he served as assistant advocate general of Himachal Pradesh from 1998 to 2003 and additional advocate general from 2008 to 2013. He also served as senior panel counsel for central govt. During his tenure as a high court judge, Justice Thakur was entrusted with administrative and guardian judge responsibilities for several sessions divisions, including Sirmaur, Una, Chamba, Kullu, Solan, Mandi, Kangra and Shimla.

headline: Chandigarh: Admission schedule for entry-level classes out
content: The UT Education Department has announced the admission schedule for entry-level classes in private unaided recognised schools for the 2027-28 academic session, with the application process set to begin on December 9.As per the public notice issued by the District Education Officer, schools have been directed to display admission-related information, including the total number of seats, age criteria, fee structure, admission criteria and documents required, on their notice boards and websites by December 7.Admission forms will be available free of cost from December 9 to December 22. Schools will display the list of eligible candidates on January 18, 2027, while the final list of selected candidates and the waiting list must be published by February 2. The last date for depositing admission fees is February 12.In a separate notice, the department clarified that parents applying under the Economically Weaker Section (EWS) and Disadvantaged Group (DG) categories must submit valid certificates. Acknowledgement receipts for applications seeking income or DG certificates will not be accepted as substitutes.The centralised online admission process for EWS/DG candidates will be conducted under Section 12(1) of the Right to Education Act. Detailed guidelines will be notified separately.

headline: Delhi to get 2 new hospitals, 40 Arogya clinics as CM pushes health infra expansion
content: New Delhi: Delhi will get two hospitals, one in Siraspur (north) and the other in Hastal (west), next year, which will add 1,815 beds to the capital’s total bed capacity.Several existing hospitals will also get specialised treatment blocks.Next month, 40 more Ayushman Arogya Mandirs will become operational, chief minister Rekha Gupta said after reviewing health department projects at the Delhi secretariat Wednesday. The expansion is aimed at easing the growing patient load on existing hospitals, reducing the distance people have to travel for routine treatment and strengthening specialised medical care.Delhi govt is also planning two medical colleges, an increase in MBBS and dental seats, and the integrated redevelopment of major hospital campuses under its plans to expand healthcare capacity and the availability of trained medical professionals in the capital.The two hospitals in Siraspur and Hastal will “significantly strengthen healthcare facilities in the capital. Govt is also targeting the opening of 40 new Ayushman Arogya Mandirs next month, on the 102nd birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee,” Gupta said.The Siraspur hospital with 1,164 beds is ready. The procurement of medical equipment is under way. The completion deadline is the end of Jan. Construction of the 651-bed hospital in Hastal is also nearing completion.CM Gupta said that govt is also developing hospitals with 691 beds each in Madipur and Jwalapuri. Both projects are scheduled for completion by 2028. The Madipur hospital is being built at a cost of Rs 466.5 crore, while the Jwalapuri hospital has an estimated cost about Rs 484 crore.Govt is also expanding maternal and child healthcare facilities in the existing hospitals. A 463-bed maternal and child healthcare block is being developed at Baba Saheb Ambedkar Hospital in Rohini. Its OPD block is ready for inauguration. A 270-bed maternal and child healthcare block at Rao Tula Ram Memorial Hospital and a 460-bed block at Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital in Khichripur are also nearing completion. These facilities will be operational shortly.Work is also under way on a plan for the integrated redevelopment of Lok Nayak Hospital and the Maulana Azad Medical College campus. The project has a stipulated timeline of approximately 30 months, including planning and construction. Efforts are also under way to bring Guru Teg Bahadur (GTB) Hospital, Rajiv Gandhi Super Speciality Hospital, Delhi State Cancer Institute and the Institute of Human Behaviour and Allied Sciences (IHBAS) in the Trans-Yamuna region under a common institutional framework.The objective is to strengthen specialised medical services and the functioning of these institutions.The CM said govt has plans to establish medical colleges at Indira Gandhi Hospital in Dwarka and Guru Gobind Singh Govt Hospital. Each of the two proposed colleges will have 150 MBBS seats. The process is also under way to increase the number of seats at Baba Saheb Ambedkar Medical College from 125 to 200 and at the Maulana Azad Institute of Dental Sciences from 50 to 70.“A total of 1,139 Ayushman Arogya Mandirs are being developed across Delhi, of which 415 are operational. Plans are also under way to introduce services in two shifts at Arogya Mandirs receiving a higher number of patients, ensuring timely treatment at the local level,” Gupta said.At the meeting, the CM directed officials to ensure that all projects related to hospitals and healthcare facilities are completed within the stipulated timelines and that there are no unnecessary delays.Health minister Pankaj Singh said all the projects are being monitored regularly.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news.
